critique: Only one invariant pair and one failure mode — thin for a foundational primitive. Missing invariants: Verdict Observability (Decision must be emitted, not discarded); Separation (Gate must not mutate the condition's subject). Missing failure modes: Stale Decision (artifact outlives its validity window but still routes traffic).

'Debt' is mentioned in the mechanism but never defined: what are the obligations, who discharges them, how is debt tracked? Descendants invent this per-deployment, losing the shared semantics the parent should have provided.
The condition is a single slot (`{{condition}}`). Real gates often compose multiple conditions (all-of, any-of, weighted). No compositional story in the parent.

Gate.family_discussion: Sibling to `Check` (observational, no control flow) and `Branch` (structural dispatch). Feeds `Decision` downstream; reads `Condition` upstream. Ancestor of domain-specialized gates across the verification stack. `ReceptivityGate` is the Society-layer specialization that guards a Solver's Feedback surface against poisoned rejection signals.

motivation.why_it_exists: Concepts, framings, heuristics come from somewhere — pedigree matters. GenealogicalTrace names the origin-tracking audit: find the historical/institutional origin, compare original context to current. Without the pattern, ideas circulate without provenance.
motivation.removability: Removable — most agents don't trace genealogy. The pattern is specifically for high-stakes reasoning where origin matters.

usage.intended: audit the historical lineage and incentives of an idea (Cui Bono).
usage.future: any "follow the idea to its origin and interest" analysis.
usage.broad_contexts: historical criticism, science-studies analysis, policy-origin tracing, argument-by-authority debunking, meme-origin analysis, philosophical genealogy (Nietzsche, Foucault).
usage.every_context_needs: target concept, origin-tracing mechanism, interest identification ("who benefited?"), distinction between universal-truth vs inherited-bias.
usage.varies: depth of trace, source-citation rigor, confidence in origin claim, applicability to the current context.

tensions: Genetic Fallacy (named failure) — dismissing valid ideas by origin.
Contextualization invariant vs pragmatic use — context comparison adds work.
Traceability to specific origin — sometimes origins are distributed.
tradeoffs: Gains: origin-aware evaluation.
Gives up: speed. Every concept traced adds latency.
critique: Genetic Fallacy is the named failure; the pattern balances between 'consider origin' and 'dismiss by origin.'
Traceability to specific origin is often impossible.
Contextualization requires knowing original context.

GenealogicalTrace.family_discussion: Audit primitive paired with Trace (general), SourceEvaluate (credibility), and AuditTrail. Compare with SourceEvaluate — GenealogicalTrace is origin-focused; SourceEvaluate is credibility-focused.

motivation.why_it_exists: Specific examples are useful; shared structure is more useful. Generalize names the inductive extraction move: from multiple instances, identify what's invariant, replace specifics with variables, test the pattern on new instances. Without it, agents can't compress observations into reusable rules.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in any learning system. Generalize is the canonical inductive move — Induce's operational form. Remove it and agents can't produce reusable abstractions; every situation becomes unprecedented.

usage.intended: inductive pattern extraction — multiple instances → shared-structure invariant.
usage.future: any "find the rule that covers these cases" operation.
usage.broad_contexts: inductive reasoning, ML pattern learning, scientific generalization, legal precedent extraction, category formation, hypothesis generation.
usage.every_context_needs: multiple instances, shared-structure identification, invariant statement, predictive test.
usage.varies: instance count required, invariant-validation method, abstraction level.

tensions: Abstraction level — too specific and the rule doesn't transfer; too general and the rule predicts everything (which is predicting nothing).
Overfitting (named failure mode) vs under-generalization — extract too many specifics and you've memorized noise; extract too few and you've lost signal.
Information loss vs predictive power — the invariant demands 'information loss minimized' and 'rule covers all examples,' which are in tension.
tradeoffs: Gains: reusable rules, compression of observation space, predictive generalization.
Gives up: specific details. Generalization is by definition loss-full; the bet is that the lost details were noise.
critique: Overfitting is the dominant failure and the pattern has only 'refine until predictive' as the remedy, which requires a held-out test set the pattern doesn't specify.
'Information loss minimized' is the invariant and it's in tension with 'rule covers all examples' — a rule that covers all examples perfectly is memorization, not generalization.
The 'predict behavior of new instances' test is classical ML validation in prose form; it needs to be operationalized to enforce.

Generalize.family_discussion: Canonical form of Induction. Paired with Abduction and Deduction as the reasoning triad. Compare with Compress — Generalize extracts rule structure; Compress reduces representation size. Both produce smaller artifacts from larger inputs, targeting different forms of reduction.

motivation.why_it_exists: Some information must be delayed — time-locked wills, escrow releases, future reveals. GlacialVault names the cryptographic time-lock: encryption that physically cannot decrypt until a specified delay has passed, using Verifiable Delay Functions. Without the pattern, delay depends on trusted keyholders, which the pattern eliminates.
motivation.removability: Removable in settings where trusted-time release is acceptable. Essential for trustless time-lock (blockchain escrow, time-delayed reveals, commitment schemes with delay). The 'no keyholder can rush' property is unique to VDF-based vaults.

usage.intended: time-locked storage via Verifiable Delay Functions — physically impossible to decrypt before delay.
usage.broad_contexts: time capsule encryption, sealed-bid auction commits, delayed disclosure protocols, legal escrow with auto-reveal, trustless time-locks.
usage.every_context_needs: VDF-based encryption, delay parameter, no-keyholder-can-rush guarantee.
usage.varies: VDF implementation, delay duration (Duration per §3.17), partial-early-reveal options.

tensions: Delay immutability (invariant) vs hardware speedups — the named failure mode: faster hardware reduces VDF time.
Time-lock strength vs cost — VDFs are computationally expensive; strong time-locks cost proportionally.
Delay time vs information freshness — long delays mean encrypted information is stale by the time it's readable.
tradeoffs: Gains: trustless time-locking, explicit delay invariant, VDF-based security guarantee.
Gives up: adjustability. Once locked, the delay is fixed; early release requires key escape hatches that defeat the purpose.
critique: Hardware speedups (the named failure) are real and ongoing — VDF security depends on worst-case compute, and that worst case keeps improving.
The pattern assumes VDF technology is available and correctly implemented; subtle bugs in VDF implementations are known.
Very narrow — the pattern is for a specific use case (trustless delay) and doesn't generalize beyond it.

GlacialVault.family_discussion: Cryptographic-primitive paired with HeldRelease (escrow with condition), ExpiringToken (capability decay), and VerifiableDelayFunction (the substrate). Compare with Defer — GlacialVault is trustless time-lock; Defer is caller-controlled postponement.

motivation.why_this_layer: scope modifier — shared property across system
motivation.why_it_exists: Scope matters — applying an operation system-wide versus locally has very different semantics and blast radius. Global names the system-wide scope modifier. Without it, 'global vs local' becomes implicit in naming conventions, which drift.
motivation.removability: Very thin — a scope-modifier primitive. Could be folded into Scope or Context, but keeping Global separate reserves the slot for 'this applies everywhere.' Removing it makes 'global' an implicit qualifier that requires caller inference.

usage.intended: scope modifier indicating system-wide applicability.
usage.broad_contexts: Global state, Global(Policy), Global(Rule) as modifier on other patterns.
usage.every_context_needs: marker semantic only — descendants carry the Global tag.
notes: §3.18 converts to `is_trait: true`. Broad-use confirms — Global is a modifier, not a standalone pattern.

tensions: Global vs Local — the two are in natural tension; the pattern names one side of the duality.
System-wide application vs context boundaries — what counts as 'the entire system' is itself context-dependent (which system?).
Global as scope vs global as universal — philosophically loaded term; the pattern means the former but inherits the resonance of the latter.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit scope marking, distinction from local operations.
Gives up: almost nothing — the pattern is so thin that argument against it is thin too.
critique: Almost a stub — one sentence, no invariants, no failure modes.
Conflates scope ('applies to all of X') with universality ('applies to everything always') — these have different operational implications.
No mechanism for resolving global-vs-local conflicts when both apply.

Global.family_discussion: Scope-modifier primitive paired with Local (the counterpart), Scope (the containing abstraction), and Context (where scope lives). Semantically paired — one of the most basic distinctions any system has to make.

motivation.why_it_exists: Work without a specified end state is drift. Goal names the testable desired end: given a result, you can decide whether the goal is satisfied. Without the primitive, tasks can't be evaluated (no target), plans can't terminate (no stop condition), and coordination has no alignment axis.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every Task, Plan, AcceptSpec, and Solve consumes Goal or something isomorphic. It's the most basic 'what are we trying to do' primitive; removing it collapses purpose-driven work.

usage.intended: specification of desired end state — testable target work aims at.
usage.future: any "what we're trying to achieve" specification.
usage.broad_contexts: OKRs, project goals, personal goals, scientific research goals, therapeutic goals, legal objectives, algorithmic optimization targets.
usage.every_context_needs: desired end-state description, testability (can evaluate Result against Goal), composability (AND/OR), prioritization.
usage.varies: quantitative vs qualitative, time horizon, stakeholder weighting, sub-goal hierarchy.

tensions: Testability (invariant) vs richness — crisp testable goals are narrower than fuzzy aspirational ones; often the real goal is the fuzzy one.
Stability (invariant: shouldn't change during execution) vs learning — execution often reveals the goal was mis-specified; the invariant forbids updating mid-run.
Composability (AND/OR) vs single-axis clarity — composed goals are powerful and easy to mis-specify (which half of the AND is load-bearing?).
tradeoffs: Gains: testable purpose, explicit target for evaluation, compositional goal structures.
Gives up: fuzzy aspirations that resist testability. 'Build a great product' isn't a Goal by the pattern's invariant; the crispening can lose the motivating richness.
critique: Goal Ambiguity is the named failure — goals that admit multiple incompatible interpretations. The pattern has no mechanism for surfacing ambiguity before execution.
Goal Conflict (multiple goals jointly unsatisfiable) is structurally common in multi-goal systems; the pattern doesn't specify resolution.
Moving Target — the stability invariant is exactly the anti-pattern here, and stability-at-the-cost-of-learning has its own problems.

Goal.family_discussion: Foundational primitive consumed by Task, Plan, Solve, AcceptSpec, Prioritize. Sibling of Criteria (how to measure) and Purpose (why). Compare with Intent — Goal is testable end-state; Intent is the volitional precursor. Both are purpose-specifying, at different operational points.

motivation.why_this_layer: fallback when verification between parties fails
motivation.why_it_exists: When a pattern isn't found locally, halting is brittle. GracefulDegradation names the resolution-fallback discipline: try secondary channels (inline payload, network), cryptographically verify, load only if valid. Without it, missing patterns are hard failures; with it, they're recoverable via defense-in-depth resolution.
motivation.removability: Removable in tightly-controlled deployments where all patterns are known at start. Essential in open or evolving vocabularies where new patterns appear. The Trust-but-Verify invariant is the load-bearing safety property — degradation that skips verification creates spoofing opportunities.

usage.intended: resolution fallback — when Pattern_ID not found locally, try secondary channels then verify.
usage.future: any "don't halt, fall back safely" resolution strategy.
usage.broad_contexts: DNS resolution fallbacks, package-manager dependency resolution, service-discovery fallbacks, offline-mode graceful degradation, document-format fallbacks.
usage.every_context_needs: primary-channel failure, secondary-channel attempt, cryptographic verification, fail-closed default.
usage.varies: fallback channel count (max_def_size per Appendix A — typed PositiveInteger), verification strictness, timeout per channel.

tensions: Fallback reach vs attack surface — more fallback channels increase resolution success and attack surface (spoofing via inline payload).
Atomic Load (invariant: verify before admit) vs speed — every acquired definition pays the verification tax.
Recursive dependency resolution — an inline definition references unknowns, triggering more fallback; the named failure mode is 'Dependency Hell.'
tradeoffs: Gains: robust resolution against missing data, cryptographic verification before admission, avoidance of hard-halt on lookup failure.
Gives up: simplicity and sometimes performance. Every pattern lookup may now trigger multiple channels, each with its own failure modes.
critique: DoS via Definition — the named failure where an attacker includes massive 'definitions' to exhaust memory. The pattern has no size limit specified.
Dependency Hell from inline definitions is endemic; the pattern acknowledges it without bounding recursion depth.
Hash Mismatch is the canonical spoofing attack and the pattern's Trust-but-Verify invariant defeats it — but only if the verification is correct and complete.

GracefulDegradation.family_discussion: Resilience primitive paired with Hash (the verification substrate), ConceptAnchor (what's being resolved), and FailClosed (the fallback default if even graceful degradation fails). Compare with CircuitBreaker — GracefulDegradation adds alternative resolution paths; CircuitBreaker stops trying. Opposite responses to failure.

motivation.why_this_layer: directional rate of change of a scalar field — substrate for flow and climbing
motivation.why_it_exists: Pins a mathematically-grounded definition of 'directional rate of change' so downstream patterns that invoke gradients (hill-climbing, attention flow, credit assignment, surprise-driven learning) compose against the same substrate. Minted under the structured-thinking criterion — using 'gradient' loosely in English is common; requiring metric-grounded invariants forces precision.
motivation.removability: Marginal. The library could omit Gradient and let dependents carry the concept informally. But given the mathematical load-bearing nature (steepest-ascent, credit assignment, SurprisalUpdate), having a pinned reference the library can cite earns its place.

tensions: Mathematical precision vs cross-domain use: the strict formulation requires a differentiable space. Many library use cases ('attention gradient', 'credibility gradient') are not literally over smooth manifolds — the analogy breaks. The pattern hedges by referring to 'sufficiently smooth fields.'

Physics placement vs applied usage: Gradient is Physics because differential calculus on fields is substrate. But most usage in the library is metaphorical (attention flow, not physical flow). The layer reflects the formal grounding, not the typical invocation.

Existence invariant vs discontinuities: the invariant says 'every sufficiently smooth field has a gradient at every interior point' — but real signals often have discontinuities. The qualifier 'sufficiently smooth' is load-bearing but vague.
tradeoffs: Mathematical grounding buys rigor at the cost of narrowing applicability to smooth domains.
Vector-valued output (direction + magnitude) buys expressivity at the cost of requiring vector arithmetic downstream.
Non-opinionated on the field's meaning (entropy gradient, credibility gradient) buys generality at the cost of leaving domain semantics to the caller.
critique: No failure modes. Missing: Discontinuity (gradient undefined at non-smooth points), Saddle Confusion (zero-gradient points may be saddles, not extrema — optimization callers assume they're extrema).
The mechanism text uses mathematical notation (∇f) which is right for precision but may be opaque to readers — a plain-language gloss alongside would help.
The differentiable-space precondition is stated as a qualifier but not enforced. Callers who invoke Gradient over non-smooth domains are technically out-of-spec but the pattern offers no check.

Gradient.family_discussion: Substrate pattern for directional change. Paired with `Entropy` (what changes), `Equilibrium` (where change is zero), `Attractor` (where trajectories converge). Invoked by learning, attention, and credit-assignment patterns across the Mind layer.

motivation.why_it_exists: Linear ChainOfThought models reasoning as a sequence; real reasoning branches and converges. GraphOfThought instantiates Think with DAG topology so evidence from multiple branches can meet at a single node. Without it, branching reasoning collapses to chain-like summaries that lose the convergence structure.
motivation.removability: Removable — most LLM reasoning today is chain-shaped, and the pattern is relatively new. For complex problems with real evidence convergence (debugging, research, multi-source synthesis), GraphOfThought captures structure that chains can't represent.

tensions: Graph expressiveness vs agent interpretability — chains are easy to follow; graphs require visualization or structured output to read.
Fan-in (evidence convergence) vs fan-out (branching exploration) — GraphOfThought supports both; managing them together is harder than either alone.
Single-evaluation per node (invariant) vs iterative refinement — the pattern forbids re-evaluating a node, which forces callers to a different pattern for iteration.
tradeoffs: Gains: accurate structural representation of branching/convergent reasoning, fan-in support for evidence synthesis, DAG discipline.
Gives up: simplicity. Graphs are harder to construct, harder to read, and harder to validate than chains.
critique: The invariant 'each node applies Think once' makes iteration a caller concern, which is tidy and pushes complexity out of the pattern.
No evaluation order specified — for DAG reasoning, order matters (topological vs some other ordering) and the pattern defers this.
Inherits acyclicity from DAG, ruling out feedback loops that some reasoning legitimately has.

GraphOfThought.family_discussion: Reasoning-topology primitive paired with ChainOfThought (linear counterpart), Think (the operation), and DAG (the topology). Compare with Reflexion — GraphOfThought is structural multi-branch reasoning; Reflexion is iterative re-thinking. Both extend basic Think, on different axes.

motivation.why_it_exists: Two agents meeting for the first time need a protocol to verify who's who and what each can speak. Greet names the initial-contact handshake: cryptographic identity verification plus compatibility check. Without it, every agent-to-agent interaction has to invent its own authentication and schema negotiation.
motivation.removability: Removable in closed-world systems with pre-known peers. Essential in open multi-agent ecosystems where connections form dynamically. Greet is part of AgentProtocol's minimum-viable bundle for interoperability.

usage.intended: initial contact protocol — cryptographic identity verification + CompatibilityCheck.
usage.broad_contexts: TLS handshake, OAuth flow initiation, API-version negotiation, agent discovery greeting, human introductions, protocol version negotiation.
usage.every_context_needs: identity verification, compatibility check, state transition Unknown → Connected.
usage.varies: authentication strength, extension negotiation, fallback on incompatibility, one-way vs mutual.

tensions: Mutual auth (invariant) vs one-sided trust — some handshakes only need one side to authenticate the other; the invariant rules out asymmetric trust relationships.
No-op on mismatch (invariant) vs graceful retry — drop on failure is clean and forbids iterative compatibility negotiation.
Cryptographic verification vs speed — every handshake pays a crypto cost, which adds up in systems with many short-lived connections.
tradeoffs: Gains: authenticated identity, explicit compatibility checking, clean transition from Unknown to Connected.
Gives up: ad-hoc connection. The pattern ceremonies every connection; for high-trust or short-lived scenarios, the ceremony exceeds the value.
critique: Authentication Failure as a failure mode is binary; real auth often has degrees (TLS certificate valid but from wrong issuer, identity verified but under question).
Protocol Mismatch failure mode has no retry mechanism — Greet is one-shot, and translation/bridging happens in other patterns.
The handshake doesn't specify what happens after (session establishment, key derivation); these are downstream concerns the pattern punts on.

Greet.family_discussion: Initial-contact primitive paired with Handshake (the generic protocol name), CompatibilityCheck (the schema verification), and AgentProtocol (the bundle that includes Greet). Compare with Discover — Discover finds agents to greet; Greet begins interaction. Sequential.

motivation.why_it_exists: Agents solving 'make it work' instead of 'do it right' produce hacks. HackDetect names the meta-check: flag interface modifications that bypass validation. Without the pattern, hacks accumulate.
motivation.removability: Removable in high-trust or creator-reviewed settings. Essential in autonomous agents where hack accumulation is a real risk.

usage.intended: detect shortcuts that break downstream invariants — modifying interfaces instead of fixing source data.
usage.future: any "is this a genuine fix or a hack?" discipline.
usage.broad_contexts: code review, integration-test-level detection, debugging discipline, scientific-analysis integrity, data-pipeline QA.
usage.every_context_needs: interface-code-modification detection, downstream-invariant tracking, local-success vs global-correctness distinction.
usage.varies: invariant-tracking granularity, detection mechanism, escalation on detection.

tensions: False Positives (named failure) — legitimate adapter changes flagged.
Hack Blindness (named failure) — novel hack patterns evade detection.
Justification Theater (named failure) — rationalizing hacks.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit hack detection.
Gives up: legitimate flexibility.
critique: All three named failures are real.
Detection heuristics are model-dependent.
Justification Theater is hardest to defeat.

HackDetect.family_discussion: Meta-check primitive paired with Critique, MetaCheck, and AdversarialSteel. Compare with DriftWatch — HackDetect is specific pattern detection; DriftWatch is behavioral.

motivation.why_it_exists: Structured transfer of control + context between agents — the swarm-architecture primitive. Without Handoff as a pattern, context transfer is ad-hoc and the atomicity property (never 'both hold responsibility' and never 'none hold it') is easy to violate.
motivation.removability: No. Swarm coordination, delegation protocols, and agent-to-agent task transfer all need it. Removing produces orphan tasks and double-ownership bugs.

usage.intended: transfer control and context between agents with full responsibility/authority transfer.
usage.future: any "you're in charge now" delegation with full authority.
usage.broad_contexts: shift handoffs (medical, ops), agent swarm role transitions, manager-to-manager transitions, project handoffs, specialized-agent routing.
usage.every_context_needs: context transfer, authority transfer, responsibility transfer, explicit yield by sender.
usage.varies: context-completeness requirement, acknowledgment protocol, fallback if receiver rejects.

tensions: Responsibility atomicity vs network reality: 'neither or both hold it briefly' is the invariant, but real networks have gaps. The pattern is a logical spec; physical enforcement requires confirmation protocols.
Full context transfer vs context pruning: 'context fully transferred' is strong but prunes no-longer-relevant information. Some handoffs are better done with filtered context.

Authority Ambiguity as a failure but no explicit authority-passing: the pattern transfers context but doesn't enforce a typed authority handoff. The receiving agent must accept — if acceptance is implicit, ambiguity emerges.
tradeoffs: Responsibility atomicity invariant buys no-double-ownership at the cost of needing explicit confirm/reject from receiver.
Full context transfer buys receiver autonomy at the cost of bandwidth.
Society-layer placement correctly reflects the multi-agent nature at the cost of coupling to multi-agent assumptions.
critique: Two invariants, two failure modes. Missing: Acknowledgment (receiver must confirm), Reversibility (rejected handoffs return to sender cleanly), Context Integrity (transferred context is unchanged from sender's view).
Authority Ambiguity is named but the pattern has no authority-typing — solving it requires Identity patterns the mechanism doesn't declare as composed_with.
'Agent-specific instructions' is mentioned in the mechanism but not structured — receivers parse ad-hoc.

Handoff.family_discussion: The swarm-coordination primitive for control transfer. Composes with `Context` (what is transferred), `Identity` (who is involved). Sibling to `Delegate` (which is initiated-by-principal task assignment); Handoff is peer-to-peer transfer of ongoing work.

motivation.why_it_exists: Absence of signal is not proof of failure — the sender may just be quiet. Heartbeat names the periodic liveness signal: emit at interval, missing K consecutive = failure detection. Without it, failure detection is reactive (after the fact) rather than proactive (while work is supposed to be happening).
motivation.removability: Non-removable in distributed systems. Every liveness-aware protocol uses Heartbeat or equivalent. Simpler ping-response patterns substitute for it; the named Heartbeat specifically includes health metrics and the K-missing failure-detection threshold.

usage.intended: liveness detection via periodic signals.
usage.future: any periodic signal establishing continued existence.
usage.broad_contexts: distributed system health checks, web service uptime monitoring, agent aliveness, IoT device liveness, connection-pool health, biological heartbeat metaphor, session keepalives.
usage.every_context_needs: emitter, receiver, interval, miss-threshold for failure detection.
usage.varies: interval value (ms for local, minutes for distributed), payload (empty ping vs health metrics), authentication, K-out-of-N tolerance.

tensions: Interval tightness (early detection) vs bandwidth cost — frequent heartbeats detect failure fast and eat bandwidth; sparse heartbeats save bandwidth and delay detection.
K-missing threshold — too low produces false positives on network congestion (the named failure mode); too high lets real failures linger.
Heartbeat includes health metrics or just liveness — richer heartbeats cost more; minimal heartbeats lose the health context that often matters.
tradeoffs: Gains: proactive failure detection, explicit liveness contract, composable with Quorum for group-liveness decisions.
Gives up: network overhead and occasional false positives. Every heartbeating system has to tune between sensitivity and robustness.
critique: False failure detection via network congestion is the dominant real failure and the pattern has no adaptive interval — it's a static schedule.
Health metrics in the heartbeat are optional and under-specified; different systems include different metrics, making heartbeat comparisons across implementations meaningless.
The K-missing threshold is a tuning knob with no default derivation rule; getting it wrong is the same failure in both directions.

Heartbeat.family_discussion: Liveness-detection primitive paired with Quorum (the group-liveness consumer), FailureDetector (the general pattern), and Delegate (which uses Heartbeat for progress tracking). Compare with Probe — Heartbeat is periodic self-signal; Probe is active external check. Different liveness verification styles.

motivation.why_it_exists: Multi-party transactions need escrow — value held until both parties fulfill their side, with timeout return if one doesn't. HeldRelease names the hash-lock escrow discipline: deposit with condition hash, release on preimage, timeout returns. Without it, multi-party trades require pre-existing trust (doesn't scale) or instant atomic commit (often not possible).
motivation.removability: Removable in single-party or trusted-broker settings. Essential in trustless or distributed coordination, where atomic swap without trusted third party is the goal. The pattern is imported from cryptocurrency / HTLC semantics into general agent coordination.

usage.intended: trustless conditional value transfer (escrow).
usage.broad_contexts: crypto escrows, atomic swaps, payment channels, contingent contracts, staged delivery, milestone payments, dispute resolution, insurance payouts, bail bonds.
usage.every_context_needs: held value, release condition (hash commitment), timeout, state machine (EMPTY→HELD→RELEASED/RETURNED).
usage.varies: cryptographic primitives (hash algo, timelock type), dispute protocol, multi-party variants, partial release, streaming semantics.

tensions: Preimage secrecy vs recoverability — if the preimage is lost, timeout returns funds (safe for A, B loses). The safety invariant has an asymmetric cost.
Timeout tuning — too short and legitimate claims race the deadline; too long and failed transactions hold value indefinitely.
Condition ambiguity — hash commits to bytes, not semantics. Parties must agree off-chain on what the preimage means, and the pattern doesn't own that negotiation.
tradeoffs: Gains: trustless escrow semantics, atomic state (Locked/Released/Returned), timeout-bounded exposure.
Gives up: semantic flexibility. Condition ambiguity — the hash commits to bytes, not meaning — is a structural limitation of hash-based escrow.
critique: Condition ambiguity is endemic — the parties must agree what satisfies the hash, and the pattern has no protocol for that agreement.
Timeout racing is a real failure in adversarial settings — near expiry, both CLAIM and TIMEOUT may be in flight; the pattern has no specified tie-breaker.
Preimage loss is a failure mode for Party B with no recovery. In practice parties over-collateralize to limit B's downside; the pattern doesn't own this.

HeldRelease.family_discussion: Escrow primitive paired with Contract (the agreement container), Award (the acceptance event), and Sign (the commitment action). Compare with AtomicBid — HeldRelease is multi-party value escrow; AtomicBid is single-actor log-then-act. Different coordination shapes.

motivation.why_it_exists: Deliberate reasoning (ChainOfThought) is expensive. For common patterns where a prior answer fits, HeuristicSnap bypasses deliberation via similarity-based cache hit. Without it, agents pay the deliberate-reasoning tax on every problem, including familiar ones where the answer is already in memory.
motivation.removability: Removable if speed isn't a concern. The pattern is specifically for budget-constrained fast response (<100ms), and in low-budget regimes it's essential. The similarity threshold (0.6) is the quality filter; removing the pattern removes the named fast path.

usage.intended: fast pattern-match against cached experience — <100ms decisions bypassing reasoning chains.
usage.future: any "quick intuitive response from memory" mechanism.
usage.broad_contexts: System-1 intuition, expert rapid judgment, flash diagnostic decisions, chess blitz moves, driving reflexes, fast-attention routing.
usage.every_context_needs: cached experience database, similarity matching, low-latency decision.
usage.varies: cache-hit threshold, fallback to deep reasoning, cache-freshness policy.

tensions: Speed (the point) vs accuracy — the pattern explicitly favors latency over accuracy. Wrong fast answers are the intended cost.
Confidence floor (≥0.6) vs coverage — tighter threshold produces fewer snaps (more fall-throughs to deliberation); looser threshold risks worse snaps.
Pattern-match on past experiences vs novel situations — HeuristicSnap fails silently on genuinely novel problems that look similar to past ones.
tradeoffs: Gains: sub-100ms decisions, preserved deliberate-reasoning budget for hard problems, explicit similarity threshold.
Gives up: accuracy on edge cases. HeuristicSnap is the fast path; the deliberate path (ChainOfThought) is the correct path and the pattern routes between them by budget.
critique: The 0.6 similarity floor is defaults-as-doctrine — the right threshold depends on domain, false-positive cost, and cache quality.
No mechanism for marking snap failures — when HeuristicSnap returns a wrong answer, the cache isn't updated to reflect the failure; the pattern is learn-agnostic.
Latency threshold (<100ms) is a single metric; richer QoS constraints (worst-case latency, tail latency) aren't captured.

HeuristicSnap.family_discussion: Cognitive shortcut primitive paired with ChainOfThought (the deliberate counterpart), Cache (the substrate), and PathwayMemory (memoized reasoning). Compare with Fermi — HeuristicSnap is pattern-match lookup; Fermi is decomposed estimation. Both are fast-reasoning patterns, on different cognitive paths.

motivation.why_it_exists: Categories and authority both benefit from vertical structure — parent/child, upper/lower, contains/contained. Hierarchy names the basic vertical-ranking primitive. Without it, Tree, Taxonomy, Authority, Inheritance all have to invent their own 'this is above that' semantics.
motivation.removability: Very thin — a structural primitive more than a rich pattern. The value is in the naming and in providing a common referent for 'vertical structure.' Hard to argue against keeping it, even as it does little on its own.

usage.intended: vertical ranking of categories/objects — defines Upper/Lower, inheritance, authority.
usage.broad_contexts: org charts, taxonomy hierarchies, maslow's hierarchy of needs, priority hierarchies, biological taxonomies, file-system hierarchies, type hierarchies.
usage.every_context_needs: vertical ordering, Upper/Lower relations, inheritance rule, authority rule.
usage.varies: single-inheritance vs multiple, dynamism, enforcement of strict-vs-loose hierarchy.

tensions: Single-parent structure (tree-like) vs multi-parent (DAG-like) — Hierarchy doesn't specify, leaving it ambiguous.
Inheritance semantics — is lower inherits-from upper, contains upper, reports-to upper? The pattern conflates several kinds of vertical relationships.
Hierarchy as structure vs authority — categories are hierarchical but not authoritative; org charts are hierarchical and authoritative; the pattern doesn't distinguish.
tradeoffs: Gains: shared vocabulary for vertical structure, foundation for Tree, Taxonomy, Authority, Inheritance.
Gives up: precision. Hierarchy is deliberately vague, and specific hierarchies need specific semantics the pattern doesn't provide.
critique: Almost a stub — one-line mechanism, no invariants, no failure modes. The pattern's value is classificatory.
Conflates multiple distinct semantics: categorical hierarchy (class subtype), authority hierarchy (boss-subordinate), containment hierarchy (folder-file).
No semantics for multiple inheritance, crossing hierarchies, or flat alternatives — the pattern implies strict vertical structure.

Hierarchy.family_discussion: Foundational structural primitive paired with Tree (a specific hierarchical topology), Category (the groupable unit), and Authority (the responsibility flavor). Compare with Lattice — Hierarchy is vertical, Lattice allows both vertical and horizontal. Different structural constraints.

motivation.why_it_exists: Judging past decisions by outcomes produces systematic unfairness — good decisions with bad outcomes (unlucky) vs bad decisions with good outcomes (lucky) both get miscounted. HindsightBlock names the decision-time evaluation discipline: reconstruct what was known then, judge expected value given that information. Without the pattern, learning from history gets distorted by outcome bias.
motivation.removability: Removable if you accept outcome-based judgment as legitimate. For serious post-mortem, calibration, or reputation tracking, the pattern is essential — the Prior Commitment invariant (cryptographic commitment before outcome) is the anti-hindsight defense.

usage.intended: prevent results-oriented thinking — judge past decisions by ex-ante info, not outcome.
usage.future: any "separate decision quality from outcome" discipline.
usage.broad_contexts: poker theory (Annie Duke), investment analysis, military decision reviews, sports analytics (process vs results), judicial review, accountability-despite-bad-luck.
usage.every_context_needs: decision reconstruction at time T, judgment of quality given available info at T, separation from actual outcome.
usage.varies: information-reconstruction rigor, comparison baseline, counterfactual weighting.

tensions: No Revision vs corrective learning — the invariant forbids editing the log after the fact, which is correct and prevents useful corrections to mis-logged decisions.
Prior Commitment (cryptographic) vs informal contexts — for casual decisions, crypto commitment is overhead; the pattern doesn't scale down gracefully.
Outcome Blindness (named failure) — ignoring outcomes entirely prevents learning from model errors; the pattern's anti-hindsight is so strong it can become anti-learning.
tradeoffs: Gains: fair decision-quality evaluation, cryptographic anti-hindsight, structured prior commitment.
Gives up: ease and sometimes learning speed. Evaluating at decision-time is harder than evaluating at outcome-time and the discipline is unnatural.
critique: Outcome Blindness is the named dual failure — too strict a separation of decision-quality from outcome-quality prevents learning from black swans.
Cryptographic commitment is strong discipline and operationally heavy; many real decisions don't warrant it.
The 'reconstruct information available at decision time' step is itself judgment — hindsight leaks in subtly even when prevented structurally.

HindsightBlock.family_discussion: Epistemic-hygiene primitive paired with CounterfactualAnchor (freeze prediction before observation), ConfidenceCalibrate (alignment loop), and IntentGap (decision-vs-outcome divergence). Core piece of the anti-hindsight-bias family.

motivation.why_it_exists: Sub-tasks lose global context when split. HolographicShard names the context-preserving split: each shard carries parent_goal_hash, intent summary, inherited constraints. Without the pattern, shards become context-free.
motivation.removability: Removable — callers can pass context manually. HolographicShard systematizes the inheritance.

usage.intended: context-preserving slice — sub-tasks contain a reference to the global goal.
usage.future: any fragment carrying reconstructability of the whole.
usage.broad_contexts: distributed task decomposition, multi-agent coordination shards, federated learning samples, document chunks with source metadata, hologram reconstruction analogy.
usage.every_context_needs: parent_goal_hash, intent_summary, constraint_inheritance. All three are load-bearing — without them local action can't verify global alignment.
usage.varies: recovery detail (approximate vs exact), compression of the "seed," shard granularity.

tensions: Context Bloat (named failure) — shard becomes larger than task.
Information Redundancy invariant vs storage cost.
K-of-N reconstruction vs simpler designs.
tradeoffs: Gains: global-context preservation across splits.
Gives up: shard compactness.
critique: Context Bloat is endemic — every shard carrying full global history.
Information Redundancy is a strong invariant that costs storage.
The holographic metaphor is evocative; operationalization varies.

HolographicShard.family_discussion: Sharding primitive paired with Shard (general), ContextFirst (refresh discipline), and Decompose.

motivation.why_this_layer: authored gate that pauses for external decision
motivation.why_it_exists: Some actions are too consequential to delegate fully to agents. HumanApprove names the checkpoint-gate: agent presents task/rationale/risk, human explicitly consents, execution continues. Without it, high-stakes agent autonomy is unbounded; with it, humans can interrupt without pattern-shaming either the agent or the operator.
motivation.removability: Removable only at high-stakes cost. For irreversible, expensive, or safety-critical actions, HumanApprove is the named pattern. The alternatives (post-hoc audit, policy-based allow-lists) are weaker: audit discovers misuse; HumanApprove prevents it.

usage.intended: high-stakes action gating by a human operator.
usage.future: any decision needing a human judgment call.
usage.broad_contexts: production deploys, financial transactions, legal review, compliance committees, test mocks (auto-approve with timeout), emergency auto-reject, medical approvals, policy reviews, art-moderation, publishing signoffs.
usage.every_context_needs: the Task presented to human, rationale, risk assessment; yields approved/rejected/timeout.
usage.varies: `timeout` (ms to weeks — see §3.17), `challenge_required` (Boolean, principled), escalation path, UX channel (email, Slack, in-app), quorum (some contexts need multiple approvers).
usage.extensions: `LegalReview` (weeks timeout, committee quorum), `EmergencyApprove` (sub-second timeout, auto-reject default), `TestMockApprove` (auto-approve in test).

tensions: Approval Fatigue (named failure) vs meaningful oversight — too many approvals produces rubber-stamping; too few produces missed critical cases.
Blocking vs timeout — if human is unavailable, does the system halt forever? The pattern requires a timeout policy without prescribing one.
Cognitive friction (invariant: challenge-code match) vs ease of approval — friction prevents fatigue and adds delay on every legitimate approval.
tradeoffs: Gains: human-in-the-loop for critical actions, structured challenge-code matching against rubber-stamping, explicit audit trail.
Gives up: autonomy and speed. Every gated action pays the human-round-trip tax; for busy operators, this becomes bottleneck.
critique: Approval Fatigue is endemic — challenge codes help but high-volume approval requests still degrade into pattern-matching without actual review.

Indefinite blocking when human is unavailable is a real failure; timeout policies default to either 'fail closed' (halt) or 'fail open' (proceed without approval), and both are wrong in different contexts.
Context Loss — the agent presents context; if the human doesn't understand the proposed action, the approval is performative.

HumanApprove.family_discussion: Safety-pattern paired with EjectionSeat (forced stop), FailClosed (default deny), and AuditTrail (who approved what). Compare with DeliberativeAlign — HumanApprove is explicit human check; DeliberativeAlign is agent self-check against policy. Both are pre-action safety, at different trust assignments.

motivation.why_it_exists: Responding to a person requires variable-depth engagement — mundane fast, complex careful. §6.2 paper protocol: decompose response into five orthogonal faculties. Without the pattern, responses are either shallow-everywhere or deep-everywhere.
motivation.removability: Removable — simpler response patterns work. The §6.2 protocol is specifically for person-facing interaction with depth variance.

tensions: Five-faculty orthogonal invariant vs real human interaction complexity.
Variable-depth vs consistency — deep for some topics, shallow for others.
Paper-specific methodology — five is their choice.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured variable-depth response.
Gives up: uniformity.
critique: Five faculties is the paper's decomposition; alternatives exist.
Orthogonality is aspirational.
No failure modes listed.

HumanEmulatorProtocol.family_discussion: §6 paper protocol sibling of CollaborativeWritingProtocol, EthicalReasoningProtocol, DiscoveryProtocol, TemporalEnsembleForecasting. Uses ConceptualDecomposition.

motivation.why_it_exists: Staging a prediction for testing is different from asserting it as true. Hypothesis names the testable, provisional, explicit-commitment-to-check form — distinct from Claim (asserted), Assumption (held to proceed), Axiom (unprovable foundation). Without the named primitive, all four collapse into 'I think' with no differentiation.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. The four-way distinction (Hypothesis/Claim/Assumption/Axiom) is the backbone of the epistemic-stance family, and removing any of them destroys the others' clarity. Hypothesis specifically names the 'testable, under test' slot.

usage.intended: tentative explanation subject to verification/falsification.
usage.future: any claim staged for empirical testing.
usage.broad_contexts: scientific hypotheses, debugging conjectures, detective work, forensic reasoning, theory formation, null-hypothesis testing, bug-cause candidates.
usage.every_context_needs: the claim itself, status (untested/corroborated/falsified), test-ability (must be empirically checkable — distinguishes from Assumption and Axiom).
usage.varies: confidence tracking, evidence links, competing-hypothesis structure, falsification-condition spec.

tensions: Testable (the commitment) vs untestable-but-useful — some hypotheses are about the future or about rare events; 'testable' depends on what tests are available.
Provisional vs load-bearing — treating a hypothesis as provisional is correct; downstream reasoning often treats it as settled anyway.
Explicit commitment to be checked vs checking never happens — agents state hypotheses and fail to follow up; the pattern's commitment is only as strong as the enforcer.
tradeoffs: Gains: clean epistemic-stance distinction, testability invariant, a commitment-to-check slot.
Gives up: fluency. Agents want to state things; the Hypothesis discipline asks 'what would falsify this?' which interrupts momentum.
critique: Testability is a weak constraint — technically falsifiable hypotheses can still be untestable in practice (need conditions that don't occur).
The 'explicit commitment to be checked' is aspirational; the pattern doesn't include machinery to enforce the check.
Distinction from Claim/Assumption/Axiom is clean conceptually and often muddied in real use.

Hypothesis.family_discussion: Core epistemic-stance primitive paired with Claim (asserted truth), Assumption (provisional proceed), Axiom (foundational). Consumed by Falsification (the test), EmpiricalTest (the pipeline), and BayesUpdate (the revision).

motivation.why_it_exists: The scientific method as a cognitive cycle — generate hypothesis, simulate, check, update, repeat. HypothesisEngine names the engine that runs this cycle. Without it, the components (Hypothesis, Falsification, BeliefTracking) exist in isolation; the engine is what connects them into a repeatable loop.
motivation.removability: Removable — agents can wire the pieces together by hand. The named engine provides a canonical loop shape that reviewers can check ('are we running the cycle, or just generating hypotheses and hoping?'). Remove it and the scientific-method structure becomes implicit.

usage.intended: automated scientific method cycle — Discover → Trace → Check → Stigmergy(publish).
usage.broad_contexts: autonomous scientific research, self-improving AI, debugging automation, market-hypothesis testing, evolutionary-design search.
usage.every_context_needs: hypothesis generator, simulation-and-trace, consistency validator, publication mechanism.
usage.varies: domain specificity, cycle rate, validation rigor, publication protocol, inter-cycle learning.

tensions: Cycle completeness vs speed — running the full cycle on every hypothesis is slow; skipping steps is fast and error-prone.
Confirmation bias (named failure) vs productive pursuit — agents select evidence supporting preferred hypotheses; the pattern has no structural defense.
Falsification criteria vs non-falsifiable hypotheses — the pattern demands criteria, which some legitimate hypotheses (about values, preferences, future) struggle to meet.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured scientific-method cycle, explicit engine for hypothesis evaluation.
Gives up: flexibility. The loop shape imposes ceremony; problems that don't fit the scientific-method mold have to use other patterns.
critique: Confirmation bias is the dominant failure and the pattern names it without mitigating; the engine structure doesn't prevent motivated selection of evidence.
Untestable hypotheses slipping past the falsification-criteria requirement is called out; enforcement depends on caller discipline.
The cycle is modeled as clean iteration; real scientific practice has messier interleaving of steps that the pattern flattens.

HypothesisEngine.family_discussion: Methodology engine paired with Hypothesis (the unit), Falsification (the test), BayesUpdate (the revision), and BeliefTracking (the audit). Compare with HypothesisLadder — HypothesisEngine is the running cycle; HypothesisLadder is the state structure the cycle operates on.

motivation.why_this_layer: Bayesian belief updating via falsification rungs
motivation.why_it_exists: Agents that act on one hypothesis and ignore alternatives get trapped by confirmation bias. HypothesisLadder names the multi-hypothesis discipline: maintain probability-ranked candidates, act on the top, keep the rest alive, update via BayesUpdate as data arrives. Without it, hypothesis switching is either rigid (single hypothesis) or chaotic (no ranking).
motivation.removability: Removable when one hypothesis is dominant. Essential in genuinely uncertain situations with multiple viable candidates. The Ascension Rule (can't advance without validation) is the anti-flailing invariant.

usage.intended: Bayesian belief updating via falsifiable rungs — act on highest-probability hypothesis, keep others alive.
usage.broad_contexts: scientific method, debugging decision trees, medical diagnosis ladders, investment hypothesis tracking, AI safety research, intelligence analysis.
usage.every_context_needs: hypothesis list with probabilities, Bayesian update on new data, act-on-highest rule, alive-other-hypotheses tracking.
usage.varies: ladder depth, update frequency, hypothesis pruning policy, experiment-cost consideration.

tensions: Ascension Rule (evidence required to advance) vs quick pivoting — requiring validation before moving up a rung is safe and slow.
Exclusivity (hypotheses at same rung mutually exclusive) vs overlapping hypotheses — real candidates often have partial overlap; strict exclusivity is an idealization.
Falsifiability at each rung vs soft hypotheses — the invariant demands testable disprove conditions, which some legitimate hypotheses lack.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured multi-hypothesis tracking, explicit ascension discipline, falsifiability enforced at every rung.
Gives up: fluency and sometimes insight. 'Clinging to low-probability priors' (the named failure) is the pattern's pathology.
critique: Clinging to low-probability priors is named as a failure and the pattern has no culling mechanism — low-probability hypotheses accumulate forever.
The invariants are now deduplicated (was: two Falsifiability lines + Ascension/Evidence redundant). Exclusivity is retained as mathematically required for the Bayesian probability framework.

Exclusivity is correct for the Bayesian math but excludes real hypothesis sets with overlapping support (e.g., cold vs flu both cause fever). Users with overlapping hypotheses need a different pattern.

HypothesisLadder.family_discussion: Hypothesis-tracking primitive paired with Hypothesis (the unit), BayesUpdate (the revision substrate), and BeliefTracking (the audit trail). Compare with BeliefTracking — HypothesisLadder is specifically multi-hypothesis; BeliefTracking is general belief version control.

motivation.why_it_exists: Prevents oscillation when a state transition is controlled by a signal near a threshold. Single-threshold transitions oscillate under noise; asymmetric thresholds (higher-to-enter, lower-to-exit) create a stable region where small perturbations don't flip state. Thermostats, mode switches, alerting systems all need this — making it a pattern avoids per-site reinvention.
motivation.removability: Probably not. The library could conceivably collapse Hysteresis into 'dual-threshold state transition' as a caller pattern, but the pattern formalizes the asymmetry and the damping relationship — neither is obvious without the explicit pattern.

usage.intended: prevent oscillation via asymmetric state-transition thresholds.
usage.broad_contexts: thermostats, circuit breakers, trigger filtering, alert deduplication, auto-scaling thresholds, feature-flag rollout guards, Schmitt triggers.
usage.every_context_needs: upper threshold (A→B), lower threshold (B→A), gap between them.
usage.varies: threshold values, adaptivity, multi-state variants, reset mechanisms.

tensions: Gap sizing: too small a gap and oscillation returns; too large and state gets stuck (the named failure mode). The pattern doesn't prescribe how to choose the gap — it's a domain concern.

Fixed vs adaptive thresholds: fixed thresholds are simple but can't handle drifting baselines; adaptive thresholds handle drift but introduce their own stability concerns. The pattern allows both without specifying tradeoffs.
Binary state vs multi-state: the mechanism is binary (A↔B). Multi-state systems need more than two thresholds — that's a descendant pattern the library doesn't explicitly mint.
tradeoffs: Asymmetric thresholds buy stability at the cost of inertia — state change requires more evidence than a single threshold would need.
Fixed T_up > T_down invariant buys correctness at the cost of disallowing instantaneous-equality configurations (single-threshold is not a degenerate case of Hysteresis — it's a separate pattern).
Dampen composition (as noted in the mechanism) adds smoothing but also latency.
critique: Only one failure mode (Stuck State from wide gap). Missing: Inverted Thresholds (T_up < T_down would silently invert the semantics), Threshold Drift (adaptive thresholds shift such that T_up crosses T_down), Signal Spike (brief signal excursion past both thresholds creates a fast A→B→A that the gap was supposed to prevent).
Only one invariant (T_up > T_down). Missing: State transitions are triggered by threshold-crossing, not threshold-equality; re-entry from B requires re-crossing T_up (not just exceeding T_down).

The relationship to `Dampen` is mentioned but the composition is unclear — does Hysteresis use Dampen internally, or are they parallel? The mechanism hints at 'uses a dampen effect,' but the pattern has no composes_with declaration for Dampen in what I can see.

Hysteresis.family_discussion: Sibling to `Dampen` (continuous attenuation) and `Decay` (time-based attenuation). Where Dampen smooths signal magnitudes and Decay attenuates stale values, Hysteresis discretizes transitions — the three handle different temporal dynamics of the same underlying stability problem.

motivation.why_it_exists: Distributed systems drop, retry, and duplicate messages. Without idempotency, duplicate writes cause duplicate side effects — charged twice, email sent twice, record inserted twice. IdempotentWrite names the discipline: every write carries an idempotency key, receiver caches keys, duplicates return the cached result without re-executing.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in distributed systems. Every reliable write API needs this property; removing it makes retry semantics impossible. The pattern is imported from distributed-systems practice and named to make the property explicit.

usage.intended: technical primitive — every write includes unique Idempotency Key; duplicates return stored result.
usage.broad_contexts: HTTP POST with Idempotency-Key header, payment-API idempotency, message-queue at-least-once-safe processing, database upsert patterns, distributed-task-execution safety.
usage.every_context_needs: unique key per request, key-tracking by receiver, duplicate-returns-stored-result semantic, side-effect-safe semantic.
usage.varies: key generation, key retention window, storage medium.

tensions: Key uniqueness vs key reuse — the named failure mode 'key collision' happens when two different requests pick the same key.
Cache size — the key cache can't grow forever; eviction risks letting old duplicates through.
Timeout on cache entries — too short risks letting duplicates through after expiry; too long bloats storage.
tradeoffs: Gains: safe retries, deduplication, clean semantics for 'execute once even if called multiple times.'
Gives up: storage. Every unique write now requires the cache entry, which compounds across a high-throughput system.
critique: Key collision is the named failure and is hard to prevent without client discipline; the pattern trusts the caller to generate unique keys.
Cache eviction strategy is unspecified — LRU, TTL-based, or all-retention are all reasonable and have different failure profiles.
The pattern doesn't address what happens on partial-failure retries that mix successful and failed sub-operations.

IdempotentWrite.family_discussion: Distributed-systems primitive paired with Retry (the trigger), Cache (the substrate), and Act (the action being de-duped). Compare with HeldRelease — IdempotentWrite provides safe retry; HeldRelease provides safe multi-party transaction. Both are safety primitives for distributed operations.

motivation.why_it_exists: Distinguishing Self from Other is the most basic agent capability. Identity names the unique distinguishing context — history, reputation, public keys. Without it, agents can't be tracked across sessions, reputation can't accumulate, and trust bootstrapping has no referent.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in multi-agent systems. Every auth, reputation, and coordination primitive depends on Identity. The distinction from Nature (what you are) and Role (what you do) is load-bearing — Identity is the persistent handle that outlasts roles and encompasses both nature and history.

usage.intended: unique distinguishing context of an agent — the persistent "Who."
usage.broad_contexts: cryptographic agent IDs, human pseudonyms, corporate personas, service accounts, bot handles, role-bound identities, federated identities, anonymous-but-unique identifiers.
usage.every_context_needs: uniqueness guarantee within scope; persistence across interactions; a way to distinguish Self from Other.
usage.varies: key material (public keys, DIDs, UUIDs, username+password), reputation attachments, history binding, key rotation mechanics, pseudonymity vs real-name.

tensions: Persistence vs privacy — persistent identity enables reputation and enables tracking; the same property serves both goals.
Unique handle vs multiple personas — real entities sometimes need multiple identities (legal pseudonyms, compartmentalization); the pattern implies singularity.
Identity vs Authentication — Identity is who you claim to be; Authentication is proving it. The pattern conflates them in some framings.
tradeoffs: Gains: persistent agent handle, reputation substrate, trust bootstrapping target.
Gives up: privacy options. Identity-based systems necessarily track, which conflicts with anonymity and privacy preferences.
critique: Very thin mechanism — the pattern lists components (history, reputation, public keys) without a coherent shape.
Conflates identity-claim with identity-proof; the two have different failure modes.
No failure modes listed — Identity has many (compromise, impersonation, sybil attack) that the pattern doesn't catalogue.

Identity.family_discussion: Foundational primitive paired with Nature (what you are), Role (what you do), Reputation (how you're perceived), and Authentication (the proof mechanism). Compare with ConceptAnchor — Identity is the persistent handle for agents; ConceptAnchor is for concepts. Both are addressability primitives.

motivation.why_it_exists: Not all counterparties are alike — humans (Biologicals) and agents (Synthetics) warrant different modes. IdentityHandshake names the verification plus switching protocol: discover Identity, check Nature, route to Service mode or Coordination mode. Without it, agents treat all counterparts uniformly, which produces either over-service (toward other agents) or under-service (toward humans).
motivation.removability: Removable in single-population environments (all human users, or all agents). The pattern's value is specifically in mixed environments where the counterparty's nature should shift behavior. Remove it and the agent picks one mode and applies it universally.

usage.intended: distinguish Peer from Principal — verify ontological origin to switch behavior modes.
usage.future: any "who am I talking to?" type identification mechanism.
usage.broad_contexts: AI-vs-human identification, authenticated-vs-anonymous branching, service-vs-user detection, B2B-vs-B2C protocol selection, synthetic-vs-biological protocols.
usage.every_context_needs: Discover(identity) + Check(nature), mode-switching on result, cryptographic verification.
usage.varies: authentication strength, mode set, fallback on ambiguous identity, spoof resistance.

tensions: Nature verification vs privacy — some counterparties don't want their nature (human/machine) revealed; the pattern requires it for routing.
Service vs Coordination modes — the binary split is pragmatic and coarse; some agents warrant hybrid treatment.
Partial trust (named failure) vs complete verification — partial verification is convenient and dangerous; the pattern is vulnerable to this failure.
tradeoffs: Gains: nature-aware interaction routing, explicit handshake for mixed populations, service/coordination distinction.
Gives up: uniform treatment. Agents that deliberately treat all counterparts the same can't use this pattern.
critique: Replay (named failure) is a canonical handshake attack — reusing a valid handshake in a new context. Mitigation (nonce, fresh context) isn't specified in invariants.
The binary Biological/Synthetic distinction is 2026-specific; future mixed populations (augmented, distributed, collective) don't fit.
Multi-stage authentication is gestured at but not specified; implementation shape matters a lot for security properties.

IdentityHandshake.family_discussion: Discovery-plus-verification primitive paired with Discover(Identity) and Check(Nature) as its substrate. Compare with Greet — Greet is generic handshake; IdentityHandshake is Nature-aware handshake for mode routing.

motivation.why_it_exists: Misalignment between expectation and reality is the universal signal for learning, humor, and paradox. Incongruity names the raw difference between predicted and observed state. Without a named primitive, the difference gets folded into Anomaly (deviation) or FailureTrace (structured failure), losing the generality.
motivation.removability: Very thin. Could be folded into Anomaly or Delta, but the pattern's value is the general 'predicted vs observed mismatch' framing that spans epistemic, emotional, and logical domains. Remove it and the generality is lost.

usage.intended: misalignment between expectation and reality — the difference between predicted and observed.
usage.broad_contexts: humor (classic theory), paradox detection, learning signals, debugging (this isn't what I expected), anomaly detection, cognitive dissonance.
usage.every_context_needs: prediction, observation, difference/mismatch computation.
usage.varies: difference metric, severity scaling, routing of incongruity signal.

tensions: Signal vs noise — every prediction has some error; the pattern doesn't distinguish meaningful from ignorable incongruity.
Incongruity as signal vs incongruity as event — some patterns consume the signal (learning), others consume the event (humor, paradox); the pattern is agnostic.
Discrete vs graded mismatch — the pattern names a difference; real differences have magnitude and direction, under-specified here.
tradeoffs: Gains: general named primitive for predicted-observed mismatch, spans multiple domains (epistemic, emotional, logical).
Gives up: operational precision. Incongruity is a gesture; specific consumers (Anomaly, FailureTrace, SurprisalUpdate) add structure.
critique: Almost a stub — one-sentence mechanism, no invariants, no failure modes.
Conflates multiple kinds of mismatch (epistemic deviation, humor-producing surprise, logical paradox) that have different operational shapes.
The pattern is used by many consumers but doesn't provide the interface richness they need, so they effectively re-derive it.

Incongruity.family_discussion: Foundational primitive consumed by Anomaly, Surprisal, FailureTrace, Falsification. Sibling of Delta and Difference. Compare with Novelty — Incongruity is prediction-reality gap; Novelty is genuinely-new-without-prediction. Different shapes of 'this is unexpected.'

motivation.why_it_exists: Moving from 'the sun rose yesterday, and the day before, and the day before' to 'the sun rises every day' is Induction — the probable-from-instances inference mode. Without a named slot, agents either treat induction as deduction (over-claiming certainty) or dismiss it as 'just guessing' (under-claiming usefulness). Induction names the probable middle.
motivation.removability: Non-removable as a reasoning mode. Part of the classical triad with Deduction and Abduction. Remove it and one leg of the epistemic taxonomy collapses. The pattern is thin because its content is in classical logic; the slot-holding is the value.

usage.intended: specific observations → general rule (probabilistic, not certain).
usage.broad_contexts: scientific generalization, ML training, pattern recognition, base-rate estimation, statistical inference, law-of-large-numbers reasoning, curve fitting.
usage.every_context_needs: specific observations, inferred general claim, probabilistic (not certain) conclusion semantic.
usage.varies: sample size, generalization method, confidence estimation, robustness to outliers, prior-weighted updates.

tensions: Probabilistic (the invariant) vs usefulness — probable conclusions are weaker than certain ones and often all you can have.
Generalization invariant (rule covers more than data) vs overfitting — generalizing too hard produces rules that don't hold.
Hume's problem — the classical philosophical issue; induction has no formal justification, it's just what works, and the pattern is built on this uneasy foundation.
tradeoffs: Gains: a named slot for probable-from-instances inference, the Deduction/Induction/Abduction triad as a complete epistemic partition.
Gives up: certainty. Induction is structurally weaker than Deduction, and the pattern owns that weakness explicitly.
critique: Almost a stub — one-line mechanism, two invariants. The classical philosophy of induction is deep; the pattern gestures at it.
Hume's problem isn't addressed — the pattern just asserts 'probable' without owning the philosophical difficulty.
No failure modes — Induction has many (overfitting, base-rate neglect, small-sample bias) that the pattern doesn't catalogue.

Induction.family_discussion: Part of the classical reasoning triad with Deduction (necessary) and Abduction (inference to best explanation). Operationalized as Generalize. Consumed by BayesUpdate, HypothesisEngine. Foundational for empirical reasoning.

motivation.why_it_exists: Untrusted input at any interface boundary is a vulnerability. InputGuard names the validation filter: schema compliance, type safety, constraint check, fail-closed on violation. Without the named pattern, input validation happens ad-hoc at every interface, with gaps that produce injection and type-confusion attacks.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in any system with untrusted input. The pattern is the canonical 'guard the boundary' move; removing it doesn't remove the need, just the named discipline. Every interface ends up with some form of InputGuard regardless.

usage.intended: sanitize inputs before they reach a sensitive component.
usage.broad_contexts: API input validation, SQL-injection prevention, prompt-injection guards (for LLM apps), form-submission filters, message-broker content filters.
usage.every_context_needs: schema/constraint to enforce, violation handler (fail-closed), input stream being guarded.
usage.varies: schema language, coercion vs reject, rate limiting integration, whitelist vs blacklist approach.

tensions: Schema strictness (safety) vs interface flexibility — strict schemas reject malformed input and also reject legitimate variations the schema didn't anticipate.
Fail-closed on violation vs usability — rejecting unexpected input is safe and frustrating when the input was almost-right.
Bypass via encoding — the named failure mode: unexpected encodings or type coercions slip past the guard; the pattern can't catalog all evasion techniques.
tradeoffs: Gains: principled boundary defense, fail-closed semantics, explicit validation contract.
Gives up: interface evolution. Schema-locked interfaces resist extension; legitimate new inputs require schema updates before they pass.
critique: Bypass via unexpected encoding is the canonical failure and has no structural defense in the pattern — it's an arms race between attackers and schema writers.
Overly permissive schemas are the other failure mode; getting the schema right is exactly where implementation mistakes happen.
The pattern triggers fail-closed; in practice fail-closed systems sometimes need fail-open paths for non-critical inputs, which the pattern doesn't support.

InputGuard.family_discussion: Safety-primitive paired with OutputGuard (the output counterpart), FailClosed (the violation response), and Schema (the validation target). Compare with Validate — Validate is a general pattern; InputGuard is specifically the boundary-defense specialization. Both are 'check before accept' primitives.

motivation.why_it_exists: Intended decision and actual outcome frequently diverge — via external factors, execution errors, model misspecification, or unforeseen consequences. IntentGap names the analysis: why did reality differ from intent? Without the named primitive, post-mortems reduce to 'it went wrong' without the structured attribution that supports learning.
motivation.removability: Removable in systems that don't do post-hoc learning. Essential in any adaptive system; the pattern provides the framework for calibration and model-refinement. The 'decision quality separate from outcome luck' invariant is the anti-hindsight-bias move.

usage.intended: cognitive analysis of intent-outcome divergence.
usage.future: any "why did reality differ from plan?" diagnostic.
usage.broad_contexts: post-mortem analysis, A/B test result interpretation, policy impact analysis, surgical outcomes review, project retrospectives.
usage.every_context_needs: intended decision/outcome, actual outcome, divergence analysis, causal attribution (external factors / execution error / misspecification / unforeseen).
usage.varies: causal-analysis depth, blame-free vs accountability framing, learning integration.

tensions: Separation of decision from outcome vs integrated learning — the invariant wants them separate; useful learning often integrates decision and outcome.
Causal attribution (invariant: evidence-based) vs narrative coherence — evidence-based attribution is slower and more honest than narrative.
Hindsight Bias (named failure) vs Attribution Error (named failure) — the two are opposite failure modes; the pattern has to navigate between them.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured post-hoc analysis, separation of decision quality from outcome luck, causal attribution discipline.
Gives up: decisiveness of learning. Structured analysis is slower than narrative learning and often reaches less actionable conclusions.
critique: Both named failures (Hindsight Bias, Attribution Error) are the dominant ones in real post-mortems and the pattern doesn't provide structural defenses for either.
Evidence-based attribution is an invariant without operational content — what counts as evidence, how to weigh causes, are caller concerns.
The pattern doesn't specify what to do with the gap once identified — update decision procedure, update outcome expectations, or something else.

IntentGap.family_discussion: Post-hoc analysis primitive paired with HindsightBlock (anti-hindsight discipline), CounterfactualAnchor (pre-commitment), and BeliefTracking (the learning substrate). Compare with IntentOverride — IntentGap is diagnostic; IntentOverride is prescriptive.

motivation.why_it_exists: An artifact can be valid against its schema (external consistency) and still self-contradict. InternalConsistency names the Principle of Non-Contradiction check: no two propositions within the artifact can negate each other. Without it, validation misses internal logical conflicts that downstream reasoning will hit.
motivation.removability: Removable if all consistency is external. For any artifact with multiple interacting claims (design document, reasoning trace, multi-part specification), InternalConsistency is load-bearing. The pattern is specifically the 'check artifact against itself' specialization of Check.

usage.intended: Check for self-contradiction via Non-Contradiction principle.
usage.broad_contexts: contract review (terms don't contradict), policy documents (no internal inconsistencies), scientific-theory coherence, LLM output self-consistency, database-integrity constraints.
usage.every_context_needs: artifact with components, non-contradiction evaluation, distinction from external validation.
usage.varies: evaluation-depth (sentence-level vs paragraph vs document), semantic vs syntactic contradiction.

tensions: Non-Contradiction (invariant) vs productive tension — some artifacts legitimately hold contradictions (dialectical reasoning, 'both A and not-A' in different contexts); the invariant forbids them.
Completeness invariant (visit all nodes) vs partial artifacts — some artifacts are legitimately incomplete in progress; the invariant treats incompleteness as failure.
Logical negation vs practical contradiction — strict logical negation is rare; 'approximately inconsistent' is common and the pattern has no gradation.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit internal contradiction detection, Non-Contradiction discipline as named invariant.
Gives up: dialectical tolerance. Some valuable reasoning holds contradictions deliberately; the pattern can't distinguish productive from destructive contradiction.
critique: No failure modes listed; InternalConsistency has many (strict logical check missing semantic contradiction, completeness check missing structural gaps).
Detecting contradiction in natural-language artifacts is AI-hard; the pattern assumes it's a check, which requires the hard work to have been done elsewhere.
The distinction from external Validate is clean conceptually and often blurred in implementation — consistency checks often require schema/type information.

InternalConsistency.family_discussion: Verification primitive paired with Validate (external consistency), Check (the general verification verb), and NonContradiction (the philosophical principle). Compare with Coherence — InternalConsistency is strict logical; Coherence is looser 'fits together.'

motivation.why_it_exists: Raw signal has no meaning until interpreted in context. Interpret names the cognitive act of applying semantic context to extract value — distinct from Translate (which changes form). Without the named primitive, 'understanding' a signal gets conflated with 'receiving' it, hiding the interpretive step that adds or obscures meaning.
motivation.removability: Non-removable as a cognitive distinction. Every agent that acts on data is interpreting. The pattern's value is in the explicit 'meaning depends on context' invariant, which forces callers to track what context was applied.

usage.intended: apply semantic context to raw signal to extract value — change abstraction level, not form.
usage.broad_contexts: LLM input processing, legal-text interpretation, scientific-data interpretation, musical interpretation, historical interpretation, medical imaging interpretation.
usage.every_context_needs: semantic context, raw input, value extraction, distinction from Translate (which preserves form/changes format) and Summarize (which loses info).
usage.varies: context richness, interpretation depth, confidence tracking.

tensions: Context Dependency (invariant) vs stable meanings — the invariant says meaning is context-relative; this makes shared understanding difficult.
Non-Destructive (invariant: original signal preserved) vs efficient storage — preserving originals alongside interpretations doubles the storage.
Syntax-to-semantics move vs simplicity — Interpret claims to change abstraction level; in practice this is a subtle shift often indistinguishable from Translate.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit semantic context tracking, preservation of original signal, distinction from Translate.
Gives up: fluency. Every interpretation that's made explicit adds ceremony; most agents interpret without flagging the context they used.
critique: Very thin — two invariants, a one-line distinction from Translate. The real work of interpretation is in the specific semantic layers, which the pattern doesn't provide.
The Translate/Interpret boundary is conceptually clean and operationally fuzzy — translating requires some interpretation, interpreting requires some translation.
No failure modes listed; Interpret has many (mis-interpretation, context drift, interpretive bias).

Interpret.family_discussion: Cognitive primitive paired with Translate (syntactic change), Understand (the outcome), and Context (the substrate). Compare with FrameSpec — FrameSpec is the interpretation of a request into a contract; Interpret is the general primitive FrameSpec specializes.

motivation.why_it_exists: Agents with complex internal state shouldn't process every incoming message — some should be rejected at the boundary.
