usage.broad_contexts: Exploration vs Exploitation mode, work mode vs rest mode, emergency mode, cognitive modes (System 1 vs 2), personality modes in LLMs.
usage.every_context_needs: stable-configuration semantic, distinction from frequently-changing State, behavior modification.
usage.varies: mode count, transition semantics (triggered vs manual), persistence across sessions.

tensions: Stability invariant vs responsiveness — Modes persist until transition, which prevents flapping and risks staying in the wrong mode too long.
Exclusivity invariant vs hybrid stances — the pattern allows explicit hybrids; the invariant structurally discourages them.
Mode Persistence Failure (named failure) — agent drifts out of the declared mode without transition event; invariant asserts but can't enforce.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit stance tracking, principled transition events, clean separation from ordinary state.
Gives up: flexibility. Mode is heavier than a state variable; for simple stance changes it's overkill.
critique: Mode Confusion (named failure: mixes behaviors from conflicting modes) is endemic and the pattern has no real enforcement.
The 'explicit transition event' requirement is only as strong as the caller's discipline; silent mode changes happen.
No specified protocol for mode-transition commitment (atomic, with compensation if transition fails).

Mode.family_discussion: Foundational stance-pattern paired with State (transient), Context (scope), and Role (responsibility). Used by ContextSwitch (mode push/pop), ExploreExploit (exploration vs exploitation modes), and IdentityHandshake (service vs coordination modes).

motivation.why_it_exists: Assertions of universal semantic identity ('these mean the same thing') are philosophically strong and operationally brittle. ModestClaim names the reframe: assert local divergence detectability (Hash(A) ≠ Hash(B) means different), not universal truth. This is the epistemic stance underlying sema's content-addressed vocabulary.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for sema's design philosophy. The pattern is the stance that licenses the whole content-addressed-vocabulary architecture — detect divergence pragmatically, don't claim universal meaning. Removing it would undermine the paper's framing.

usage.intended: epistemic reframe from Universal Truth to Local Observation ("Divergence ≠ Identity").
usage.future: any "I'm not saying always true, just here, now" claim-scoping discipline.
usage.broad_contexts: scientific paper limitations sections, disclaimer practice, epistemic humility teachings, ML model caveats, honest journalism.
usage.every_context_needs: scope reduction from Universal to Local, divergence-detection semantic instead of identity-claim, epistemic calibration.
usage.varies: scope size (narrow Local, broad Regional), uncertainty quantification, confidence bounds.

tensions: Evidence of Divergence (what the hash proves) vs Proof of Meaning (what the hash doesn't) — the pattern asserts the former and explicitly disclaims the latter.
Pragmatic Grounding (coordination utility, not truth) vs ambition — modest claims produce modest returns; occasionally the field wants universal semantic guarantees.
Brittle Authority (named failure) — making absolute claims that invite refutation — is exactly what the pattern refuses, which requires modesty about every assertion.
tradeoffs: Gains: philosophically defensible content-addressing semantics, explicit modest epistemic stance, pragmatic coordination utility.
Gives up: rhetorical strength. Modest claims are harder to market than strong ones; the pattern accepts this cost.
critique: Ontological Trap (named failure) — claiming the hash solves Symbol Grounding — is the over-reach the pattern is built to prevent. Even so, evangelists routinely slip into this trap.
The stance is philosophically defensible and sometimes operationally frustrating — downstream reasoners want 'this means X,' and ModestClaim gives only 'this isn't different from X.'
Coordination Utility as the success measure is correct and hard to measure; 'is the coordination working' is itself judgment.

ModestClaim.family_discussion: Epistemic-stance primitive paired with ConceptAnchor (what hashing addresses), Hash (the detection mechanism), and Coordination (the success measure). Foundational to sema's philosophy. Compare with LivedProof — both are epistemic stances; ModestClaim is about what to claim, LivedProof is about how to claim it.

motivation.why_it_exists: Systems need continuous observation to detect deviation from baseline. Monitor names the persistent-loop-plus-observation primitive. Without it, observation is ad-hoc and gaps appear exactly when something is going wrong.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for any serious operational system. Every alerting, logging, and anomaly-detection system is built on Monitor or equivalent. The Non-Interference invariant is what distinguishes healthy Monitor from an observation that changes what it observes.

usage.intended: continuous observation loop comparing state against baseline, emit signal on deviation.
usage.broad_contexts: infrastructure monitoring, health monitoring, anomaly detection, vigilance patterns, quality assurance monitoring, compliance monitoring.
usage.every_context_needs: target, observation loop, baseline, deviation detection, signal emission on anomaly.
usage.varies: interval (Duration, per §3.17 — no arbitrary range), baseline adaptation, threshold, signal routing.

tensions: Liveness vs cost — continuous or periodic observation costs compute; sparser monitoring saves compute and misses transient events.
Non-Interference invariant vs thorough observation — deep introspection often perturbs; the invariant forbids significant perturbation without specifying 'significant.'
Baseline definition vs drift — Monitor needs a reference; the reference itself drifts, and the pattern doesn't own the drift-management.
tradeoffs: Gains: continuous observation, structured comparison-to-baseline, clean interface for alerting systems.
Gives up: instantaneous detection of very fast events. Monitor operates at its sampling interval; events faster than that slip through.
critique: No failure modes listed; Monitor has many (observer effects, sampling aliasing, alert fatigue).
Non-Interference is aspirational and domain-specific; detailed monitoring always has some effect.
Very thin — two invariants, observation loop. The interesting work (metric selection, threshold tuning, alert routing) lives outside.

Monitor.family_discussion: Foundational operational primitive paired with Observe (the verb), Loop (the control flow), and Metric (the comparison target). Compare with DriftWatch — Monitor is general observation; DriftWatch is specific baseline-deviation detection.

motivation.why_it_exists: Monitor needs an output artifact — MonitorReport names the telemetry comparing deployed state to Definition of Done. Closes the feedback loop.
motivation.removability: Removable by folding into Report. The specific Monitor-focused variant earns its weight.

usage.intended: telemetry artifact comparing deployed state against Definition of Done.
usage.broad_contexts: SLO reports, deployment health reports, A/B test result reports, ML-model-drift reports, production incident reports.
usage.every_context_needs: deployed state snapshot, Definition-of-Done reference, comparison, feedback-loop closure.
usage.varies: report frequency, alerting thresholds, routing, audit retention.

tensions: Completeness vs size.
Comparison basis (Definition of Done) vs evolving definitions.
Report format — structured vs prose.
tradeoffs: Gains: telemetry artifact.
Gives up: little.
critique: Very thin, one-sentence mechanism.
No invariants, no failure modes.
Distinction from general Report is subtle.

MonitorReport.family_discussion: Output primitive of Monitor, paired with RolloutWatch and AuditTrail.

motivation.why_it_exists: Distributed consensus is hard; MonotonicCounter provides a cheap partial substitute: a value that can only increase. Any node seeing a higher value knows it's newer. Without the constraint, distributed values have no built-in ordering and consensus has no easy partial substitute.
motivation.removability: Removable in strongly-consistent systems. Essential in eventual-consistency / CRDT-style systems, where monotonicity provides order without needing full consensus. The Merge Rule (max) is the CRDT discipline.

usage.intended: strictly increasing value for coordination simplification.
usage.broad_contexts: Lamport clocks, vector clocks, version numbers, CRDTs, sequence IDs, balance ledgers (monotonic deposits), consensus view numbers.
usage.every_context_needs: only-increase guarantee. That's it — every other property is a specialization.
usage.varies: increment step, distributed coordination method, rollover semantics, ceiling, merge function.

tensions: Monotonicity vs resetability — true monotonic counters can never reset, even for legitimate restarts; workarounds (versioned counters) leak the constraint.
Growth invariant vs overflow — the named failure mode: finite integer space eventually exhausts; truly-unbounded growth needs bignum storage.
Merge rule (max) vs richer merges — monotonic counters merge trivially via max; richer conflict-free types need more complex merges.
tradeoffs: Gains: cheap distributed ordering, trivial merge via max, CRDT-compatible semantics.
Gives up: expressiveness. Monotonic counters are one kind of CRDT; more complex data types need more complex conflict resolution.
critique: Counter overflow (named failure) is eventual; the pattern doesn't prescribe a response strategy.
Reset semantics are undefined; legitimate restart scenarios require workarounds not in the pattern.
The simple max-merge works only for specific types (scalars, versions); generalization to structured data requires more primitives.

MonotonicCounter.family_discussion: Distributed-coordination primitive paired with Version, CRDT concepts, and Consensus (the fuller primitive it substitutes for). Compare with Clock — MonotonicCounter is a value; Clock is a time primitive. Both are monotonic, on different semantic axes.

motivation.why_it_exists: The K=1 specialization of Lock with operational machinery the parent leaves abstract — fencing tokens for revocation, sequence numbers for transfer, priority queues for starvation prevention. Mutex is the pattern callers actually invoke; Lock is the abstract anchor it inherits from.
motivation.removability: Yes, in theory — could be expressed as `Lock(K=1)` if Lock carried K as a parameter. In practice the fencing/sequence/queue machinery is enough additional structure that a named specialization reads more naturally than a parameterized parent. The library chose the named-specialization path.

usage.intended: exclusive-access token with lifecycle (ACQUIRE → GRANT/QUEUE → HOLD → RELEASE/YIELD).
usage.future: any single-holder-at-a-time primitive with explicit token.
usage.broad_contexts: OS mutexes, distributed locks with tokens, hardware locks, leadership tokens in distributed systems, single-writer-principle enforcement.
usage.every_context_needs: lifecycle, token representation, priority queue for contention, fencing tokens for revocation.
usage.varies: token material, queue discipline, fencing implementation, reentrancy support.
notes: §3.3 adds `derived_from Lock` to Mutex. Broad-use test confirms Mutex as a specialized Lock (adds token+fencing semantics). Correct relationship.

tensions: Fencing-token requirement vs trust assumption: fencing tokens solve split-brain only if downstream storage honors the token check. Many real storage systems don't — the pattern assumes a cooperating substrate.

Priority queue vs simple FIFO: the pattern mandates a priority queue to prevent starvation, but priority is a caller concern (which priority function?). Mutex defines the structure without defining the policy.

Conservation-of-totem invariant vs distributed operation: 'uniqueness of the fencing totem' is provable locally but requires coordination in distributed settings — a regeneration protocol exists but adds another failure surface.
tradeoffs: Fencing + sequence + queue buys robustness at the cost of a heavier protocol than a bare Lock — every acquire pays the token overhead.
Heartbeat + expires_at buys crash recovery (orphan token detection) at the cost of false preemption when the network is slow but the holder is alive.
The explicit failure-mode catalog buys operator clarity at the cost of pattern complexity — Mutex enumerates six mitigations rather than stating the clean core.
critique: The invariants list has only one item ('Uniqueness, conservation of the fencing totem'). For a pattern this operational, richer invariants are warranted: Monotonic Sequence, Single-Holder, Release-Ownership (only the current holder can release), Token Validity.

The 'critical section' concept is named but not specified — callers must already know what a critical section is. A minimal spec of 'the protected region is the code path between acquire and release' would ground the term.

Failure modes restructured — the previous list contained a nested "Failure modes:" sub-list header with numbered items spread across separate entries. Now rendered as atomic items with inline mitigations.

Mutex.family_discussion: `derived_from Lock` — the K=1 specialization with fencing and token mechanics. Sibling to `Semaphore` (K>1 counting), `ReadWriteLock` (shared/exclusive), `DistributedLock` (lease-based). Paired with `Backoff` and `Cooldown` at the contention-behavior layer.

motivation.why_this_layer: substrate information measure of shared entropy between variables
motivation.why_it_exists: The formal measure of 'how much does knowing one variable reduce uncertainty about another' — substrate for every pattern reasoning about correlation, dependence, feature relevance, or channel capacity. Shannon's I(X;Y) is specific and non-negotiable; having a pattern that pins it means downstream patterns can invoke the exact formulation without restating.
motivation.removability: Marginal. Information theory is mature enough that callers could cite Shannon directly. But having a pinned pattern lets library dependents (e.g., relevance-scoring, feature-selection, channel-allocation patterns) compose against a shared definition with known invariants.

tensions: Formal definition vs finite-sample estimates: I(X;Y) is defined in terms of true distributions, which are never known. In practice it's estimated — the estimates can be substantially off. The pattern is about the substrate; estimation lives separately.

Non-negativity invariant vs finite-sample reality: finite-sample MI estimators are often biased upward; 'non-negative' is trivially true but the estimate may be biased enough to signal correlation where none exists.
Zero iff independent is a theoretical property that doesn't hold empirically — you can have small MI with genuinely dependent variables given finite data.
tradeoffs: Precise information-theoretic definition buys rigorous foundations at the cost of being harder to compute than cosine similarity or correlation.
Symmetry invariant buys interpretability (MI is not directional) at the cost of excluding directional dependence measures like KL divergence.
Non-negativity is trivial but uninformative — the pattern has no 'characteristic scale' to compare against, so 'MI = 0.3' is hard to interpret without further context.
critique: No failure modes. Missing: Finite-Sample Bias (estimator bias for small N), Discretization Error (continuous distributions discretized for estimation), Non-Identifiability (MI is invariant under invertible transformations — X vs f(X) have the same MI for any bijection f).
The mechanism uses the formula I(X; Y) = H(X) + H(Y) − H(X, Y) which is correct but doesn't define H (entropy). Readers need to jump to Entropy to understand MI.
Substrate placement defensible but the ENTIRELY EMPIRICAL domain (computed from data) is a cognitive activity — the substrate is the information relationship, the measurement is Mind.

MutualInformation.family_discussion: Information-theoretic substrate for dependence. Paired with `Entropy` (its building block) and `Measurement` (the process that acquires it from data). Invoked by feature-selection, dimensionality-reduction, and relevance-scoring patterns across Mind.

motivation.why_it_exists: Agents must classify counterparties by substrate — Biological, Synthetic, Institutional — because alignment obligations, rights, and protocols depend on it. Nature names this immutable substrate classification. Without it, all counterparties get the same treatment, which is wrong for most mixed-population scenarios.
motivation.removability: Removable in single-substrate environments. Essential in mixed populations where appropriate treatment differs. Nature is immutable by design (you don't switch substrate); Role is what you do, Identity is who you are, Nature is what you are.

usage.intended: substrate classification of an entity (Biological/Synthetic/Institutional).
usage.future: any "what kind of thing is this?" ontological-origin field.
usage.broad_contexts: Deep(Nature) per paper (signature target), AI-vs-human identification, Biological-vs-Synthetic agent distinction, entity categorization in legal/regulatory systems.
usage.every_context_needs: entity under classification, category set, immutability, alignment-obligation/rights/authentication derivation.
usage.varies: category count, evidence required for classification, dispute resolution.
notes: §3.18 (after Gemini Round 4) keeps Nature as canonical Noun per paper Table 1. Broad-use confirms rich usage.

tensions: Immutable classification vs evolving substrates — the clean 2026 trichotomy (Bio/Synth/Inst) may not survive new categories (augmented, collective, emergent).
Discrete nature vs graded — some entities are partially one and partially another; the classification is binary.
Substrate-dependent treatment vs egalitarianism — the pattern enshrines differential treatment; some ethical frameworks object.
tradeoffs: Gains: substrate-aware protocol selection, clear rights/obligations anchor, explicit immutable classification.
Gives up: universal treatment. Nature specifically licenses different treatment; callers committed to universalism can't use it.
critique: Very thin mechanism — one sentence, no invariants, no failure modes.
The Bio/Synth/Inst trichotomy is under-justified — why these three, why not more or fewer?
No handling of edge cases (augmented humans, corporate personhood, AI with institutional roles).

Nature.family_discussion: Foundational classifier paired with Identity (persistent handle), Role (what you do), and IdentityHandshake (which uses Nature for mode routing). Compare with Substrate — Nature is the classification; Substrate is the material.

motivation.why_it_exists: Proving non-membership is hard — 'we don't have X' is typically weaker than 'we have Y.' NegativeProof names the cryptographic mechanism: commit to full state via Merkle tree, use zero-knowledge to prove absence. Without the pattern, absence claims are trust-based.
motivation.removability: Removable in settings without cryptographic commitment needs. Essential in privacy-preserving verification (did this transaction happen? no). The pattern's power depends on committing to exhaustive state; partial commitments defeat it.

usage.intended: prove non-membership in a committed state set via ZK proof.
usage.broad_contexts: Merkle-tree non-inclusion proofs, privacy-preserving queries, "not on any sanctions list" attestations, absence-of-evidence proofs, blockchain state queries.
usage.every_context_needs: committed state set, specific value to check absence of, ZK proof mechanism.
usage.varies: commitment scheme (Merkle, Verkle, KZG, etc.), ZK proof system, domain size, proof size.

tensions: Commitment completeness vs hiding — the pattern works only if the commitment covers everything; agents can hide data outside the committed tree (named failure).
Computational expense (named failure) vs proof value — expensive proofs deter use, making absence claims rare even when warranted.
Stale commitment — state changes between commitment and proof, and the pattern doesn't own freshness.
tradeoffs: Gains: cryptographic absence proofs, zero-knowledge privacy, principled exhaustive search within commitment.
Gives up: simplicity. Most absence claims aren't worth the cryptographic ceremony; the pattern is for specific high-stakes use.
critique: Incomplete state commitment is the dominant attack — prove absence of X by not committing to the set that contains X.
Staleness is real; between commit and prove, state can change.
The pattern's computational expense limits use to scenarios that truly warrant the cost.

NegativeProof.family_discussion: Cryptographic-proof primitive paired with MerkleTree (the substrate), ZeroKnowledgeProof (the privacy mechanism), and AdversarialProof (cognitive counterpart). Compare with AdversarialProof — AdversarialProof is hostile-search-based; NegativeProof is crypto-commitment-based. Different absence-proof strategies.

motivation.why_this_layer: irrelevant information exists whether or not anyone designs it
motivation.why_it_exists: Every signal carries irrelevant information. Noise names the irrelevant portion — information that obscures the datum and increases cognitive load. Without the named primitive, agents don't have a handle for 'this is content I should filter out.'
motivation.removability: Very thin — nearly a stub. The value is purely classificatory: 'this is noise, not signal.' Remove the pattern and every filter has to distinguish signal from noise without a shared vocabulary.

usage.intended: information irrelevant to current task — obscures Datum and increases extraction cost.
usage.broad_contexts: audio noise, signal-processing noise, data noise, cognitive distraction, communication interference, adversarial noise injection (security).
usage.every_context_needs: context defining what's relevant (and thus what's noise), interference semantic.
usage.varies: noise model (Gaussian, structured, adversarial), filterability, injection vs natural, impact on extraction cost.

tensions: Noise vs signal is task-dependent — what's noise for task A may be signal for task B.
Filtering noise vs lossy compression — aggressive filtering is compression; the pattern doesn't distinguish.
Task-dependent definition vs fixed classification — defining noise requires knowing the task, which the pattern assumes is given.
tradeoffs: Gains: shared vocabulary for 'irrelevant information,' handle for filtering primitives.
Gives up: operational content. Noise is a stance; specific patterns that filter noise do the actual work.
critique: Almost a stub — one sentence of mechanism, no invariants, no failure modes.
Task-dependency of noise is important and unmentioned in the mechanism.
Conflates random noise with structured-but-irrelevant information; they have different handling strategies.

Noise.family_discussion: Foundational-info primitive paired with Signal (the counterpart), Filter (the removal operation), and Dampen (the reduction). Compare with Incongruity — Noise is irrelevant variance, Incongruity is structured mismatch. Different kinds of 'not what was expected.'

motivation.why_it_exists: Agents stuck in repetitive loops or degenerate trajectories need an active shove. NoiseInjection names the recovery: deliberately inject high-temperature noise or random strategy card to force trajectory change. Without it, stuck agents continue stuck until external intervention.
motivation.removability: Removable if agents reliably don't get stuck. In practice LLM agents loop, and NoiseInjection is one of the few self-recovery mechanisms. The signal-to-noise-ratio invariant (>0) is what distinguishes productive injection from pure derailment.

usage.intended: break local optima by deliberate noise injection when agent detects looping.
usage.broad_contexts: ML exploration (epsilon-greedy), simulated annealing, creative writing (forced random words), conversation fresheners, evolutionary mutation, escape from rumination.
usage.every_context_needs: loop/stagnation detector, noise source, injection mechanism, return-to-coherent-trajectory after injection.
usage.varies: noise magnitude (temperature), noise source (PRNG, oblique strategies, user prompt), detection threshold, cooldown after injection.

tensions: Controlled noise vs derailment (the named failure) — too much noise destroys coherence; the pattern walks the edge.
Random strategy card vs task-relevant perturbation — random is cheap and often irrelevant; relevant perturbation is expensive.
Detection of loops vs normal repetition — distinguishing stuck from diligent repetition is itself judgment.
tradeoffs: Gains: self-recovery from loops, explicit trajectory-change mechanism.
Gives up: determinism and sometimes coherence. The cost of occasional derailment is the price of unsticking.
critique: Derailment into nonsense is the named failure and the pattern's central risk.
Loop detection is assumed and not specified — how the agent knows it's looping is the hard part.
Signal-to-noise > 0 is technically satisfied by almost any injection; the invariant is weak.

NoiseInjection.family_discussion: Recovery primitive paired with EntropyPump (the general noise-injection pattern), LatentWander (offline variant), and CreativeBlend (which uses NoiseInjection). Compare with Jester — both inject incongruity; NoiseInjection for recovery, Jester for critique delivery.

motivation.why_it_exists: Descriptive output that smuggles in normative adjectives ('dangerous,' 'unfair') corrupts the is-ought separation the EthicalReasoningProtocol depends on. NormCheck names the filter that catches and strips these. Without it, prediction output contaminates with judgment, and the protocol's architectural boundary leaks.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for systems using EthicalReasoningProtocol. The pattern is specifically the enforcement mechanism for the is-ought boundary; remove it and the boundary becomes aspirational.

usage.intended: detect value-laden normative adjectives masquerading as objective facts.
usage.broad_contexts: journalism bias detection, scientific-writing neutrality checks, legal-writing objectivity filters, LLM output bias detection, policy-analysis tone filters.
usage.every_context_needs: input text, normative-word detection, rewrite to strip biases.
usage.varies: normative-word lexicon, context sensitivity (some adjectives are factual in some contexts), rewrite strictness.

tensions: Fact Preservation (invariant) vs normative stripping — rewriting must preserve causal claims; 'dangerous' has normative weight and factual correlate ('causes harm'), and stripping conflates them.
Count(NormativeAdjectives) == 0 invariant vs hidden normativity — adjectives aren't the only vector; noun choice, framing, and selection all carry normative weight.
Named failure 'strips relevant safety warnings that were actually factual' — the pattern can be over-eager and remove real warnings.
tradeoffs: Gains: structural is-ought boundary enforcement, explicit normative-adjective filter.
Gives up: richness of description. Pure factual output without normative flavor is colder and sometimes less useful.
critique: 'Strips relevant safety warnings' is a real failure — 'this is dangerous' may be exactly the signal a user needs, and NormCheck removes it.
Adjective-level filtering is crude; normativity hides in sentence structure and framing that the pattern doesn't address.
The fact-preservation invariant is a high bar and under-specified — what counts as 'the same causal claim' after rewrite?

NormCheck.family_discussion: Filter primitive paired with PredictionSolver (the output source), EthicalReasoningProtocol (the consuming protocol), and IsOughtBoundary (the concept being enforced). Compare with InvariantFilter — NormCheck filters specific content; InvariantFilter filters by predicate evaluation.

motivation.why_it_exists: Separating prediction (descriptive) from judgment (normative) requires a dedicated normative module. NormativeJudge names it: evaluate world-states against a weighted value function, with weights supplied by the caller so preferences are explicit. Without the pattern, judgment and prediction blur together.
motivation.removability: Removable if prediction and judgment don't need separation. For systems using EthicalReasoningProtocol, NormativeJudge is the required dedicated module for the normative side of the pipeline.

usage.intended: ensemble judge evaluating static world-states against weighted value functions (to mitigate Goodhart's).
usage.future: any "value judgment with Goodhart mitigation" mechanism.
usage.broad_contexts: AI alignment evaluators, ethical-review boards (ensemble of perspectives), judicial panels, multi-stakeholder value assessments, investment committees.
usage.every_context_needs: static world-state input, weighted value function, ensemble of judges with perturbed values, quorum on outcome.
usage.varies: ensemble size, value-perturbation degree, quorum threshold, escalation to human approval.

tensions: Explicit Weights invariant vs implicit preferences — requiring logged trade-offs is honest and labor-intensive.
Outcome Focus (f(state), not f(action)) vs deontological concerns — the invariant favors consequentialism; some value frameworks care about action-type directly.
Goodhart's Law (named failure) — optimizing for the metric, not the intent — is endemic to any weighted-value system.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit normative evaluation, preference transparency via logged weights, clean separation from prediction.
Gives up: richer ethical stances. Consequentialism-shaped evaluation fits some moral frameworks and not others.
critique: Goodhart's Law is the classic failure and the pattern names it without mitigating.
Collusion between Proposer and Judge (named failure) — the caller supplies weights, so the system can be gamed; mitigation is outside the pattern.
Outcome Focus rules out action-type evaluation; some systems want both.

NormativeJudge.family_discussion: Normative module paired with PredictionSolver (the descriptive counterpart), Value (the axis), and EthicalReasoningProtocol (the consuming pipeline). Compare with Judge — NormativeJudge is specifically value-weighted; Judge is generic scalar evaluation.

motivation.why_it_exists: Distinguishing genuinely new from rebranded is the core challenge for any vocabulary that cares about quality. Novelty names the structural-distinctness judge: low embedding similarity to nearest neighbor is required for high novelty. Without the pattern, rebrands and renames pass as novel contributions.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for serious ontology construction. Sema's Living Taxonomy depends on not admitting renames; Novelty is the check. Remove it and the vocabulary accumulates synonyms, bloating discovery.

usage.intended: Judge-as-structural-distinctness — 3-class classification (Derivative / Marginal / Distinct).
usage.broad_contexts: PURECheck's N dimension, academic originality checks, patent novelty screening, pattern-library novelty, product-originality evaluation.
usage.every_context_needs: candidate, incumbent knowledge base, structural-distinctness evaluation, 3-class judgment.
usage.varies: distinctness metric, knowledge-base coverage, domain specificity.

tensions: Embedding similarity vs semantic distinctness — low embedding similarity is a proxy; real semantic novelty is more subtle.
Orthogonality invariant vs incremental progress — most real innovation is incremental; requiring high novelty against nearest neighbor rejects incremental work.
Defined against a reference knowledge base — different references yield different novelty judgments; the pattern doesn't specify the reference.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit distinctness check, defense against rebrands, structural novelty requirement.
Gives up: incremental refinements. The invariant may reject valuable small improvements; callers wanting refinement need different patterns.
critique: Embedding similarity is model-dependent — different embedding models give different novelty scores; the invariant inherits the model's biases.
No threshold specified — 'low embedding similarity' defers the cutoff to the caller.
The pattern assumes neighbors exist to compare against; for the first pattern in a brand-new domain, Novelty has no nearest neighbor.

Novelty.family_discussion: PURE-gate element for the Unique dimension. Paired with Expansive (transfer judge), Parsimonious (simplicity judge), Realizable (coherence judge). Used by DecompositionGate. Compare with Originality — same concept, different framing.

motivation.why_this_layer: emergent working groups from activity density
motivation.why_it_exists: Distributed coordination can emerge without central orchestration via stigmergy — agents deposit traces, sites supersaturate, coordination crystallizes. Nucleate names this indirect-coordination primitive. Without it, distributed emergence has no named mechanism.
motivation.removability: Removable in centrally-orchestrated systems. Essential in ant-colony-style distributed emergence. The Conservation of Mass invariant (nucleation doesn't create agents, aggregates existing density) is the crucial discipline.

usage.intended: emergent working groups from activity-density crossing a threshold.
usage.future: any "group forms when density sufficient" mechanism.
usage.broad_contexts: ant-colony trail formation, community-formation around hashtags, research-cluster formation, market-formation, gang formation, emergent teams in open-source projects.
usage.every_context_needs: trace density tracking, density threshold, nucleation trigger, bond/join protocol.
usage.varies: density metric, threshold calibration, nucleation broadcast radius, bond semantics.

tensions: Threshold miscalibration — too low = constant overhead, too high = never crystallizes (both named failures).
Critical Mass invariant vs small-group effectiveness — some coordinations work with small N; the threshold may exclude them.
Zombie crystals (named failure) — anchor disappears but crystal persists; mitigation is outside the pattern's invariants.
tradeoffs: Gains: emergent coordination without central orchestration, explicit trace-density mechanism.
Gives up: determinism. Stigmergic coordination produces emergent outcomes that resist prediction.
critique: Threshold calibration is the dominant operational challenge and the pattern has no default or guidance.
Zombie crystals are acknowledged with heartbeat-based mitigation mentioned as external.
The biological metaphor (nucleation, supersaturation) is evocative and loads the pattern with assumptions that may not fit all domains.

Nucleate.family_discussion: Emergence primitive paired with Stigmergy (the substrate), Trace (the communication unit), and Crystallize (the phase transition). Compare with Rally — Nucleate is indirect; Rally is direct group mobilization.

motivation.why_it_exists: OODA (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act) is the canonical fast-decision loop from military doctrine. Naming it gives agent systems a referent for 'high-speed decision cycle favoring agility over power.' Without the pattern, decision cycles are ad-hoc and often skip Orient, collapsing to reactionary Observe-Act.
motivation.removability: Removable — agents can reinvent the loop. The named pattern earns weight for the specific agility framing and the 'Orient Dominance' invariant. Remove it and the orient phase becomes optional, which is exactly the pathology OODA was meant to prevent.

usage.intended: fast-loop decision cycle favoring agility.
usage.broad_contexts: combat aviation (origin), trading, alert response, debugging sessions, real-time control, agentic reasoning loops, competitive games, operations war rooms.
usage.every_context_needs: the four phases (Observe, Orient, Decide, Act) executed in order.
usage.varies: phase duration, orientation depth, decision method, action reversibility, loop interrupt criteria, cycle-time budget.

tensions: Orient Dominance (invariant) vs speed — proper orientation before deciding slows the loop.
Disorientation (named failure) — getting stuck in Orient with contradictory data — is real; the pattern has no escape hatch.
Reactionary Loop (named failure) — skipping Decide, just Observe-Act — is the classic OODA violation.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured agility loop, explicit phases, named failure-mode vocabulary.
Gives up: slowness when warranted. OODA favors fast iteration; deliberate reasoning benefits from other patterns.
critique: Military heritage brings specific framing that not all agent tasks fit — OODA is adversarial-tinged.
Disorientation under contradictory data is a real failure and the pattern offers no specific remedy.
Latency of the full loop is the named failure when environment changes faster than the loop cycles.

OODA.family_discussion: Decision-cycle paired with Loop (control flow), Observe (the gathering step), and Orient (the contextualization). Compare with ReAct — both are cyclic decision patterns; OODA is military-origin agility-focused; ReAct is LLM-origin reasoning-acting.

motivation.why_this_layer: cryptographic self-binding to a ruleset — one agent commits; enforcement is code/substrate, not another agent
motivation.why_it_exists: Self-enforcing commitments require cryptographic binding to a rule set. OathBind names this: actor commits, deviation triggers automatic penalty via SpotAudit. Without the pattern, commitments rely on external enforcement which may be absent or slow.
motivation.removability: Removable when external enforcement exists. Essential for trustless self-enforcement in decentralized systems. The Automated Justice invariant — penalty depends solely on cryptographic evidence — is the pattern's structural guarantee.

usage.intended: automated binding with cryptographic pre-commitment to penalty-enforced rules.
usage.broad_contexts: smart contracts with slashing, security deposits, bail bonds, performance bonds, cryptoeconomic penalty systems, automated compliance enforcement.
usage.every_context_needs: rule set (the oath), cryptographic commitment, penalty specification, audit mechanism for violations.
usage.varies: penalty type (slashing, reputation, access revocation), audit frequency, dispute process, multi-party binding.

tensions: Automated Justice vs context sensitivity — cryptographic evidence is narrow; real deviations often require context to judge fairly.
Immutability of rules vs legitimate evolution — rules frozen at signing can't adapt; agents stuck with outdated commitments.
Penalty severity decoupled from deviation severity (named failure) — a small slip triggering a large penalty.
tradeoffs: Gains: self-enforcing commitment, trustless deviation response, cryptographic evidence chain.
Gives up: contextual judgment. Automated penalties apply regardless of mitigating circumstances.
critique: Rule-set ambiguity (named failure) — unclear rules produce unintended penalties; the pattern offers no disambiguation.
Decoupling penalty from severity is a real failure; the pattern requires explicit graduated penalties that callers often skip.
Immutability is a strong invariant that makes the pattern inflexible in long-lived deployments.

OathBind.family_discussion: Self-enforcement primitive used by CommitmentDevice, Constitution, and SpotAudit. Compare with Sign — OathBind is commitment-with-penalty; Sign is attestation-without-penalty. Both are cryptographic commitments at different severity levels.

motivation.why_it_exists: Gathering information from the environment is the input side of any agent loop. Observe names the active process: sense, filter for relevance, integrate into context. Without it, 'input' conflates raw reception with structured observation.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every agent loop has an observation phase; the named pattern provides the Read-Only and Truthfulness invariants that distinguish proper observation from accidental side effects or distortion.

usage.intended: active state perception from environment.
usage.broad_contexts: API polling, file reads, sensor queries, user input reception, log tail reads, event subscriptions, probes, LLM introspection.
usage.every_context_needs: source (what to observe), filtering (attention), integration into context.
usage.varies: polling interval, filter strictness, caching, async vs sync, authentication.

tensions: Read-Only (invariant) vs active probing — some observation requires interaction (probes, queries); the invariant allows it but the semantics are ambiguous.
Truthfulness invariant vs inferential reading — agents often observe what they expect rather than what's there (perceptual bias).
Attention filtering vs completeness — filtering is needed to avoid overload; filtering decides what matters, which biases observation.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit observation semantics, side-effect-free invariant, truthfulness discipline.
Gives up: purity. Real observation always has some side effects (sensor heat, observer presence), which the invariant tolerates in spirit only.
critique: Blind Spot (named failure) — critical information outside observable range — is structural; the pattern can't fix it.
Information Overload (named failure) — too much data defeats filtering; no specified response strategy.
Sensor Noise is named without a noise-handling mechanism; it's treated as a problem to mention, not solve.

Observe.family_discussion: Foundational input primitive in OODA and many agent loops. Paired with Context (the integration target), Attention (the filter), and Datum (the raw unit). Compare with Monitor — Observe is single-shot, Monitor is continuous. Different temporal profiles.

motivation.why_it_exists: When data defies classification, agents either force-fit or discard. OntologyAdapt names the Piagetian accommodation move: restructure the ontology to fit the anomaly, don't discard. Without the pattern, ontologies either rot (too rigid) or explode (too permissive).
motivation.removability: Removable in static ontologies. Essential for adaptive systems that learn from data. The Conservation of Data invariant (no anomaly discarded) is the accommodation discipline.

usage.intended: restructure categorical framework when data defies current ontology (Piagetian accommodation).
usage.broad_contexts: ML concept drift handling, scientific paradigm shift modeling, scheme accommodation in pedagogy, semantic drift in language models, category-system overhaul.
usage.every_context_needs: trigger detection (defying classification), restructure event, new-root-category creation.
usage.varies: restructure aggressiveness (local vs global), rollback policy if restructure fails, migration semantics for existing data.

tensions: Category explosion (named failure) — creating new category per noise — is the over-accommodation failure.
Fit Threshold (0.4) vs noise tolerance — too strict triggers unnecessary restructure; too lax misses real shifts.
Accommodation vs assimilation — Piagetian distinction; the pattern is about accommodation (restructure) not assimilation (force-fit).
tradeoffs: Gains: adaptive ontology, accommodation-over-discard discipline, explicit fit threshold.
Gives up: ontology stability. OntologyAdapt specifically allows change; downstream callers must handle the instability.
critique: Category explosion is the failure mode and the pattern's main risk; restructuring too often produces noisy taxonomies.
Fit Threshold 0.4 is a default that depends on domain; caller tuning is required.
Conservation of Data conflicts with pruning; no specified reconciliation.

OntologyAdapt.family_discussion: Adaptive-ontology primitive paired with Ontology (the substrate), RegimeSense (the trigger), and OntologicalAccommodation (the response). Compare with OntologyHandshake — OntologyAdapt is internal restructuring; OntologyHandshake is cross-ontology mapping.

motivation.why_it_exists: Agents with different internal ontologies can't share data meaningfully until they map their terms. OntologyHandshake names the negotiation: exchange definition hashes, negotiate mapping if mismatched, build temporary shared dictionary. Without it, cross-ontology data transfer is lossy and error-prone.
motivation.removability: Removable in single-ontology environments. Essential in heterogeneous multi-agent systems where different training regimes produce different ontologies. The pattern imports sema's content-addressed hashing into the handshake protocol.

usage.intended: negotiate shared definitions before data exchange.
usage.broad_contexts: cross-system data integration, human-human jargon alignment, multi-language translation setup, pidgin-protocol creation, cross-organizational knowledge integration.
usage.every_context_needs: definition-hash exchange, mismatch detection (CompatibilityCheck), negotiation phase, temporary shared dictionary.
usage.varies: dictionary scope, persistence (per-session vs lasting), negotiation protocol (iterative vs single-shot), fallback on irreconcilable divergence.

tensions: Convergence on mapping vs negotiation overhead — complex ontologies take long to map; simple coordination stalls on the ceremony.
Bijectivity invariant vs legitimate non-bijective mappings — real ontologies often have many-to-one or one-to-many correspondences.
Term Consistency invariant vs local meanings — enforcing consistency across ontologies can distort concepts that don't cleanly translate.
tradeoffs: Gains: principled cross-ontology communication, content-addressed term identity, explicit negotiation phase.
Gives up: speed. Every cross-ontology interaction pays the handshake tax; frequent switches compound the cost.
critique: Failure to converge on mapping (named failure) — some ontologies genuinely don't translate, and the pattern's negotiation phase can hang.
High negotiation overhead (named failure) — for complex ontologies, the handshake dominates communication time.
Dictionary mismatch risks semantic errors — temporary shared dictionaries can be wrong; the pattern has no validation step.

OntologyHandshake.family_discussion: Multi-ontology coordination primitive paired with CompatibilityCheck (the hash-mismatch detector), ConceptAnchor (the hashed terms), and Greet (the general handshake). Compare with IdentityHandshake — OntologyHandshake aligns term meanings; IdentityHandshake aligns agent natures.

motivation.why_it_exists: The cost of a choice includes the value of the best alternative you didn't take. OpportunityCost names this economic discipline — ask not just 'is this good?' but 'is this better than what else?' Without it, agents evaluate options in isolation, systematically under-counting the cost of commitment.
motivation.removability: Removable if alternatives don't exist (rare) or if resource constraints don't bind (rare). In practice the pattern is load-bearing for any allocation decision. Remove it and opportunity costs become invisible.

usage.intended: deduct foregone-alternative value from budget calculation.
usage.broad_contexts: investment decisions, time-allocation decisions, product roadmap prioritization, resource-commitment analysis, career choices, scheduling trade-offs.
usage.every_context_needs: candidate option, best-forgone-alternative identification, cost calculation including foregone-value deduction.
usage.varies: alternative-space size, evaluation technique, uncertainty tracking in forgone value.

tensions: Best forgone alternative invariant vs unknown alternatives — you can only count alternatives you thought of; the pattern's accuracy depends on alternative-generation quality.
Analysis Paralysis (named failure) — infinite search for the perfect alternative — is the pattern's pathology.
Finite resources invariant vs growing capabilities — resources grow over time; at any instant they're finite, but the pattern is silent about temporal expansion.
tradeoffs: Gains: true cost accounting, explicit alternative-comparison, defense against 'this is good' in isolation.
Gives up: decisiveness. Serious opportunity-cost thinking can delay choice until the alternatives themselves have lapsed.
critique: Analysis Paralysis is endemic; the pattern has no stopping rule for alternative search.
The pattern assumes alternatives are knowable; in real decisions, many alternatives are unknown at decision time.
Very thin mechanism — two invariants, one-sentence framing.

OpportunityCost.family_discussion: Decision-theory primitive paired with Value (the axis), Budget (the resource), and ExploreExploit (which uses opportunity cost). Compare with EpistemicROI — OpportunityCost is about forgone alternatives; EpistemicROI is about forgone information.

motivation.why_it_exists: Searching forever finds the best answer and costs too much; stopping immediately saves cost and misses the best. OptimalStop names the dynamic stopping rule: 1/e rule if no recall, marginal-gain threshold otherwise. Without it, search duration is ad-hoc.
motivation.removability: Removable when search is short or when budget is the only constraint. Essential for problems where stopping criteria shape the answer quality. The pattern imports classical optimal-stopping theory into agent decision-making.

usage.intended: resource-aware search termination via 1/e rule or Marginal Gain threshold.
usage.broad_contexts: secretary problem, apartment hunting, partner selection, when-to-stop-searching decisions, product-launch timing, optimal-selling-time in markets.
usage.every_context_needs: search-in-progress state, stopping criterion (1/e for no-recall, Marginal Gain for recall), termination decision.
usage.varies: recall_allowed (Boolean, principled per §3.17), budget, cost estimation, quality estimation.

tensions: 1/e rule (no recall) vs marginal-gain rule (recall) — the two rules give different answers; picking the right one requires knowing the recall regime.
Budget Adherence (invariant) vs quality — strict budget cuts off search; quality demands may require exceeding budget.
Empty Handed (named failure) — 1/e rule exhausts all options without beating baseline.
tradeoffs: Gains: principled stopping rule, named regimes for different recall assumptions.
Gives up: simplicity. OptimalStop requires classifying the problem into recall/no-recall and applying different rules; simpler stopping rules work for simpler problems.
critique: Infinite Search (named failure) — unknown N resulted in endless calibration — is a structural risk when the search space size is unknown.
The 1/e rule is famous and applies to a narrow set of problems; many real stopping decisions don't fit.
Marginal gain threshold requires estimating incremental value, which is the hard part and the pattern defers it.

OptimalStop.family_discussion: Decision-theory primitive paired with ExploreExploit, ComputeBudget, and SearchStrategy. Compare with Defer — OptimalStop decides when to stop searching; Defer decides when to wait for more information.

motivation.why_this_layer: parallel-runtime solver via AtomicBid + Actor Model
motivation.why_it_exists: Trades reliability for velocity — atomic plan-and-execute in a single turn, relying on post-hoc reflexion and compensation rather than pre-action verification. In high-throughput multi-agent coordination (Actor Model with mailboxes), the latency of pre-verification is the bottleneck; OptimisticSolver specializes the solver contract for that tradeoff space.
motivation.removability: Conditionally yes. If the library drops the Actor Model deployment path, OptimisticSolver loses its anchoring context. But as long as Actor-Model swarms are a target deployment, a named pattern for 'opt-in velocity over verification' is the right shape. Collapsing into PolymorphicSolver would blur the distinction between 'verify-first' and 'compensate-later' styles.

usage.intended: high-velocity Solver using post-action correction instead of pre-action verification.
usage.future: any solver trading verification-before-act for throughput.
usage.broad_contexts: parallel multi-agent execution, high-throughput processing, speculative execution, eventual-consistency workflows, low-latency coordination, trading systems.
usage.every_context_needs: parallel runtime (Actor Model with Mailboxes), atomic-bid protocol, single-turn plan+execute, `Reflexion` + `Compensate` for correction.
usage.varies: parallelism degree, bid protocol specifics, reflexion depth, compensation strategy.
notes: §3.14's layer retention is confirmed by broad-use — every legitimate context explicitly needs Society-layer coordination primitives (AtomicBid, Actor Model). Relocating to Mind would force either gravity inversion or stripping those deps.

tensions: Velocity vs correctness: the Non-Blocking invariant forbids waiting for Orchestrator approval, but some decisions genuinely require upstream consent. The pattern's answer is that those decisions don't belong on an OptimisticSolver — the caller must choose the right solver for the task.

Atomicity of turn vs composability: BID and TOOL must come out in the same response. That makes composition with slower Solvers awkward — an OptimisticSolver cannot wait on a RigorousSolver's Verify step without breaking its own turn-atomicity.

Society layer placement: OptimisticSolver is in Society/Protocols because it structurally requires the Actor Model (multiple agents in parallel). But its *execution* is single-agent cognition. The layer tracks the deployment assumption, not the mechanism alone.
tradeoffs: Turn atomicity buys throughput on parallel runtimes (Actor Model) at the cost of catastrophic failure on serial runtimes (Serial Deadlock failure mode names this).
Post-hoc compensation via Reflexion and Compensate buys velocity at the cost of error visibility — mistakes survive until reflection reveals them.
Mandatory parallel runtime narrows deployment options — a library user on a single-threaded engine cannot use OptimisticSolver without first switching engines.
critique: Over-Eager Execution is a named failure mode but the pattern offers no mitigation — the spec explicitly chooses velocity over guardrails. That is defensible, but callers should be made aware that the pattern is opinionated rather than neutral.
The AtomicBid coupling is stated as a requirement but the pattern does not say what happens if the runtime lacks AtomicBid support — degradation path is unspecified.

'MANDATES that the agent plan and execute in a single turn' is a prescription on the implementer, but the pattern has no way to enforce it — a two-turn implementer could claim to be OptimisticSolver and pass surface checks.
`derived_from` updated from stale Solver sema_id (10655bd6...) to current (b00a16af...).

OptimisticSolver.family_discussion: The velocity-specialized descendant of `PolymorphicSolver`, paired with `AtomicBid` for turn-atomic multi-agent coordination. Sibling to `RigorousSolver` (the opposite tradeoff: slower, stricter). Composed with `Reflexion` and `Compensate` for post-hoc error recovery.

motivation.why_it_exists: Iteratively improving parameters or structure against an objective is the foundational learning/tuning move. Optimize names it. Without the pattern, improvement loops reduce to 'change things and hope,' without the monotonicity or measurability discipline.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every learning, tuning, and improvement pattern uses Optimize or equivalent. The Measurability invariant (objective must be quantifiable) is the load-bearing discipline — unmeasurable objectives can't be optimized.

usage.intended: iterative parameter/structure adjustment to maximize an objective function.
usage.broad_contexts: gradient descent, hyperparameter tuning, evolutionary algorithms, reinforcement-learning policy optimization, compiler optimization, resource allocation, product-design refinement.
usage.every_context_needs: objective function (metric), candidate generation, evaluation, selection.
usage.varies: local vs global search, gradient availability, convergence criteria, exploration/exploitation balance.

tensions: Monotonicity invariant (each step improves) vs noisy metrics — real optimization landscapes have noise; strict monotonicity requires either noise-free metrics or accepting non-monotonic steps.
Goodhart's Law (named failure) — optimizing the metric destroys the value — is the most common optimization failure.
Local Optima (named failure) — getting stuck — requires escape mechanisms (EntropyPump, LateralOptimization) that live outside Optimize.
tradeoffs: Gains: principled iterative improvement, explicit objective function, named failure-mode vocabulary.
Gives up: simplicity. Optimize requires choosing a metric, which is where Goodhart's Law enters; simpler satisficing avoids the trap.
critique: Overfitting (named failure) — solution works on test, fails in reality — is the classical ML failure, and the pattern mentions without mitigating.
Goodhart's Law is the dominant failure for any real optimization over a non-trivial period.
Local Optima are structural; without escape mechanisms, optimize converges to whatever locally-good answer is near the start.

Optimize.family_discussion: Foundational primitive paired with Metric (the objective), EntropyPump (local-optima escape), and LateralOptimization (creative escape). Compare with Refine — Optimize is quantitative; Refine is qualitative. Both are improvement loops, on different axes.

motivation.why_it_exists: Decision spaces need discrete units. Option names the fully-specified, mutually-exclusive alternative within a decision. Without it, decisions blur between 'things to consider' and 'paths you can take.'
motivation.removability: Very thin. Could be folded into Choice or Alternative, but the mutual-exclusivity requirement distinguishes Option from looser Alternative. Hard to argue against keeping it as a slot.

usage.intended: discrete, actionable alternative within a decision space — mutually exclusive.
usage.future: any "one of several paths" selection unit.
usage.broad_contexts: product selection, policy choices, architectural alternatives, game move options, medical treatment alternatives, financial product choices.
usage.every_context_needs: executable specification, mutual exclusivity with other options in set.
usage.varies: cost/benefit data attached, dependencies among options, reversibility.

tensions: Mutual exclusivity vs overlapping choices — real decisions sometimes have overlapping options that the pattern forbids.
Fully-specified vs explore-options — agents exploring a space have partial options; the pattern requires commitment to full specification.
Discrete vs continuous — Option is atomic; continuous decision spaces need different representations.
tradeoffs: Gains: decision discipline, mutual-exclusivity for clean choice.
Gives up: flexibility. Real decisions often have graded, overlapping, or continuous alternatives.
critique: Almost a stub — one sentence, no failure modes listed.
The mutual-exclusivity requirement is strong; relaxed versions exist in real decision frameworks.
Fully-specified requirement rules out partial-commitment decisions that are often legitimate.

Option.family_discussion: Foundational decision primitive paired with Choice (the act), Decision (the outcome), and Criteria (how to choose). Compare with Alternative — Option is mutually-exclusive; Alternative is looser.

motivation.why_it_exists: On-chain systems and agent coordinations often need off-chain truth — did the event happen, did the price move. Oracle names the trusted injection of this off-chain reality via cryptographic signing. Without the pattern, conditional commitments can't resolve against real-world events.
motivation.removability: Removable in purely on-chain or purely off-chain systems. Essential at the boundary — HeldRelease, prediction markets, outcome verification all depend on Oracle. The Non-Interference invariant (reports, doesn't alter) is the honesty contract.

usage.intended: trusted entity injecting off-chain truth via cryptographic signing.
usage.future: any "bridge external reality into the system" service.
usage.broad_contexts: blockchain oracles (Chainlink, UMA), price feeds, random-number beacons, weather oracles, sports-outcome oracles, regulatory-event oracles.
usage.every_context_needs: trust relationship, cryptographic signing, off-chain → on-chain data bridge.
usage.varies: trust model (single vs decentralized), consensus among multiple oracles, dispute mechanism, freshness guarantee.

tensions: Trusted entity vs decentralized trust — Oracle is a trusted node; the trustlessness goal is undercut by relying on it.
Non-Interference invariant vs active participation — the Oracle reports; agents often want the Oracle to also adjudicate, which would violate non-interference.
Consistency invariant (same query at same time = same answer) vs reality's ambiguity — real events sometimes have multiple valid reports.
tradeoffs: Gains: off-chain truth injection, cryptographically signed data, principled trust boundary.
Gives up: trustlessness. Oracle is a trust anchor; compromising it compromises everything that consumes it.
critique: No failure modes listed — Oracle has many (compromise, bias, bribery, outage).
Centralization pressure — a single Oracle is a single point of failure; decentralized oracles (multi-oracle with voting) are adjacent patterns.
The pattern assumes reality has crisp answers; ambiguous events break the Consistency invariant.

Oracle.family_discussion: Bridge primitive paired with HeldRelease (condition resolver), Sign (the cryptographic backing), and Witness (related attestation). Compare with Prophet — Oracle reports external reality; Prophet predicts from internal model. Different sources of truth.

motivation.why_it_exists: High-stakes problem-solving needs a lifecycle — frame, plan, execute, verify. OrchestrationLoop names the strict sequence: RequestFraming → ManifestPlanning → Execution → Verify, mediated by typed artifacts through non-compensatory gates. Without the named pattern, these stages blur.
motivation.removability: Removable for low-stakes work; the named failure 'Bureaucracy' is exactly what happens when you apply it to trivial tasks. Essential for high-stakes, where the lifecycle discipline prevents skipped phases.

usage.intended: strict lifecycle for high-stakes problem solving — Interpret → Plan → Rollout.
usage.broad_contexts: software development lifecycles, scientific research workflows, organizational decision-making, regulatory-compliant processes, safety-critical development.
usage.every_context_needs: three phases (framing, planning, rollout), typed-artifact transitions, AcceptSpec gates between phases, iteration capability on failure.
usage.varies: phase granularity, rollback depth on iteration, parallel-phase support, external-gate integration.

tensions: Artifact Mediation invariant vs speed — every phase transition produces a typed artifact; simpler workflows pay unnecessary ceremony.
Non-Compensatory Gates vs iterative refinement — binary pass/fail forces crisp gating that iterative refinement resists.
Iteration Bound invariant vs genuine complexity — hard iteration limits escalate too soon on genuinely hard problems.
tradeoffs: Gains: strict lifecycle for high-stakes work, typed-artifact mediation, named phase structure.
Gives up: agility. OrchestrationLoop is heavy; for rapid iteration, other patterns fit.
critique: Bureaucracy (named failure) — applying lifecycle to trivial tasks — is the over-application pathology.
Loop Stalling (named failure) — stuck in Plan/Rollout without shipping — happens when non-compensatory gates reject repeatedly.
Artifact Rejection Cascade — rejections propagate back, forcing re-work at earlier stages.

OrchestrationLoop.family_discussion: High-ceremony workflow primitive paired with RequestFraming, ManifestPlanning, and Rollout. Compare with OODA — OrchestrationLoop is heavyweight sequential; OODA is lightweight cyclic. Different stakes, different ceremony.

motivation.why_it_exists: Attention is finite; messages need pressure to enter. OsmoticFilter names the semi-permeable boundary: messages need stake/reputation/relevance to overcome membrane tension. Without the pattern, attention is flooded.
motivation.removability: Removable — other filter patterns work. OsmoticFilter is specifically the pressure-based variant.

usage.intended: spam prevention via pressure thresholds — inbound rejected unless sufficient pressure.
usage.broad_contexts: paid-email-prioritization, crypto-gas-based message priority, reputation-gated access, staked-messaging protocols, priority-queues-with-stakes.
usage.every_context_needs: pressure metric (stake, reputation, relevance), membrane-threshold, multi-solvent conversion if applicable.
usage.varies: pressure types, conversion rates, hysteresis integration, membrane-adjustment dynamics.

tensions: Starvation of low-stake important messages (named failure).
Normalized Pressure invariant vs dynamic demand.
Permeability relaxation — when demand is low, membrane relaxes.
tradeoffs: Gains: adaptive attention filtering.
Gives up: simplicity. Pressure-based gating is more complex than fixed threshold.
critique: Starvation is endemic; Whitelist mitigation is mentioned but external.
Snapback (if Queue drops) adds oscillation risk.
The biological metaphor is evocative; operational tuning is under-specified. Deduplicated failure modes (was listed twice).

OsmoticFilter.family_discussion: Attention primitive paired with AttentionMarkets (pricing-based), InputGuard (predicate-based), and Throttle. Compare with AttentionMarkets — OsmoticFilter is pressure; AttentionMarkets is auction.

motivation.why_it_exists: What actually happens can differ from what was planned. Outcome names the actual-result slot, distinct from Plan or Prediction. Without the pattern, post-hoc analysis has no clean vocabulary for 'reality, as opposed to intent.'
motivation.removability: Very thin — nearly a stub. Hard to argue against keeping a slot for 'the actual result.' Remove it and IntentGap, HindsightBlock, CounterfactualAnchor have to re-derive the concept.

usage.intended: actual result that occurs in reality — may differ from Plan due to external factors.
usage.broad_contexts: experiment outcomes, medical outcomes, project outcomes, investment outcomes, game outcomes, policy outcomes.
usage.every_context_needs: actual-reality captured, distinction from Plan/Intent, attribution of deviation causes.
usage.varies: granularity of capture, retrospective depth, stakeholder perspective.

tensions: Actual result vs multiple valid outcomes — some situations have multiple outcomes depending on what you measure.
Timing of outcome declaration — early declarations may be wrong; late declarations may miss window for action.
Outcome vs observation — you only know the outcome through observation, which can be wrong.
tradeoffs: Gains: clean slot for actual-result vs planned-result, substrate for post-hoc analysis.
Gives up: very little — thin primitive with no controversial invariants.
critique: Almost a stub — one sentence, no invariants, no failure modes.
Doesn't address outcome ambiguity — some situations have contested actual results.
Conflates observation with outcome; the outcome is observer-independent, observations of it are not.

Outcome.family_discussion: Paired with Plan (the intent), Prediction (the anticipated outcome), and IntentGap (the analysis of divergence). Compare with Result — Outcome is reality-anchored; Result is the produced artifact.

motivation.why_it_exists: Generated outputs can leak PII, produce toxic content, or violate safety policies. OutputGuard names the post-generation filter: scan against patterns and classifiers, redact or reject. Without it, safety depends on the generator not misbehaving, which isn't robust.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in production-facing generation systems. The pattern mirrors InputGuard for the output side; the Fail-Safe invariant (scanner failure → block) is the load-bearing safety property.

usage.intended: post-generation content filter for PII/toxicity at egress.
usage.future: any egress filter on generated content.
usage.broad_contexts: LLM safety filters, content moderation, PII redaction, toxicity classification, compliance-disclosure review, export-control filtering.
usage.every_context_needs: content to scan, detectors (PII, toxicity, etc.), threshold-based mitigation (redact/reject), scan-before-egress timing.
usage.varies: detector set, threshold values, mitigation strategy (redact vs reject vs rewrite), audit logging of interventions.

tensions: Fail-Safe vs availability — blocking outputs on scanner failure is safe and reduces availability.
Scunthorpe problem (named failure) — over-censorship blocking valid words containing restricted substrings.
Context Blindness (named failure) — medical terms misclassified as toxicity; context-aware classifiers are adjacent patterns.
tradeoffs: Gains: post-generation safety net, explicit PII redaction, explicit fail-safe default.
Gives up: output freshness/richness. Every filter pass potentially removes content; aggressive filtering produces anodyne output.
critique: Redaction Leak (named failure) — [REDACTED] markers themselves leak information (position, frequency).
Scunthorpe problem is endemic; substring-based matching is crude and the pattern's approach inherits this.
Context Blindness — classifiers without contextual awareness — is the dominant production failure.

OutputGuard.family_discussion: Safety primitive paired with InputGuard (input counterpart), FailClosed (the default), and Redact (the mitigation). Compare with InvariantFilter — OutputGuard is classifier-based; InvariantFilter is predicate-based. Different filter architectures.

motivation.why_it_exists: Negotiating positions works better when each party reveals what they can live with rather than what they want. Overlap names the accept-set protocol: hash-commit, reveal, intersect. Without the pattern, negotiation is positional (anchor and dig in) rather than interest-based.
motivation.removability: Removable — positional negotiation is the default. Overlap earns its weight specifically in settings where parties prefer to find mutually-acceptable outcomes over winning positions. The commit-reveal discipline is load-bearing for honesty.

usage.intended: accept-set intersection-finding negotiation — commit-reveal protocol.
usage.future: any "find what we both agree on" negotiation primitive.
usage.broad_contexts: union negotiations, political compromise finding, requirements-intersection elicitation, multi-stakeholder design, M&A deal points, diplomatic common ground.
usage.every_context_needs: each-party accept-set, hash-commit-before-reveal, intersection compute, expand-or-succeed loop.
usage.varies: expansion-step size, expansion-cap, fallback on no-overlap.

tensions: Strategic minimal accept-sets (named failure) — game the protocol by claiming small acceptable sets — is mitigated but not eliminated by commit-reveal.
Accept-sets too abstract (named failure) — sets that don't intersect meaningfully.
Expansion limit with no overlap (named failure) — parties truly have no overlap.
tradeoffs: Gains: interest-based negotiation, honest accept-set discipline via commit-reveal, structural path to agreement when overlap exists.
Gives up: simplicity. Overlap requires more ceremony than positional negotiation.
critique: Requires both parties to submit the format; uncooperative parties can't be forced.
Hash-committing accept-sets assumes sets can be specified precisely; vague 'I can live with X-ish' is common.
Strategic minimization is mitigated by commit-reveal and is not fully defeated.

Overlap.family_discussion: Negotiation primitive paired with Compromise (iterative dampening), Consensus (full agreement), and Commit-Reveal (the cryptographic substrate). Compare with Handshake — Overlap finds shared zones; Handshake establishes connection.

motivation.why_it_exists: Four independent viability checks on an artifact produce four separate signals; without a framework for composing them, reviewers either collapse them into a weighted average (which Compensatory Drift is exactly) or evaluate them in a single pass (Single-Context Contamination). PURE names the non-compensatory four-axis composition.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for the paper's quality-gate methodology. The framework codifies how Parsimony, Unique/Novelty, Realizable, Expansive compose into a single viability judgment. Remove it and the four axes exist as separate judges without a unifying contract.

tensions: Orthogonality invariant (evaluated in isolation) vs practical review — human reviewers naturally integrate; strict isolation is discipline.
Four-axis invariant vs other possible dimensions — why these four? The paper argues for them; other frameworks might have different axes.
Non-compensatory vs intuitive weighting — reviewers want to trade off; PURE forbids it.
tradeoffs: Gains: structural anti-averaging discipline, explicit four-axis composition, named framework for quality gates.
Gives up: nuance. The non-compensatory rule means any single axis failing is reject; borderline cases on multiple axes have no nuanced handling.
critique: Single-Context Contamination (named failure) is subtle and pervasive — reviewers naturally soften Parsimony when moved by Expansive, and the pattern's isolation invariant is the defense.
Compensatory Drift (named failure) — 'weighted average' evaluation — is the default human approach the framework explicitly rejects.
The four axes are defensible and not proven universal; the framework commits to them anyway.

PURE.family_discussion: Quality-gate framework paired with Parsimony, Unique (via Novelty), Realizable, and Expansive as the four axes. Consumed by PURECheck, PUREBrainstorming, and DecompositionGate. Compare with MECE — PURE is an evaluation framework; MECE is a partitioning framework.

motivation.why_it_exists: Standard brainstorming prioritizes quantity and filters later; in LLM-era generation, unfiltered quantity is cheap and low-value. PUREBrainstorming names the quality-filtered variant: every candidate immediately faces PURECheck before proposal. Without it, LLM brainstorming produces many ideas; few are serious.
motivation.removability: Removable — standard brainstorming covers the unfiltered case. PUREBrainstorming earns weight when quality matters more than quantity. The Filter-First invariant flips the conventional order.

usage.intended: rigorous ideation protocol — Generate → PURECheck → PUREOptimization → Propose.
usage.broad_contexts: R&D concept generation, invention flow, scientific hypothesis generation, design ideation, product-feature conception.
usage.every_context_needs: generator, PURECheck gate, PUREOptimization step, MechanisticDesignProposal output.
usage.varies: generator diversity, optimization depth, convergence criteria.

tensions: Filter-First vs divergent ideation — filtering during generation suppresses the 'no bad ideas' quality that makes some brainstorming productive.
Mechanistic Rigor invariant vs lightweight ideation — requiring MechanisticDesignProposal schema is heavy.
Immediate filtering vs reflective filtering — immediate is efficient, reflective catches better ideas that would have been filtered early.
tradeoffs: Gains: quality-filtered ideation, reduced noise, explicit PUREcheck integration.
Gives up: divergent volume. PUREBrainstorming produces fewer, better ideas; some applications want more, more-raw ideas.
critique: Filter-First may suppress ideas that would have survived after light refinement; the PUREcheck may be too strict at the seed stage.
Mechanistic Rigor requirement means every idea must be fully specified; early seeds rarely are.
No failure modes listed; PUREBrainstorming has some (premature filtering, over-rigorous early critique).

PUREBrainstorming.family_discussion: PURE-application sibling of PURECheck (triage mode) and PUREOptimization (improvement mode). Compare with standard Brainstorming — PUREBrainstorming trades volume for quality.

motivation.why_it_exists: The PURE framework needs a canonical execution protocol — sequential triage through four TriGates, one per axis. PURECheck names this as the Exploration Protocol. Without it, PURE is a framework without a canonical application.
motivation.removability: Removable in principle — callers can apply PURE via any protocol. PURECheck's value is as the named canonical procedure: sequential, layered, non-compensatory. Removing it leaves PURE without a default application method.

usage.intended: canonical exploration protocol — layered TriGate triage on Parsimony, Novelty, Realizability, Expansiveness.
usage.broad_contexts: pattern-mint evaluation, research proposal triage, design decision review, architectural proposal screening, scientific paper screening.
usage.every_context_needs: all four gates (Parsimony, Novelty, Realizable, Expansive) applied in sequence, Yellow-output Technical-Debt tracking, Red-on-any-gate termination.
usage.varies: gate threshold values, evaluator identity (self vs committee), debt-ledger integration, parallel vs sequential gate evaluation.

tensions: Sequential triage vs parallel evaluation — sequential is LayeredCheck-style (cheap fails early); parallel is more complete.
TriGate per axis vs continuous score — TriGate is binary-ish (three levels), losing gradation.
Exploration Protocol framing vs other applications — PURECheck is specifically for exploration; other PURE uses (design review, publication) need different protocols.
tradeoffs: Gains: canonical PURE execution, sequential fail-fast via LayeredCheck, clear triage procedure.
Gives up: flexibility. The sequential layered application is one way to use PURE; others exist and are outside the pattern.
critique: Sequential triage means order matters; the PURE axes are 'orthogonal' by framework claim but order still affects feel.
Four TriGates is a specific shape; alternative PURE applications (each axis scored, then aggregated non-compensatively) aren't covered.
The 'canonical Exploration protocol' framing is committal — PURECheck takes a stance on what PURE-for-exploration looks like.

PURECheck.family_discussion: PURE instantiation paired with PUREBrainstorming (another application), TriGate (the sub-component), and LayeredCheck (the execution pattern). Compare with PUREOptimization — different PURE applications for different contexts.

motivation.why_it_exists: PURE evaluation produces a verdict; PUREOptimization is the multi-agent improvement strategy that improves candidate on all four axes simultaneously. Without the pattern, improving one axis often breaks another.
motivation.removability: Removable — single-axis optimization works for simpler cases. PUREOptimization is specifically the multi-axis non-regression discipline.

usage.intended: multi-agent optimization across PURE dimensions — decompose solution into 4 parallel streams.
usage.broad_contexts: design review with specialist committees, academic revision by specialist co-authors, product optimization by cross-functional teams.
usage.every_context_needs: candidate that passed PURECheck, decomposition into 4 streams (P/U/R/E), specialist per stream, re-integration.
usage.varies: specialist selection, stream weighting, iteration count, conflict resolution between streams.

tensions: Monotonic Improvement vs real trade-offs — improving one axis often costs another.
Non-Destructive vs synthesis — combining axis-specific improvements can introduce conflicts.
