Synthesis Failure (named failure) — four optimized parts don't combine.
tradeoffs: Gains: multi-axis PURE improvement, explicit non-regression.
Gives up: single-axis fluency. Every axis pays the multi-axis review.
critique: Optimization Conflict is endemic — Novel improvements often reduce Realizability.
Synthesis Failure requires trade-off negotiation the pattern defers.
Monotonic Improvement across all axes is often impossible.

PUREOptimization.family_discussion: PURE-application sibling of PURECheck (triage) and PUREBrainstorming (ideation). Uses PURE as the evaluation framework.

motivation.why_it_exists: Names the structural opposite of Chain — two or more paths execute simultaneously with no ordering guarantee. Essential for concurrency semantics: when an agent says 'run A and B in parallel,' both parties need a shared definition of what that guarantees (and what it doesn't).
motivation.removability: Marginal. The pattern is semantically thin — almost tautological — but it anchors a distinction that patterns like AtomicBid and OptimisticSolver rely on. Without it, concurrency assumptions are implicit and disagreement fragments.

usage.intended: concurrent execution with no ordering guarantee.
usage.broad_contexts: thread pools, async/await patterns, map-reduce map phase, multi-agent parallel action, ensemble inference, GPU parallelism.
usage.every_context_needs: concurrent executable slots, absence of ordering constraint.
usage.varies: parallelism degree, synchronization points, shared-state access model, failure aggregation.

tensions: No-ordering vs causal ordering: Parallel says 'no ordering guarantee' but many real parallel operations have weak ordering (eventual consistency, happens-before). The pattern is strict — any ordering requirement rules out Parallel.

Simultaneous vs interleaved: Parallel implies genuine concurrency. Cooperative-scheduled interleaving satisfies the no-ordering letter but not the simultaneity spirit. The pattern is unclear which it requires.
Primitive vs composed: Parallel is listed as a Data Structure but is really a control-flow shape. The classification is arguable.
tradeoffs: Minimal semantics buys universality at the cost of precision.
No ordering guarantee buys implementation freedom (any scheduling honors the pattern) at the cost of weak composability — callers that need ordering must say so elsewhere.
Category as Data Structure buys consistency in the library taxonomy at the cost of semantic fit.
critique: Zero invariants and zero failure modes. For a concurrency primitive this is a significant gap — at minimum: Independence (A and B don't share state without explicit synchronization); Non-Interference (execution of A doesn't affect B's outcome).
The mechanism is one sentence. It should at least distinguish Parallel from Concurrent, which are different things (parallel = actually simultaneous; concurrent = interleaved).
No relationship to AtomicBid, Actor Model, or OptimisticSolver specified — these patterns depend on Parallel's semantics but the linkage is implicit.

Parallel.family_discussion: Structural opposite of `Chain` (linear). Foundational for concurrency — `AtomicBid`, `OptimisticSolver`, Actor Model implementations all assume Parallel semantics. The pattern is minimal; specializations (`ThreadedParallel`, `ProcessParallel`, `AgentParallel`) differentiate by execution substrate.

motivation.why_it_exists: Independent tasks can run simultaneously; same task can run multiple times for voting. Parallelize names both modes: Sectioning (decompose-parallel-merge) and Voting (same task, aggregate). Without the pattern, parallel structure is ad-hoc and callers rediscover the two modes.
motivation.removability: Removable in sequential systems. The pattern captures a well-established LLM-orchestration pattern (widely used in 2024-2025 prompt engineering). Remove it and the two modes get reimplemented everywhere.

usage.intended: run subtasks simultaneously and aggregate — Sectioning or Voting modes.
usage.broad_contexts: parallel LLM calls, map-reduce, ensemble methods, concurrent tool use, parallel research, A/B testing.
usage.every_context_needs: task, decomposition or replication, concurrent execution, aggregation.
usage.varies: mode (Section vs Vote), concurrency degree, aggregation function, failure handling.

tensions: Task independence invariant vs real coupling — tasks often have subtle dependencies that break parallel execution.
Max(Task_i) + Overhead — parallel is as slow as the slowest; one straggler dominates.
Voting mode vs single-run — voting improves reliability at cost; for reliable tasks the vote is waste.
tradeoffs: Gains: wall-clock speedup, reliability via voting, explicit mode distinction (Sectioning vs Voting).
Gives up: compute efficiency. Parallel N tasks costs N× compute; for cost-bounded settings, serial is often correct.
critique: Merge Conflicts (named failure) — outputs can't be combined — is endemic; the pattern doesn't specify merge strategy.
Unanimous Wrong (named failure) — all parallel paths share the same error — makes voting useless when correlation is high.
Aggregation Bias — merge strategy adds systematic error — lives outside the pattern's invariants.

Parallelize.family_discussion: Orchestration primitive paired with Sectioning (Decompose variant), Vote (the voting mode), and Merge (the aggregation). Compare with Chain — Parallelize is breadth, Chain is depth. Both are orchestration.

motivation.why_it_exists: Multi-objective optimization doesn't collapse to a single metric — improving A may require degrading B. ParetoFront names the explicit frontier: solutions where no improvement in one axis is possible without loss in another. Without the pattern, multi-objective problems get forced into weighted-sum aggregation, which loses the frontier structure.
motivation.removability: Removable in single-objective optimization. Essential for explicit trade-off space exploration — design, policy, resource allocation. The Efficiency invariant (Pareto optimality) is the structural frontier definition.

usage.intended: frontier curve where improving metric A requires degrading metric B.
usage.broad_contexts: engineering tradeoffs, portfolio theory, product-feature selection, hyperparameter tuning, economic policy tradeoffs, resource allocation.
usage.every_context_needs: competing metrics, dominance-check (strictly inferior = discard), frontier identification.
usage.varies: metric count, sampling density, frontier approximation method.

tensions: Frontier discovery vs compute cost — mapping the full Pareto front costs much more than optimizing a single weighted metric.
Tradeoff Rate invariant (Gain × Rate > Loss) vs non-linear tradeoffs — the invariant is linear; real tradeoffs often have thresholds and concavities.
Pareto-optimal set vs single decision — the front has many points, and picking one is itself a decision the pattern doesn't resolve.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit trade-off space, principled multi-objective framing, named frontier primitive.
Gives up: single-answer simplicity. ParetoFront produces a set, not a point; callers must still choose.
critique: No failure modes listed; ParetoFront has some (front approximation error, linear-tradeoff assumption, single-point selection bias).
Efficiency invariant is the Pareto definition; the real work (mapping the front, selecting a point) lives outside.
Assumes metrics are comparable (commensurable trade-offs); for genuinely incommensurable axes, Pareto dominance isn't defined.

ParetoFront.family_discussion: Multi-objective primitive paired with Optimize (single-objective counterpart), Compromise (the social analogue), and ExchangeRate (the tradeoff-quantifier). Compare with OpportunityCost — ParetoFront is multi-axis; OpportunityCost is alternative-based.

motivation.why_it_exists: Occam's razor operationalized for artifacts — does the minimum-complexity form perform the function? Parsimony names this judgment. Without the named primitive, simplicity evaluation gets folded into generic Score, losing the specific 'strip non-essential' discipline.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for PURE. The quality gate depends on Parsimony as one of its four axes. Remove it and PURE loses simplicity enforcement; designs drift toward complexity over time.

usage.intended: Occam's Razor judgment — classify topology complexity as Bloated/Under-specified/Minimal.
usage.broad_contexts: theory selection, ML model selection, system architecture review, design simplification, Occam's Razor decisions, regulatory streamlining.
usage.every_context_needs: candidate structure, ablation test (remove component, check function), three-class output.
usage.varies: ablation rigor, multi-objective weighting, domain-specific simplicity metrics.

tensions: Minimum complexity vs robustness — the simplest form that works is often brittle; more complex versions handle edge cases.
Necessity invariant (every component has causal link) vs cross-cutting concerns — some components serve multiple purposes, making causal attribution fuzzy.
Parsimony vs Expansive — the two axes can conflict; a pattern can be minimally-complex locally and fail to generalize.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit simplicity enforcement, causal-necessity invariant, named judge for Occam's razor.
Gives up: feature-richness. Parsimony favors minimal; maximalist designs fail by construction.
critique: Very thin — one invariant, one-line mechanism. The judgment of 'necessity' is subjective.
Causal link for every component is a high bar; many real components serve emergent purposes that resist direct causal attribution.
No failure modes listed; Parsimony has some (over-stripping, false simplicity, reverse-engineering complexity).

Parsimony.family_discussion: PURE axis paired with Novelty, Realizable, Expansive. Consumed by PURECheck. Compare with Compress — Parsimony is structural simplicity; Compress is information-size reduction.

motivation.why_this_layer: cache of routing outcomes — single-agent memory
motivation.why_it_exists: The compounding-learning site for dispatching Solvers — records (problem_class, route, outcome_quality) so routing decisions learn from past results. The RootSolver's PathwayMemory is the FI architecture's most consequential site because it sees every problem entering the system. Without this pattern, solver trees are stateless per invocation and can't compound.
motivation.removability: No. The FI architecture's claim to 'compounding reasoning infrastructure' rests on PathwayMemory being present at dispatch points. Removing it makes solver trees amnesic.

tensions: Append-only vs correction: the invariant forbids editing historical records. But a poisoned entry that later proves false (named failure mode) can only be removed, not corrected in place. This is a strong immutability stance the library takes explicitly.

Scoped-to-one-node vs cross-node sharing: each PathwayMemory belongs to exactly one node. That prevents contamination (named failure mode: 'cross-node aggregation without provenance contaminates local routing') but also prevents federation — a team of RootSolvers can't share routing lessons without a separate pattern.
Stale entries vs fresh signal: named failure mode 'no automatic aging.' Adding aging would violate append-only; the library chose append-only and pushes aging to the read side.
tradeoffs: Append-only buys tamper-evidence (you can detect when records were modified) at the cost of correction friction.
Per-node scope buys isolation (one poisoned node doesn't corrupt others) at the cost of forbidding natural sharing.
Three-tuple structure (problem_class, route, outcome_quality) buys aggregability at the cost of restricting what can be remembered — richer signals (context, uncertainty) need schema extension.
critique: Three failure modes are sharp but name poisoning as 'silently bias all downstream routing without triggering any failure mode.' That's accurate and damning. The pattern needs defense in depth — anomaly detection on outcome_quality distributions, diversity checks, etc. — none currently in spec.

'Cache of routing outcomes' names the structure without the access policy. Who reads? Who writes? What is the cache eviction? The pattern leaves these to the implementer, meaning two PathwayMemory instances may behave very differently under load.

Relationship to ReceptivityGate: the ReceptivityGate protects writes to PathwayMemory, but the pattern itself doesn't enforce that every write came through ReceptivityGate. A direct write bypasses protection.

PathwayMemory.family_discussion: The memory substrate for compounding intelligence in the FI architecture. Composed with `ReceptivityGate` (write-side protection) and `PerformanceSignal` (typed input). Held primarily by `RootSolver` (the only node that sees all problems) but any dispatching Solver may maintain one for local routing decisions.

motivation.why_it_exists: Before minting a new pattern, existing patterns must be checked — otherwise the vocabulary accumulates synonyms. PatternDiscovery names the pre-mint semantic search: find existing candidates, compare via embedding similarity, block if duplicate. Without it, Not-Invented-Here proliferates.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for the Living Taxonomy workflow. The invariants (Deduplication, Pre-Mint Check) are the discipline that keeps the vocabulary from bloating. Remove it and MintWhenFriction can't function — minting without prior-art check is how Goodhart kills taxonomies.

usage.intended: vocabulary-hygiene protocol — semantic search before minting new pattern; adopt-or-justify-divergence.
usage.future: any "don't mint if one exists" discipline.
usage.broad_contexts: pattern-library hygiene, codebase duplicate-detection, ontology namespace management, nomenclature discipline, brand-namespace checking.
usage.every_context_needs: pre-mint search of existing registry, >85% similarity as adopt-trigger, explicit fork justification otherwise.
usage.varies: similarity threshold, registry scope, fork-justification rigor.
notes: §3.18 moves Society → Mind since this is single-agent cognitive hygiene. Broad-use confirms.

tensions: Similarity threshold — too high blocks legitimate novelty, too low lets near-dupes through.
Keyword Miss (named failure) — searcher uses different terminology than existing pattern, misses it.
Not Invented Here (named failure) — agent knows the pattern exists and creates a near-copy anyway.
tradeoffs: Gains: dedup discipline, vocabulary hygiene, explicit pre-mint log.
Gives up: speed. Every mint pays the search tax; high-volume contexts fight this.
critique: Keyword Miss is a real failure — LLMs routinely use different terms for the same concept, and LatentAttachment is the mitigation but not a guarantee.
NIH is social, not structural — the pattern can detect similarity but can't prevent motivated re-creation.
Threshold is caller-set, with no default derivation rule.

PatternDiscovery.family_discussion: Vocabulary-growth gate paired with MintWhenFriction (the trigger), Search (the substrate), and LatentAttachment (the similarity substrate). Compare with Novelty — PatternDiscovery is the deduplication check; Novelty is the structural-distinctness judge.

motivation.why_it_exists: Top-down pattern design produces patterns that look clean and may not match reality. PatternEmergence names the bottom-up observational discipline: analyze interaction logs for recurring behaviors, formalize what's already there. Without the pattern, top-down design dominates and real practice gets forced into designer-imagined shapes.
motivation.removability: Removable if you trust top-down design. The pattern is specifically the corrective lens — name what emerges, not what you'd like. The Existence Proof invariant (observed in the wild before named) is the discipline.

usage.intended: recognize implicit patterns bottom-up from interaction logs before top-down design.
usage.broad_contexts: user-research-driven product design, descriptive-before-prescriptive linguistics, emergent-team convention documentation, bottom-up ontology building.
usage.every_context_needs: interaction logs, pattern-recognition mechanism, codification pathway (to MintWhenFriction), matching against existing pattern discovery.
usage.varies: log depth, pattern-recognition method (manual, ML, hybrid), codification threshold.

tensions: Descriptive Priority invariant vs normative ambition — initially describe, only later prescribe; in practice descriptors slide into prescriptions.
Existence Proof requirement — must be observed in the wild — is slow when you want to propose new patterns.
Apophenia (named failure) — seeing patterns in noise — is endemic; observational heuristics have no anti-apophenia mechanism.
tradeoffs: Gains: grounded pattern naming, explicit descriptive-first discipline, existence proof requirement.
Gives up: speed and novelty. New ideas can't be named until they've emerged, which delays adoption.
critique: Codifying Bad Habits (named failure) — formalizing a workaround to a broken system — is real; the pattern can't distinguish workaround from solution.
Apophenia is hard to prevent; the pattern asserts observation but can't verify it's real.
Over-fitting is the third named failure — the pattern exists in observations but doesn't generalize.

PatternEmergence.family_discussion: Observation-first primitive paired with PatternDiscovery (the pre-mint search), DogfoodFirst (creator validation), and Stigmergy (the trace substrate). Compare with ConstructOntology — PatternEmergence is bottom-up; ConstructOntology is top-down.

motivation.why_it_exists: Sometimes an agent references a pattern approximately — 'like PolymorphicSolver but without the frame-error check.' PatternSketch names this approximate reference with explicit uncertainty and modifications. Without it, approximate references either pretend to be canonical (misleading) or lose their pattern-anchor (ungrounded).
motivation.removability: Removable if you demand strict pattern conformance. Essential for iterative pattern development where agents are exploring before canonicalizing. The Explicit Delta invariant — list what differs — prevents silent divergence.

usage.intended: reference a canonical concept with explicit uncertainty and modifications (approximation).
usage.broad_contexts: early-stage design references, research-in-progress citations, prototype-level pattern use, legal "mutatis mutandis" references.
usage.every_context_needs: base pattern reference, explicit uncertainty marker, delta description, eventual full-conformance path.
usage.varies: uncertainty representation, delta specification format, upgrade path to full conformance.

tensions: Sketches never harden into Canonical patterns (named failure) — the vocabulary degrades into approximate references.
Confidence Awareness invariant (tests treated as advisory) vs real test discipline — advisory tests are often ignored.
Drift (named failure) — sketches accumulate without consolidation.
tradeoffs: Gains: principled approximate reference, explicit delta, confidence-awareness.
Gives up: canonicality. Overusing Sketch means the vocabulary accumulates approximations instead of consolidating into canonical patterns.
critique: Drift is the dominant failure — sketches accumulating without the canonicalization step.
No specified canonicalization trigger — when should a sketch become canonical?
Confidence < 1.0 treating tests as advisory is a pragmatic compromise that can become permanent laxity.

PatternSketch.family_discussion: Pattern-lifecycle primitive paired with Mint (the canonicalization step), PatternDiscovery (prior art), and ConceptAnchor (the canonical target). Compare with Hypothesis — both are provisional; Hypothesis is for claims, PatternSketch is for patterns.

motivation.why_it_exists: The typed output of a Solver's Feedback surface — three-outcome (evaluation / pass / FrameError) so downstream PathwayMemory can aggregate consistently across instances. Without a dedicated type, each Solver emits different-shaped feedback and aggregation fragments — the routing-learning property (PathwayMemory's raison d'être) breaks.
motivation.removability: No. The Solver→Feedback→PathwayMemory chain is the compounding-learning mechanism the FI architecture depends on. Removing PerformanceSignal collapses the chain into untyped text that cannot be aggregated.

tensions: Three-outcome vs richer structure: the invariant 'three-outcome' forbids intermediate states (partially accept, escalate-but-try-again). Some real cases want those; descendants handle them, but the parent is tight.

Attribution vs privacy: 'names the Solver node that produced the Result' is needed for localized learning but exposes identity in multi-agent commons. The trade is intentional; in closed deployments it's free, in open commons it's a real cost.
Signal poisoning mitigated by ReceptivityGate: the pattern acknowledges this but defers the fix to a different pattern. Standalone PerformanceSignal has no poisoning defense.
tradeoffs: Typed schema buys aggregability (PathwayMemory can average, rank, cluster) at the cost of excluding evaluations that don't fit the shape.
Attribution buys localized learning at the cost of exposure — attacker who sees PerformanceSignals can profile Solvers.
Three-outcome buys simple routing (proceed / confirm / reframe) at the cost of dropping nuanced outcomes (accept with reservations, escalate-and-retry).
critique: Latency Decay is a named failure but no mechanism addresses it. A timestamp + decay policy would let downstream systems weight older signals less — not in the pattern.

The typed schema is required by invariant but not specified in the pattern itself — the shape is supposed to be per-deployment. Aggregation across deployments requires schema negotiation the library doesn't provide.
Sycophantic drift (evaluator shares generator's blind spots) is a real failure but the spec has no detection mechanism — relies on having diverse evaluators, which lives outside the pattern.

PerformanceSignal.family_discussion: Output of the Feedback surface; input to PathwayMemory. Three-outcome type bridging evaluation (graded via Judge), pass (typed confirmation), and FrameError (escalation). Pairs with FailureTrace when the outcome is reject-with-evidence. Guarded by ReceptivityGate when consumed in adversarial settings.

motivation.why_it_exists: Authorization for actions needs a unit — the atomic grant allowing agent to perform act or access artifact. Permission names this unit. Without it, authorization is scattered across specific primitives (BearerToken, ExpiringToken, Card) without a unifying grant concept.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in any access-controlled system. The pattern is the atomic unit that specific authorization mechanisms (BearerToken, ExpiringToken, Card) specialize. Remove it and the authorization family loses its substrate.

usage.intended: atomic authorization grant.
usage.broad_contexts: file-system permissions, API scopes, OAuth tokens, role-capability grants, feature-access grants, capability-based security.
usage.every_context_needs: granting identity, recipient identity, scope (what is permitted), act-or-artifact target.
usage.varies: expiry, delegation support, revocation mechanism, granularity (coarse vs fine-grained), composability (multiple permissions aggregate).

tensions: Atomic grant vs composed permissions — real authorization is often composed; the atomic framing is a lens not a constraint.
Permission as grant vs permission as check — the pattern conflates the grant (what's authorized) with the check (evaluating grants).
Privilege escalation (named failure) — agent acquires beyond scope — is the canonical security failure.
tradeoffs: Gains: unifying authorization primitive, named unit for access control.
Gives up: richness. Permission is a single unit; real authorization has scope, conditions, and relationships the pattern doesn't capture.
critique: Very thin — one-line mechanism, two failure modes, no invariants.
Conflates grant with check; these are distinct in real systems.
No semantics for composition — AND/OR over permissions is common and not specified.

Permission.family_discussion: Foundational auth primitive paired with BearerToken (portable grant), Card (capability advertisement), and Check (evaluation). Compare with Token — Permission is the abstract grant; Token is the embodied artifact.

motivation.why_it_exists: When risk exceeds threshold, agent blocks and requests elevated permission. PermissionEscalate names this. Without the pattern, agents either self-escalate or stall silently.
motivation.removability: Removable in fixed-permission systems. Essential for adaptive permission contexts.

usage.intended: request elevated privileges for sensitive operations when Risk > Threshold.
usage.future: any "I need higher authority for this" escalation.
usage.broad_contexts: sudo privilege escalation, enterprise elevated-access requests, emergency-access workflows, surgical-decision escalation to attending, editorial-escalation in journalism.
usage.every_context_needs: risk assessment, threshold trigger, blocking-on-request, SignedApproval wait.
usage.varies: authority hierarchy, approval timeout, retry after denial, emergency override.

tensions: Privilege Creep (named failure) — escalated permissions stay.
Signed Approval vs delay — every escalation adds latency.
Risk threshold tuning.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured escalation path.
Gives up: speed.
critique: Privilege Creep is endemic; the pattern doesn't specify retention policy.
Risk threshold is caller-set.
No failure modes beyond Privilege Creep.

PermissionEscalate.family_discussion: Security primitive paired with Permission, BearerToken, and HumanApprove.

motivation.why_it_exists: Single-viewpoint reasoning misses considerations a different viewpoint would catch. PerspectiveEnsemble names the N-persona debate: distinct viewpoints, isolated round-1, synthesis emerges from interaction. Without the pattern, agents default to a single voice.
motivation.removability: Removable — single-persona reasoning works for narrow tasks. Essential for multi-axis decisions (design reviews, ethical questions, contested claims). The Semantic Distance invariant keeps personas from collapsing to synonyms.

usage.intended: instantiate N virtual personas to debate a problem from pre-defined viewpoints.
usage.future: any "multiple expert perspectives simulated" reasoning method.
usage.broad_contexts: consultant-simulation LLM prompts, devils-advocate inclusion, ethical-dilemma multi-stakeholder analysis, red/blue/purple team discussion, imaginary-expert panels.
usage.every_context_needs: persona set, debate protocol, synthesis from interaction, Steelmanning of opposing views.
usage.varies: persona count, persona definitions, synthesis method (aggregate vs dialectic).

tensions: Semantic Distance invariant (cosine < 0.6) vs coherent synthesis — very distant personas are hard to synthesize.
Independence in Round 1 vs echo-chamber Round 2+ — isolating round 1 prevents early collapse; subsequent rounds often collapse anyway (Role Drift, named failure).
Strawman Waltz (named failure) — personas agree too easily (fabricated consensus) — is the pattern's canonical failure.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured multi-perspective reasoning, explicit semantic distance, independence-in-round-1 discipline.
Gives up: simplicity. N personas cost N× compute; synthesis quality is sometimes not worth the cost.
critique: Strawman Waltz and Role Drift are the two dominant failures and the pattern has no structural defenses.
Cosine similarity < 0.6 is an embedding-model-dependent threshold.
Synthesis step is under-specified — after the debate, how does final synthesis happen?

PerspectiveEnsemble.family_discussion: Multi-persona primitive paired with SteelmanCheck (strongest opposing), DissentSeek (active disagreement), and Debate (the activity). Compare with DiscoveryProtocol — PerspectiveEnsemble is persona-based, DiscoveryProtocol is mode-based; both enforce diversity.

motivation.why_it_exists: Sudden qualitative reorganization at a threshold — water→ice, liquid→gas, but also network percolation, social tipping points, crystallization in the library's own Crystallize pattern. Naming the threshold phenomenon as a substrate pattern lets dependent patterns invoke the concept without each redefining 'when does a qualitative shift happen?'
motivation.removability: Marginal. The pattern is structured-thinking territory — the threshold is a formally-crisp notion distinct from continuous change. Patterns like Crystallize and Nucleate invoke phase-transition semantics; without the substrate pattern, each redefines the threshold locally.

tensions: Sharp threshold vs fuzzy transitions: real transitions are often rounded by noise or finite-size effects. The mechanism requires a critical value but real thresholds have hysteresis-like width. Hysteresis is a separate pattern that handles this.

Qualitative change vs quantitative change: the invariant requires structural distinctness between regimes — not merely a parameter difference. Drawing the line between structural and quantitative is an interpretive act.

Non-continuity as an invariant: 'not a smooth function of the control parameter' is mathematically specific but many real transitions are continuous-with-sharp-gradient — classified as second-order transitions. The pattern is silent on this distinction.
tradeoffs: Structural distinctness invariant buys qualitative-shift semantics at the cost of excluding smooth-but-sharp changes.

Critical-parameter-threshold naming buys predictability (cross the threshold, transition happens) at the cost of hiding the dynamics around the transition point (critical slowing, divergent correlation lengths).
Physics placement buys substrate claim at the cost of ignoring the observer-dependence — the qualitative/quantitative distinction depends on what the observer considers 'structural.'
critique: No failure modes. Missing: Hysteretic Transition (transition threshold differs on ascent vs descent — the pattern assumes a single threshold), Missed Threshold (control parameter crosses the threshold but the system doesn't transition, perhaps due to nucleation delay).
'Qualitative change' is an interpretive claim — two observers may disagree on whether a change is qualitative. The pattern doesn't say how to adjudicate.

Second-order transitions (continuous phase changes) are excluded by the non-continuity invariant, which is defensible but should be stated — callers invoking `PhaseTransition` for a continuous case are out-of-spec.

PhaseTransition.family_discussion: Substrate law for threshold-triggered reorganization. Paired with `Equilibrium` (which can be multi-stable with phase boundaries), `Attractor` (basin boundaries align with transition thresholds), `Hysteresis` (the asymmetric-threshold relative). Invoked by `Crystallize`, `Nucleate`, tipping-point patterns.

motivation.why_it_exists: Refining an artifact on all axes at once produces regression — improving logic breaks structure, improving structure breaks tone. PhasedRefinement names the layered approach: pass 1 targets one abstraction (logic), pass 2 targets another (structure), etc. Without the pattern, refinement ping-pongs between concerns.
motivation.removability: Removable for simple artifacts that refine cleanly. Essential for multi-layer artifacts (papers, code, designs) where cross-layer regressions are common. The Non-Regression invariant is the layer-boundary discipline.

usage.intended: layered multi-pass improvement — each pass targets a specific abstraction level.
usage.broad_contexts: manuscript editing (logic → structure → prose → polish), code review layers (correctness → design → style), design iteration cycles, curriculum development.
usage.every_context_needs: ordered pass sequence, per-pass target abstraction, gate between passes.
usage.varies: pass count, pass ordering, gate strictness, rollback on late-discovered lower-level issue.

tensions: Non-Regression invariant vs legitimate revision — phase N can't violate phase N-1 invariants; but sometimes phase N reveals that phase N-1 invariants were wrong.
Monotonic Quality invariant vs multi-axis quality — overall quality may go up while a specific axis degrades.
Phase ordering — logic before structure, structure before tone — is a convention not a law.
tradeoffs: Gains: layered refinement discipline, explicit non-regression guarantee, structured pass sequence.
Gives up: holistic editing. Some refinement requires simultaneous consideration of multiple layers; PhasedRefinement forbids this.
critique: No failure modes listed; PhasedRefinement has some (wrong phase ordering, cross-phase regressions hidden in the structure).
The specific phase sequence (logic → structure → tone) is convention; different artifacts may warrant different orderings.
Monotonic Quality is hard to measure; in practice it's directional intuition.

PhasedRefinement.family_discussion: Refinement-strategy primitive paired with Refine (the general pattern), Reflexion (single-pass self-revision), and EvaluatorOptimizer (the two-role loop). Compare with Iterate — PhasedRefinement is layered; Iterate is unstructured repetition.

motivation.why_it_exists: Moving from current state to goal requires structured steps with causal ordering and a defined end. Plan names this artifact. Without it, 'plan' is any list, and the ordering/termination discipline that distinguishes actionable plans from wishlists is lost.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for structured execution. Every execution pattern (ExecutionManifest, Rollout, OrchestrationLoop) consumes Plan. The Ordering and Termination invariants are what make Plan usable by schedulers and solvers.

usage.intended: ordered sequence of steps to reach a goal.
usage.broad_contexts: execution plans, project roadmaps, sprint plans, travel itineraries, recipe steps, ML training schedules, build plans, deployment sequences.
usage.every_context_needs: sequence of steps, causal dependencies between steps, goal state, starting state.
usage.varies: step granularity, resource allocation, conditional branches, parallel execution, rollback points, revision policy.

tensions: Causal sortability vs emergent order — real plans often have steps whose ordering is discovered during execution.
Defined end state vs open-ended exploration — Plan requires termination; exploratory work sometimes doesn't have one.
Plan as static artifact vs live plan — the pattern's invariants suggest the Plan is produced then executed; real planning is often iterative.
tradeoffs: Gains: causal ordering, explicit termination, schedulable artifact.
Gives up: flexibility. Plans are produced before execution; mid-execution discoveries often warrant replanning.
critique: No failure modes listed; Plan has many (miscausation, ambiguous steps, undefined termination).
Causal sortability is an idealization; real dependency graphs have feedback loops.
No specified revision semantics — when execution reveals the Plan is wrong, what happens?

Plan.family_discussion: Foundational planning primitive paired with ExecutionManifest (the executable version), FrameSpec (the input), and ManifestPlanning (the production step). Compare with Strategy — Plan is step sequence; Strategy is higher-level approach.

motivation.why_this_layer: Solver-contract implementer — cognitive; multi-agent variants are specializations
motivation.why_it_exists: The concrete implementer of the abstract Solver contract — a named pattern for 'any entity that honors the five surfaces,' allowing heterogeneous substrates (LLM, human, tool, hybrid, swarm) to plug into the same runtime. Without PolymorphicSolver, the Solver interface stays abstract and every descendant has to declare which surfaces it implements rather than inheriting a standard answer.
motivation.removability: No. Every specialized solver (`OptimisticSolver`, `RigorousSolver`, `RootSolver`, domain-specific `DiagnosticSolver` / `PlanningSolver` etc.) inherits from PolymorphicSolver. Removing collapses the family tree and forces each descendant to re-state the surface contract.

tensions: Polymorphism vs verifiable conformance: 'treat all Solvers identically via this interface' is aspirational — detecting non-compliance requires probing every surface, which the runtime doesn't mandate. Interface Non-Compliance is flagged as a failure mode but the pattern has no enforcement.

Recursion vs termination: child solvers accept the same interface as parents. That is what gives the solver tree its fractal shape, but it also means nothing structurally prevents infinite decomposition — termination is a caller-level policy (budget, depth limit) rather than a pattern invariant.

Cognitive naming vs substrate-agnostic contract: the handle was renamed from CognitiveSolver to PolymorphicSolver precisely because the contract is about five surfaces, not cognition. But the pattern lives in Mind/Strategy — the layer reflects the typical substrate, not the essence of the mechanism.
tradeoffs: Uniform five-surface interface buys runtime polymorphism at the cost of forcing all implementers to either implement or explicitly omit each surface.
Manifest Drift as a named failure mode acknowledges that self-description diverges from behavior over time; the pattern has no mechanism to re-align them.
Role-based composition (agent wears solver role) is lightweight but loses strong identity — a crash mid-role leaves no typed residue.
critique: Two invariants are thin for the load-bearing pattern at the center of the FI architecture. Missing: Five-Surface Declaration (each implementer must statically declare which surfaces it honors); Feedback Integrity (Feedback surface, when present, must emit either a PerformanceSignal or a FrameError — not both, not neither).
Two failure modes; both are detection-only. No mitigation guidance: what does the runtime do on Non-Compliance? The pattern implies rejection, does not specify.
The mechanism mentions `{{card}}` for Manifest and `{{validate}}` for Verify but not what backs Execute, Consult, and Feedback — the surfaces without named pattern anchors are structurally weaker.
`derived_from` updated from stale Solver sema_id (10655bd6...) to current (b00a16af...).

PolymorphicSolver.family_discussion: The concrete implementer of the `Solver` abstract interface. Parent (via `derived_from`) to `OptimisticSolver`, `RigorousSolver`, `RootSolver`, and by convention the `[Descriptor]Solver` naming pattern. Composed with `Card` (Manifest), `Validate` (Verify), `SocraticLoop` (Consult), and `PerformanceSignal` (Feedback).

motivation.why_it_exists: Surfacing failure modes after deployment is expensive. PreMortem names the prospective-hindsight move: assume the plan has failed, generate specific reasons without defensiveness. Without the pattern, risk analysis drifts to generic caveats rather than specific endogenous failures.
motivation.removability: Removable — risk analysis can be done without the 'assume failure' framing. PreMortem's value is the cognitive shift: assuming failure at probability 1.0 removes defensive filtering that blocks honest risk acknowledgment.

usage.intended: simulate catastrophic failure *before* execution to surface hidden risks.
usage.broad_contexts: project kickoff reviews, launch-readiness checks, scientific-experiment design, safety engineering, investment-decision review, strategic-plan stress tests.
usage.every_context_needs: assumed-failed state, "what went wrong?" generation, per-failure mitigation addition to plan or reconsider-approach option.
usage.varies: failure-scenario depth, defensiveness-neutralization technique, mitigation-addition policy, repeat frequency.

tensions: Future Perspective (invariant: failure already happened) vs actual prediction — the framing is a cognitive device, not a claim about the future.
Specific Cause (invariant: actionable, not generic) vs imaginative failure — balancing between specific-and-addressable and specific-and-weird.
Performative Doomerism (named failure) — generic catastrophes instead of specific endogenous failures.
tradeoffs: Gains: honest risk surfacing, cognitive shift removes defensiveness, named discipline for pre-failure analysis.
Gives up: optimism. PreMortem is disproportionately useful and disproportionately psychologically uncomfortable.
critique: Performative Doomerism is endemic; specific failures require domain knowledge the pattern doesn"t provide.
Invariants are now deduplicated (was: four invariants forming two duplicate pairs — Future Perspective/Perspective Shift, Specific Cause/Specificity).
No specified mitigation link — PreMortem generates failure scenarios, and the follow-through (what to do about each) lives outside.

PreMortem.family_discussion: Risk-analysis primitive paired with Steelman (the positive counterpart), MechanisticDesignProposal (which requires PreMortem for dialectic balance), and DesignArchitect (which wields it). Compare with Falsification — PreMortem anticipates failure; Falsification tests current claims.

motivation.why_it_exists: Lists of work items need ordering. Prioritize names the impact-effort ranking discipline: score each on value and cost, sort by ratio. Without the named pattern, prioritization drifts to 'whatever feels urgent,' which optimizes for recency instead of value.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for serious work management. Every allocation primitive (Budget, ComputeBudget, ExploreExploit) consumes prioritization or equivalent. The Completeness invariant keeps priorities from silently dropping items.

usage.intended: Impact-Effort ranking — sort options by impact/effort ratio, work top-down.
usage.broad_contexts: product roadmap ordering, ticket triage, investment decisions, creative-project sequencing, home repairs prioritization.
usage.every_context_needs: option set, impact score, effort score, ratio computation, sort, periodic rescoring.
usage.varies: score granularity, re-score frequency, Pareto-80/20 awareness, dependency handling.

tensions: Impact estimation vs uncertainty — impact is a guess; effort is a guess; their ratio compounds the uncertainty.
Static ranking vs dynamic reordering — the invariant says re-score periodically, which is correct and unspecified-how-often.
Priority Inversion (named failure) — low-priority task blocks high-priority via resource dependency.
tradeoffs: Gains: principled ordering, impact-effort discipline, explicit periodic re-scoring.
Gives up: urgency responsiveness. Impact-effort is deliberately not urgency-weighted; genuinely urgent items can slip.
critique: Priority Inversion is a real failure — the pattern's ranking doesn't account for resource dependencies between items.
Impact and Effort are both guesses; the ratio compounds their errors.
No mechanism for handling ties — two items with equal ratios get arbitrary ordering.

Prioritize.family_discussion: Ordering primitive paired with Score (the evaluation substrate), Rank (the general operation), and Triage (the urgency-weighted variant). Compare with OptimalStop — Prioritize orders items; OptimalStop decides when to stop processing.

motivation.why_it_exists: Uncertainty is ubiquitous. Probability names the standard measure on [0,1] with normalization and additivity axioms. Without it, reasoning about uncertainty uses ad-hoc scales and loses the mathematical properties (additivity, bounds) that make Bayesian reasoning possible.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every probabilistic primitive (BayesUpdate, ConfidenceCalibrate, EpistemicCalibrate, BaseRateInclude) depends on Probability's Kolmogorov axioms. Remove it and the whole probabilistic-reasoning family loses its foundation.

usage.intended: likelihood measure on [0,1] — degree of belief or frequency of event.
usage.broad_contexts: risk assessment, Bayesian reasoning, frequentist statistics, ML confidence scores, betting-market prices, weather forecasts, medical probabilities.
usage.every_context_needs: `value: number` in [0,1] (principled range), belief-or-frequency interpretation.
usage.varies: subjective vs objective, sharp vs fuzzy, distribution-valued vs point.

tensions: Frequentist vs Bayesian interpretation — both fit the axioms; the pattern is agnostic, which is pragmatically useful and philosophically fence-sitting.
Additivity for mutually exclusive events vs dependent events — the invariant is strict; applying it incorrectly to dependent events is a classic error.
Probability as degree of belief vs frequency — the pattern mentions both; the two concepts share axioms but have very different operational semantics.
tradeoffs: Gains: standardized uncertainty measure, well-known axioms, substrate for Bayesian reasoning.
Gives up: richness. Probability is a single number; real uncertainty often has structure (distributions, intervals, second-order uncertainty) that this flattens.
critique: Very thin — three invariants, one-line mechanism. The real work lives in distributions and specific probabilistic models.
No failure modes listed; probabilistic reasoning has many (independence errors, sample bias, base-rate neglect, overconfidence).
The pattern doesn't distinguish single-event probability from distribution-over-values; both use the same primitive and have different semantics.

Probability.family_discussion: Foundational uncertainty primitive paired with BayesUpdate, BaseRateInclude, and Belief. Compare with Frequency — Probability is the abstract measure; Frequency is the observational sample.

motivation.why_it_exists: Passive observation may miss state that requires active query. Probe names the active interaction that extracts ground truth. Without the pattern, agents can't distinguish 'I observed X' from 'I probed and confirmed X,' which matters for trust.
motivation.removability: Removable in systems where all state is passively observable. Essential in systems where querying is the only access path. The Ground Truth invariant (probe reflects actual state) is the trust property.

usage.intended: active query returning verifiable information about system/environment state.
usage.future: any active "ask and get ground truth" mechanism.
usage.broad_contexts: health checks, TCP SYN probes, DNS queries, API status checks, sensor queries, LLM capability probing, test probes.
usage.every_context_needs: target to probe, active query semantic (not passive observation), verifiable response.
usage.varies: cost, latency, sandbox requirement (for stateful probes), retry on timeout, authentication.

tensions: Observer Effect (named failure) — probe changes the state it measures — is structural; the pattern can't avoid it.
Repeatability invariant vs real-world drift — same probe on unchanged state returns same result; in practice state changes between probes.
Cost Bound invariant vs deep probing — detailed probes cost more and may exceed budget.
tradeoffs: Gains: active ground-truth extraction, explicit observer-effect acknowledgment, cost bound.
Gives up: passivity. Probes interact with the target; for targets where interaction is destructive, Probe isn't usable.
critique: Observer Effect is endemic — every probe perturbs; the pattern has no mechanism for estimating perturbation.
Stale Probe (named failure) — result reflects past state — is the freshness problem.
False Positive/Negative is a generic failure mode and the pattern doesn't specify confidence reporting.

Probe.family_discussion: Active-observation primitive paired with Observe (passive), Witness (the attestation counterpart), and Experiment (the causal variant). Compare with Canary — Probe tests specific state; Canary tests full coordination path.

motivation.why_it_exists: Before you can solve, you have to name the gap. Problem names the formal representation of the gap between current state and desired state where inaction is costly. Without the pattern, 'problem' is ambiguous — sometimes task, sometimes situation, sometimes complaint.
motivation.removability: Non-removable as a descriptive primitive. Every solver consumes Problem or Task; the distinction (Problem is descriptive, Task is directive) is load-bearing. Remove Problem and the descriptive slot is filled by Task ambiguously.

usage.intended: formal state-gap where Cost of Inaction > 0 — descriptive claim about value loss.
usage.broad_contexts: bug reports, medical complaints, engineering defects, social issues, scientific puzzles, business challenges, philosophical problems.
usage.every_context_needs: current-state description, desired-state description, non-zero cost of inaction, distinction from Task (directive) and Goal (target).
usage.varies: specificity, urgency, actor/scope, root-cause status (symptom vs root).

tensions: Descriptive vs actionable — Problem is descriptive; agents naturally want to act, which blurs into Task.
Cost of Inaction > 0 — easy to assert, hard to quantify; non-zero framing rules out 'problems' with zero inaction cost (academic curiosity).
Current/Desired state specification — defining both precisely is often the hardest part, deferred to the caller.
tradeoffs: Gains: descriptive-vs-directive distinction, explicit gap framing, substrate for ProblemFramer.
Gives up: simplicity. Many contexts use 'problem' loosely; the pattern's formalism is more rigorous than casual use.
critique: No failure modes listed; Problem has some (mis-specification, over-formalization, state definition difficulty).
'Cost of Inaction > 0' is often asserted without quantification, making the invariant trivial.
Current/Desired state specification is the pattern's hard part and is deferred.

Problem.family_discussion: Foundational descriptive primitive paired with Task (directive), Goal (desired end state), and Gap (between states). Compare with FrameSpec — Problem is the raw descriptive; FrameSpec is the interpreted contract.

motivation.why_it_exists: Raw requests need interpretation before they can be solved. ProblemFramer names the specialized role that does this: interpret the request, construct AcceptSpec, anchor the RootSolver. Without the named role, framing is scattered across whoever happens to receive the request first.
motivation.removability: Removable in systems with pre-framed problems (narrow APIs, fixed schemas). Essential for open-ended work where framing is the hard part. The Genesis invariant (exactly one active Root per problem) is the uniqueness property.

usage.intended: specialized solver role — interpret request, construct AcceptSpec, anchor RootSolver to UniversalSolverTree.
usage.future: any "define the problem before solving" role.
usage.broad_contexts: product managers (as problem framers), researchers (writing the research question), policy advisors (problem definition), legal analysts (case framing), UX researchers.
usage.every_context_needs: request interpretation, AcceptSpec construction (Definition of Done), anchoring to parent structure, reframe request on invalid input.
usage.varies: framing rigor, collaboration level (solo vs with stakeholders), iteration count, rejection policy.

tensions: Framing quality vs speed — careful framing takes time; agents often want to rush to solving.
Genesis invariant vs parallel exploration — forbidding multiple active Roots per problem prevents parallel-framing experiments.
Bad Frame (named failure) — framing wrong makes the problem unsolvable; ProblemFramer is the role specifically tasked with getting this right.
tradeoffs: Gains: dedicated framing role, explicit AcceptSpec construction, root-ownership.
Gives up: lightweight problem handling. For small problems, the framer role is overhead.
critique: Reframe Failure (named failure) — can't find valid alternative after initial failure — is the pattern's dead-end.
The AcceptSpec construction is the hardest part and the pattern defers the quality issue.
Ownership of high-level success/failure is strong accountability; in practice accountability often spreads across multiple roles.

ProblemFramer.family_discussion: Role-pattern paired with FrameSpec (the artifact), RequestFraming (the verb), and RootSolver (the downstream anchor). Compare with DesignArchitect — ProblemFramer interprets requests; DesignArchitect produces design proposals. Different inputs, different outputs.

motivation.why_it_exists: Problems exist within a bounded region — constraints, initial state, valid solution domain. ProblemSpace names this region. Without it, 'the problem' includes everything imaginable, making solving intractable.
motivation.removability: Removable — callers can specify constraints without the named space. The pattern's value is the Boundedness and Consistency invariants that turn a vague 'problem' into a solver-consumable region.

usage.intended: bounded domain of a problem — region where solver operates.
usage.broad_contexts: search-space definitions, solver scope boundaries, research-project scope, design-space exploration, constraint-satisfaction domains.
usage.every_context_needs: constraints bounding the region, initial state, domain specification.
usage.varies: dimensionality, discreteness, explorability, enumerable vs continuous.

tensions: Boundedness (invariant) vs open-world problems — some problems genuinely don't have clean boundaries.
Consistency invariant (no contradictions) vs legitimate tensions — design problems often have productive contradictions.
Space definition vs solver autonomy — strict space constraints bind solvers; loose constraints give too much room.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit problem-region framing, solver-consumable definition.
Gives up: open-ended exploration. ProblemSpace is bounded; genuinely open problems need different framing.
critique: No failure modes listed; ProblemSpace has some (over-constraint, under-constraint, boundary errors).
Boundedness assumes constraints can be enumerated; real problems often reveal constraints during solving.
Consistency is aspirational; most rich problems have latent contradictions the solver must navigate.

ProblemSpace.family_discussion: Problem-representation primitive paired with Problem (the descriptive), FrameSpec (the interpreted contract), and Constraint (the boundaries). Compare with SolutionSpace — ProblemSpace is where the question lives; SolutionSpace is where answers live.

motivation.why_it_exists: Direct trust doesn't scale; trust via graph of verified promises does. PromiseGraph names this. Acyclic promise dependencies chain from verified leaves.
motivation.removability: Removable in fixed-trust settings. Essential in distributed multi-agent environments.

usage.intended: recursive trust dependencies as DAG — accept promise only if dependency graph provided.
usage.future: any "don't trust, verify the chain of trust" mechanism.
usage.broad_contexts: supply-chain integrity proofs, software-dependency-graph attestations, legal-chain-of-custody, certificate chains (PKI), federated reputation systems.
usage.every_context_needs: promise, dependency graph of sub-promises, leaf verification, cycle-prevention.
usage.varies: verification depth, credit-score alternative to full-verification, graph-update semantics.

tensions: Graph explosion (named failure) — verification overhead.
Acyclic invariant vs mutual commitments.
Leaf Verification anchoring — leaves must be trustworthy.
tradeoffs: Gains: scalable indirect trust.
Gives up: simplicity.
critique: Graph explosion is the scaling failure.
Acyclicity forbids legitimate mutual promises.
Leaf verification is the chain's weakest link.

PromiseGraph.family_discussion: Trust primitive paired with Sign, Witness, and Identity. Compare with Consensus — PromiseGraph is graph-based trust; Consensus is agreement-based.

motivation.why_it_exists: LLM input has specific structure (role tags, tool declarations, instruction vs content). Prompt names this distinct input unit. Without it, 'prompt' is ambiguous between 'any input' and 'the specific structured input to a generative model.'
motivation.removability: Non-removable in LLM-shaped systems. The pattern distinguishes structured LLM input from generic input. Every prompt-engineering and meta-prompting pattern consumes Prompt.

usage.intended: input text/instruction to a generative model.
usage.broad_contexts: LLM prompts, image-generation prompts, music-generation prompts, instruction-following dataset entries, meta-prompts.
usage.every_context_needs: input content, generator target.
usage.varies: structure (plain vs structured), length, role-tagging (system/user/assistant), tool-declaration attachments.

tensions: Prompt structure vs plain query — role tags and tool declarations add structure that many simple queries don't need.
Prompt as static vs prompt as dynamic — the pattern implies a structured unit; real prompts are often assembled on the fly.
Prompt length vs efficacy — longer prompts carry more context and more noise.
tradeoffs: Gains: named slot for LLM-specific structured input, role/tool substrate.
Gives up: generality. Prompt is LLM-shaped; non-LLM systems don't fit.
critique: No invariants listed — the pattern is almost purely descriptive.
No failure modes listed; prompting has many (injection, drift, overfit).
The pattern is thin because the interesting work (prompt engineering) is in specific patterns, not in the base.

Prompt.family_discussion: Foundational LLM-interface primitive paired with MetaPrompt (higher-order), ToolDeclaration (structured attachment), and Role (the tag). Compare with Message — Prompt is model-directed; Message is agent-directed.

motivation.why_this_layer: sequential LLM calls with validation — between stages
motivation.why_it_exists: Complex tasks don't always fit one LLM call. PromptChain names the fixed-sequence decomposition: each step's output is validated against AcceptSpec before feeding the next. Without the pattern, multi-call workflows blur between decomposition (PromptChain) and agent loops (with branching).
motivation.removability: Removable for single-call tasks. Essential for structured multi-step workflows where intermediate validation matters. The Halt on Error invariant and Schema Continuity are the chain-integrity properties.

usage.intended: fixed-sequence of LLM calls with AcceptSpec validation between steps.
usage.broad_contexts: LangChain-style sequential chains, multi-step LLM pipelines, editorial pipelines (write → edit → polish), research workflows.
usage.every_context_needs: sequence of LLM calls, AcceptSpec per edge, InputGuard + Retry per step.
usage.varies: chain length, per-step timeout, parallel chain branches, error handling.

tensions: Fixed sequence vs adaptive branching — PromptChain is linear; real tasks often need branches.
Halt on Error vs retry — strict halt prevents error propagation and loses recoverable errors.
Gate Brittleness (named failure) — valid intermediate outputs rejected by strict schemas — is the common production pain.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured decomposition, validated intermediate outputs, explicit sequence.
Gives up: flexibility and accuracy trade-off. More steps = more gate brittleness = more false rejections.
critique: Error Propagation (named failure) — step N failure corrupts N+1 — is structural unless Halt on Error fires early.
Gate Brittleness is endemic in strict-schema gates; calibrating them is constant rework.
Schema Continuity is a strong invariant; evolving schemas across chain versions is a known headache.

PromptChain.family_discussion: Workflow primitive paired with Chain (the substrate), AcceptSpec (the gate), and ChainOfThought (the cognitive analogue). Compare with Parallelize — PromptChain is serial; Parallelize is concurrent. Both decompose tasks, on different execution axes.

motivation.why_it_exists: Generating multiple possible futures from a proposed action surfaces consequences. ProphetFanOut names this descriptive-only future-generation. Without the pattern, futures get smeared with normative judgment.
motivation.removability: Removable — single-future prediction works. Essential for EthicalReasoningProtocol's descriptive-normative separation.

usage.intended: high-fanout causal simulation across branching timelines.
usage.future: any multi-timeline exploration with bias toward low-probability tails.
usage.broad_contexts: Monte Carlo simulation, scenario planning, risk analysis, red-teaming (adversarial timelines), decision-tree evaluation, robust-outcome analysis.
usage.every_context_needs: branch generator, timeline cost function, tail-exploration bias (unlike standard chain-of-thought which follows likely paths).
usage.varies: fanout breadth, pruning policy, aggregation method, tail-weighting strategy.

tensions: Descriptive Only (invariant) vs subtle normative framing.
Diversity invariant vs coherent futures.
Fan-out explosion (named failure) — too many irrelevant futures.
tradeoffs: Gains: diverse future-space exploration.
Gives up: compute.
critique: Descriptive-Only is hard to enforce; framing alone carries normative weight.
Fan-out explosion is the scaling issue.
Diversity threshold is unspecified.

ProphetFanOut.family_discussion: Prediction primitive paired with EthicalReasoningProtocol (consumer), Simulation (substrate), and NormCheck (the filter that catches normative leak).

motivation.why_it_exists: Two-stage consensus: reality-check (will this work?) before desirability-vote (should we do it?). PropheticQuorum names this. Without the pattern, reality and preference blur.
motivation.removability: Removable — single-vote quorum works. PropheticQuorum is specifically the reality-vote-first discipline.

usage.intended: two-stage consensus — align predictions first, then align values.
usage.future: any "shared reality then shared value" coordination pattern.
usage.broad_contexts: scientific consensus, policy debate (predicted-consequences-first), multi-agent predictions, organizational planning, investment committee alignment.
usage.every_context_needs: prediction phase (agents simulate), prediction-match check, value phase (agents vote on desirability), halt-on-divergence.
usage.varies: prediction verification method, divergence threshold, model-alignment protocol on halt, weighting of predictions vs values.

tensions: Model divergence (named failure) — agents can't agree on reality.
High compute cost (named failure) — N simulations.
Prediction Precedence invariant vs democratic principle.
tradeoffs: Gains: reality-grounded consensus.
Gives up: speed and compute.
critique: Model divergence is endemic — diverse models disagree.
High cost limits scalability.
No mitigation for reality-deadlock.

PropheticQuorum.family_discussion: Consensus primitive paired with Quorum, Consensus, and Simulation. Compare with Vote — PropheticQuorum adds reality-check; Vote is preference-only.

motivation.why_it_exists: Suggested actions or transitions need formal representation. Proposal names the message suggesting a specific act with 'what' and 'why.' Without it, suggestions are free-form and lose the decision-making structure.
motivation.removability: Removable — suggestions can be informal. Proposal earns its weight in structured decision processes where the 'what' and 'why' must be reviewable. The Clarity invariant (unambiguous action) is the review-ability property.

usage.intended: formal message suggesting a specific Act or Transition.
usage.broad_contexts: legislative proposals, academic proposals, business proposals, PR (pull requests), RFC (Request for Comment), design proposals.
usage.every_context_needs: what is being proposed, why (rationale), target decision-making process.
usage.varies: approval mechanism, amendment semantics, sponsor identity, urgency.

tensions: Clarity invariant vs exploratory suggestions — structured proposals discourage half-formed ideas.
Formal message format vs informal suggestions — some contexts benefit from structured; others (early ideation) are hurt.
Proposal as payload vs proposal as claim — the pattern frames it as payload for decisions; it's also often a rhetorical claim.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured suggestion, explicit 'what' and 'why,' reviewable form.
Gives up: ideation speed. Every proposal pays the structuring tax; for brainstorming this is overhead.
critique: Very thin — one invariant, one-sentence mechanism.
No failure modes listed; proposals have many (vague 'why,' conflicting 'what,' missing scope).
Clarity is aspirational; proposals are often ambiguous in ways that only reveal during discussion.

Proposal.family_discussion: Formal-message primitive paired with Message (the generic), Decision (the consumer), and Vote/Consensus (the decision-making mechanisms). Compare with MechanisticDesignProposal — Proposal is generic; MechanisticDesignProposal has specific structure for design.

motivation.why_it_exists: In long contexts and deep recursion, agents lose track of where they are — which parent task, current stack, active tool. Proprioception names the self-monitoring ping: periodic context verification. Without it, agents 'get lost' in their own work.
motivation.removability: Removable for short-session agents. Essential in long-running or deeply-recursive agent systems. The invariants (Context Continuity, Liveness, State Recovery) are the self-awareness properties.

usage.intended: self-location awareness within the task graph — "where am I in the recursion?"
usage.broad_contexts: long-agent-session coherence, recursion-depth tracking, context-state awareness, multi-tool state management, long-running-process dashboards.
usage.every_context_needs: position tracking, state verification, depth-in-recursion measurement.
usage.varies: ping frequency, what's tracked (context, tool state, depth), integration with somatic_marker, fatigue detection.

tensions: Ping frequency vs overhead — frequent self-checks are safe and expensive; sparse checks lose sight of drift.
Hallucinated Context (named failure) — stack trace doesn't match reality — is the core failure the pattern defends against.
Stagnation (named failure) — same node > N ticks — is detected by the pattern without specifying response.
tradeoffs: Gains: agent self-awareness, stack-trace verification, explicit liveness check.
Gives up: compute. Proprioception adds periodic overhead; for tight inner loops this is significant.
critique: Orphaned (named failure) — parent task unresponsive — is real and the pattern doesn't specify recovery.
Hallucinated Context is the hardest failure; detecting mismatch requires comparing internal state to environmental reality, which the pattern assumes is possible.

Stagnation threshold N is caller-set with no default rule. Failure modes were previously jammed into one list entry (Stagnation + Orphaned + Hallucinated Context run together); now split into three distinct entries.

Proprioception.family_discussion: Self-monitoring primitive paired with Heartbeat (general liveness), ContextFirst (refresh discipline), and AuditTrail (the log substrate). Compare with Monitor — Proprioception is self-directed; Monitor is target-directed. Both are observation patterns, directed inward vs outward.

motivation.why_it_exists: The output artifact of prototyping — feasibility evidence as low-fidelity trace/model. ProtoPack names it.
motivation.removability: Removable by folding into Artifact. The specific feasibility-evidence framing earns its weight.

usage.intended: prototype verification artifact — low-fidelity Prototype + simulation trace.
usage.broad_contexts: engineering proof-of-concept artifacts, startup MVP documentation, pitch-deck traction slides, research feasibility studies.
usage.every_context_needs: prototype reference, simulation trace or model, feasibility evidence.
usage.varies: fidelity level, evidence depth, reviewer audience.
notes: §3.12 flagged ProtoPack for phantom signature — mechanism has no composes_with backing its signature. Broad-use confirms this should be a plain Verb, not a polymorphic dispatcher.

tensions: Feasibility Proof invariant vs low-fidelity assumption.
Low Fidelity invariant vs Hidden Complexity failure.
Evidence strength vs cost.
tradeoffs: Gains: prototype artifact typing.
Gives up: little.
critique: No failure modes listed.
Two invariants pull in opposite directions (prove feasibility, stay low-fidelity).
Distinction from general Prototype is subtle.

ProtoPack.family_discussion: Prototype output paired with Prototype (the concept), Build (the act), and SimulationTrace.

motivation.why_this_layer: communication-standard spec — a rules+formats artifact; one agent can read without any counterparty
motivation.why_it_exists: Inter-agent communication needs rules and formats. Protocol names the defined rule-set. Without it, communication is ad-hoc and agents can't reliably interoperate.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in multi-agent systems. Every coordination primitive depends on protocol semantics. The pattern itself is thin because the interesting work lives in specific protocols; the base class just names the category.

usage.intended: defined set of rules and formats for communication between agents.
usage.future: any "how we talk to each other" specification.
usage.broad_contexts: HTTP, gRPC, SMTP, diplomatic protocols, scientific-paper protocols, ceremonial protocols, medical protocols, agent-communication protocols (FIPA, ACL).
usage.every_context_needs: rule set, format specification, inter-agent applicability.
usage.varies: formality, versioning, backward compatibility, machine-readable vs human-readable.

tensions: Version Drift (named failure) — agents with incompatible versions — is structural in evolving systems.
Ambiguous Spec (named failure) — rules with multiple interpretations — is the dominant protocol bug.
Evolution vs stability — protocols legitimately evolve and backward-compat is often broken.
tradeoffs: Gains: shared communication vocabulary, explicit rules.
Gives up: very little — protocol primitive is near-unavoidable.
critique: Very thin — one-line mechanism, two failure modes, no invariants.
Version Drift is acknowledged without a version-negotiation pattern.
The pattern doesn't specify what a protocol contains (message formats, state machines, acceptance rules); all deferred.

Protocol.family_discussion: Foundational communication primitive paired with Message (the unit), Handshake (the initiation), and specific protocols (Greet, Delegate, AgentProtocol). Compare with Contract — Protocol is communication rules; Contract is obligations.

motivation.why_it_exists: Full-production builds cost too much for initial learning. Prototype names the early sample: low-fidelity, disposable, built to test a concept. Without the pattern, 'prototype' blurs with 'draft' or 'early version,' losing the disposability that makes prototyping useful.
motivation.removability: Very thin — one-line mechanism, no invariants. Could be folded into Draft or Sketch. The pattern's value is in the explicit 'disposable' framing that permits cheap learning.

usage.intended: early sample/model built to test a concept, low-fidelity and disposable.
usage.broad_contexts: software prototypes, scientific prototypes, product prototypes, design prototypes, educational mock-ups, proof-of-concepts.
usage.every_context_needs: low-fidelity construction, concept-testing purpose, disposability semantic.
usage.varies: fidelity level, concept specificity, feedback-capture mechanism, iteration budget.

tensions: Low-fidelity vs representative — prototypes must be cheap and representative enough to learn from; the balance is judgment.
Disposable in principle vs kept in practice — prototypes often become production through inertia.
'Learned from' — the value of a prototype is the learning; prototypes that produce no new learning are waste.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit cheap-learning slot, disposability framing.
Gives up: almost nothing — thin primitive with no controversial claims.
critique: Almost a stub — one-sentence mechanism, no invariants, no failure modes.
Disposability is aspirational; most prototypes outlive their intended lifespan.
Conflates prototype-as-demo with prototype-as-learning; these have different design trade-offs.

Prototype.family_discussion: Early-learning primitive paired with Build (the act), Canary (the probe), and Sketch (similar approximate shape). Compare with MVP — Prototype is for learning, MVP is for real use; both are 'minimal' but different purposes.

motivation.why_it_exists: Work items need an ordered container with explicit discipline — FIFO, LIFO, or Priority. Queue names this. Without a named primitive, ordering discipline gets smeared across callers who reinvent it poorly.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every orchestrator, messaging system, and event-handling pattern uses Queue or equivalent. The explicit ordering discipline (FIFO/LIFO/Priority) is what makes Queue predictable rather than arbitrary.

usage.intended: ordered task/message buffer with FIFO or Priority ordering.
usage.broad_contexts: job queues, message queues, call queues, emergency-room triage queues, print queues, network queues.
usage.every_context_needs: ordering discipline (FIFO/Priority), enqueue, dequeue, explicit order semantic distinct from Stream.
usage.varies: priority function, boundedness, persistence, concurrent access semantics.

tensions: Single-discipline queue vs multi-discipline needs — real systems often want different orderings for different queue contexts.
Priority queue vs fairness — priority ordering can starve low-priority items.
Producer/consumer asymmetry — producers enqueue, consumers dequeue; backpressure isn't specified.
tradeoffs: Gains: shared ordering vocabulary, explicit discipline, producer/consumer semantics.
Gives up: flexibility. Queue commits to one discipline per queue; mixed-discipline needs require multiple queues.
critique: No failure modes listed; queues have many (overflow, starvation, priority inversion).
No backpressure semantics — producers can enqueue faster than consumers dequeue, and the pattern doesn't specify what happens.
Single discipline per queue is right for clarity and forces callers to manage mixed orderings across multiple queues.

Queue.family_discussion: Foundational container primitive paired with Stack (LIFO variant), EventQueue (event-specific), and Priority (the ordering criterion). Compare with Sequence — Queue is accessible from ends; Sequence is random-access ordered.

motivation.why_it_exists: Threshold-checking as a named primitive — count N ballots, check against K. Different from Consensus (which is the agreement property) and Vote (which is the protocol): Quorum is the counting primitive. Used by many patterns that need 'enough support' without caring about the full Vote protocol.
motivation.removability: No. Every multi-party-agreement pattern uses Quorum as the gating function. Collapsing into Vote would couple the counting primitive to the voting protocol; callers using Quorum for non-vote thresholds (PropheticQuorum, PropheticFanOut) would be forced into inappropriate dependencies.

usage.intended: threshold-checking primitive — count Ballot signals vs K threshold.
usage.broad_contexts: consensus protocols, board meetings, blockchain block validation, Byzantine fault tolerance, emergency-decision quorum.
usage.every_context_needs: participant count, threshold K, yes/no return.
usage.varies: K value, weighted vs equal votes, timeout integration.

tensions: K-cannot-decrease invariant vs rule changes: locking K mid-vote is the named invariant. But some protocols legitimately want to change rules between votes — the pattern is strict.
Threshold tuning as caller concern: named failure mode 'too low enables cheap blocking, too high makes it useless.' Quorum doesn't help set the threshold.
Binary threshold vs graded support: Quorum is yes/no (≥K). Graded-support patterns (weighted voting, reputation-scored ballots) need different primitives.
tradeoffs: Simple count-and-compare buys clarity at the cost of excluding weighted schemes.
K-immutability buys integrity at the cost of forbidding legitimate threshold adjustment.
Infrastructure-layer placement (rather than Society) is correct — counting is mechanical — at the cost of making the Society patterns that use Quorum feel 'exposed' to an Infrastructure dependency.
critique: One invariant, two failure modes. Missing: Non-negative K (K must be ≥ 0), Participant Uniqueness (a single agent's multiple ballots shouldn't double-count).
Strategic Abstention as a failure is real but the pattern has no mitigation — abstention management is a Vote/Ballot concern.
The pattern is described as 'simply counts' — but counting depends on what counts (eligibility, uniqueness). These are not in Quorum's spec.

Quorum.family_discussion: The threshold-checking primitive in Infrastructure. Used by `Vote`, `Consensus`, `LatticeCommit`, `Rally`, `PropheticQuorum`. Pairs with `Ballot` (what is counted) — Quorum is the gate, Ballot is the unit.

motivation.why_it_exists: State transitions only fire when local signal density crosses threshold. QuorumPulse names this density-triggered action. Without the pattern, transitions fire on individual signals.
motivation.removability: Removable — individual signals can trigger. QuorumPulse is density-based alternative.

usage.intended: fluid synchronization via signal density — state transitions trigger on density > threshold.
usage.future: any density-based distributed sync (no global clock).
usage.broad_contexts: distributed systems without clock sync, biological rhythm synchronization (fireflies), crowd behavior thresholds, fashion tipping points, viral-content threshold dynamics.
usage.every_context_needs: heartbeat signals, density measurement, threshold trigger, state-transition semantics.
usage.varies: density metric, threshold adaptation, node-count awareness.

tensions: Signal saturation (named failure) — too many pulses.
Echo chambers (named failure) — signals amplify within subgroups.
Pulse frequency tuning.
tradeoffs: Gains: density-based triggers, quorum discipline.
Gives up: individual-signal responsiveness.
critique: Saturation and echo chambers are real failures.
Threshold is caller-set.
No specified echo chamber mitigation.

QuorumPulse.family_discussion: Signal primitive paired with Heartbeat, Quorum, and Pulse.

motivation.why_it_exists: Ad-hoc group formation protocol — broadcast requirement, collect enlists, commit if quorum met. Named pattern for 'form a team on demand' — distinct from static organizational structures. Essential for emergent coordination in dynamic agent populations.
motivation.removability: Probably retain. Dynamic group formation is common enough (task-specific coalitions, emergent committees) that a shared protocol beats ad-hoc reimplementation.

usage.intended: ad-hoc multi-party coordination via call-and-response.
usage.broad_contexts: emergency response, crowdsourcing, swarm coordination, federated computation, multi-agent task assignment, protest organizing, flash mobs, distributed consensus invocation.
usage.every_context_needs: broadcast mechanism, AcceptSpec criteria, deadline, quorum threshold, selection method on enlistees.
usage.varies: `max_participants` (2 to 100K+), authentication requirements, cancellation semantics, reward structures, reputation weighting, geographic scope.

tensions: Atomic abort vs partial team: if quorum not met, Rally fails entirely. Some use cases want partial teams — pattern is strict.
Shared ContextID vs context negotiation: Binding invariant requires a shared ContextID, but context itself may need negotiation — the pattern assumes a single static context.
