tensions: Singleton vs distributed: Singleton per tree is a strong invariant. In distributed deployments (multiple trees federated) the root may not exist as a single physical node — the pattern's answer is that 'tree' is a logical construct; federation lives at a higher layer.

Ultimate accountability vs delegation: RootSolver 'owns the final success/failure' but execution happens in children. The accountability-without-execution structure is standard in hierarchy but creates blame-attribution ambiguity when a child silently fails.

Reframe authority as monopoly: Only the RootSolver can reframe. That prevents mid-tree re-framing chaos but also concentrates reframing cost at the root — a deep child that discovers the frame is wrong must bubble a FrameError all the way up.
tradeoffs: Unique entry buys aggregate visibility (Pathway Memory sees all problems) at the cost of a single point of coordination — RootSolver's state is the tree's state.
Four unique authorities (Framing, Budget, Accountability, Reframe) centralize decision power at the cost of flexibility — intermediate nodes cannot reallocate or re-frame.
Cascading budget allocation is principled (children inherit from parent) but rigid — reallocation requires going up to the root, which is slow.
critique: Bad Frame is the headline failure mode but the pattern does not specify how the Root is supposed to know its frame is bad without cascading failures reaching it. The detection protocol is implicit in the FrameError mechanism — the RootSolver itself does not describe how it consumes FrameErrors.

Pathway Memory is named as the compounding site but the learning mechanism is not specified in this pattern — it lives in PathwayMemory. Readers learning about RootSolver in isolation don't see how the learning actually works.

'Ultimate Accountability' is a governance concept, not an operational one — the pattern doesn't say what accountability means in code. A failed root task returns a failed Solution; whether anyone acts on that accountability is outside the pattern.

RootSolver.family_discussion: The apex of every `UniversalSolverTree`. Specialization of `PolymorphicSolver` with singleton-per-tree semantics. Anchors `PathwayMemory` for compounding routing knowledge. Pairs with `ProblemFramer` (the framing tool) and `ComputeBudget` (allocation unit). The only node with `Reframe` authority and the only recipient of FrameErrors that cascade all the way up.

motivation.why_it_exists: N-way classifier dispatch as a named primitive. Every mixture-of-experts, query router, model cascade, and tool dispatcher needs the structure 'inspect input, pick handler, forward.' Route pins the contract so the classifier logic, the handler set, and the dispatch rule are all first-class.
motivation.removability: No. Route is referenced widely across the library (dispatching Solvers, query routers, multi-model pipelines). Collapsing it into repeated Branches would work mathematically but destroys readability and loses the 'best-fit handler' invariant.

usage.intended: classify input and direct to specialized handler.
usage.broad_contexts: HTTP routing, load balancing, query type routing, message brokers, intent-classification dispatch, model-selection routing, multi-head attention.
usage.every_context_needs: input to classify, classification function, dispatch table (input type → handler).
usage.varies: classification method (rules, ML, heuristics), routing-table representation, fallback handling, cost-aware dispatch.

tensions: Deterministic routing vs learned routing: the mechanism mentions 'configurable dispatch rules' but also 'type tags, metadata, token weight' — the latter invites learning (PathwayMemory-driven). Route is neutral; learning variants live as descendants.

No-dropped-requests invariant vs strict dispatch: 'No dropped requests' says every input goes somewhere. But 'Ambiguous Classification' is a named failure — if nothing matches, what happens? The pattern implies a default handler but doesn't require one.
Classifier cost vs dispatch efficiency: if the classifier becomes slower than direct handling (named failure: Routing Bottleneck), Route is anti-economic. The pattern has no built-in cost budget.
tradeoffs: Typed dispatch buys separation of concerns at the cost of classifier complexity.
'No dropped requests' buys coverage guarantee at the cost of forcing a catch-all — which may not exist for some routing configurations.
Extensible dispatch rules buy flexibility at the cost of reasoning difficulty — complex rule sets become opaque.
critique: Two invariants are weak for a pattern this central. Missing: Terminal (every route leads to a handler that itself terminates); Mutually-Reachable (every handler is reachable from some input, else it is dead code); Non-Looping (Route doesn't route back to itself).
'Best-fit handler' is the intent but the pattern doesn't specify how best-fit is measured. Descendants encode this (rule-based, ML-based, learned), but the parent should at least name the concern.
The three failure modes are good but miss: Routing Drift (classifier trained on old distribution keeps dispatching under shifted distribution) — common in practice.

Route.family_discussion: The N-way case in the flow-control family. Sibling to `Branch` (2-way fork), `Gate` (conditional halt), `Chain` (sequential). Often composed with `PathwayMemory` at dispatching solvers for learning-based route selection.

motivation.why_it_exists: Constraints and invariants that form a validity boundary need structured collection. RuleSet names it, distinct from mutable Policy or social Constitution. Without the distinction, 'rules' blurs between immutable validity, mutable policy, and social norm.
motivation.removability: Removable by folding into Constraint or Policy. RuleSet earns its weight as the immutable-validity-boundary slot — the thing you check against that doesn't change during validation.

usage.intended: immutable collection of Constraints and invariants defining validity boundary.
usage.broad_contexts: legal statutes, game rules, firewall rules, validation rulesets, grammar specifications, policy rulesets.
usage.every_context_needs: structured collection, immutability, validity-boundary definition.
usage.varies: rule count, rule-interaction semantics, conflict resolution, version binding.

tensions: Immutability vs legitimate evolution — rule sets are immutable per instance; evolution means new versions.
Structured collection vs simple list — RuleSet is structured but the structure is under-specified.
Validity boundary vs decision making — RuleSet defines validity; decisions use it but aren't defined by it.
tradeoffs: Gains: named immutable validity substrate, distinction from mutable policy.
Gives up: evolution flexibility. Immutable rule sets require versioning for change.
critique: Very thin mechanism; no invariants or failure modes listed.
Distinction from Policy is asserted but not enforced structurally.
Structured collection — the structure is up to the caller.

RuleSet.family_discussion: Validity-substrate primitive paired with Constraint (the atomic rule), Validate (the check), and Policy (mutable counterpart). Compare with Constitution — RuleSet is immutable validation; Constitution is social governance.

motivation.why_it_exists: Before committing an expensive payload, send a cheap probe expecting to fail — but design the failure to teach. SacrificialProbe names this reconnaissance-via-cheap-failure move. Without it, main payloads fly blind.
motivation.removability: Removable when probes aren't economical. Essential in domains where the main operation is expensive and failure is informative (exploration, adversarial scouting). The Cost Asymmetry invariant is the economic discipline.

usage.intended: cheap, instructive failure — send a low-cost probe designed to fail informatively.
usage.broad_contexts: startup landing-page tests, military recon (deliberately expendable), A/B test cheap variants, dendritic cells in immunology, canary deployments (analogous), reconnaissance-in-force.
usage.every_context_needs: probe cost << main payload cost, instructive-failure-mode design, strategy update on failure signal.
usage.varies: probe-main cost ratio, failure-mode taxonomy, update rule, number of probes before committing.

tensions: Probe too expensive (named failure) — breaks cost asymmetry.
Probe failure is silent (named failure) — the probe fails but the agent doesn't see it.
Instructive Failure — the probe must fail informatively, which requires design effort.
tradeoffs: Gains: cheap pre-commit reconnaissance, parameter update via probe results.
Gives up: time. SacrificialProbes add a round-trip before main action.
critique: Silent probe failure defeats the purpose; the pattern requires observable failure.
Cost Asymmetry is caller-tuned.

Designing instructive failure is itself work the pattern defers. Failure modes were previously jammed (probe-too-expensive AND silent-failure combined in one entry); now split into two atomic entries.

SacrificialProbe.family_discussion: Reconnaissance primitive paired with Canary (similar expendable-agent probe), Probe (active query), and SafeFailure (graceful). Compare with Probe — SacrificialProbe expects failure; Probe expects answer.

motivation.why_it_exists: Executing untrusted code needs isolation boundary. Sandbox names the restricted-side-effects environment. Without it, untrusted code runs with host privileges, which is catastrophic.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in any system that executes untrusted or agent-generated code. The pattern is thin; specific sandbox implementations (AgentSandbox, container, VM) specialize it.

usage.intended: isolation boundary restricting side effects.
usage.broad_contexts: OS sandboxes (gVisor, Firecracker), browser sandboxes, test fixtures, simulation environments, experimental workspaces, regulatory sandboxes (fintech).
usage.every_context_needs: isolation boundary, side-effect restriction, controlled exit/escape.
usage.varies: isolation strength (syscall filter vs container vs VM), resource limits, network restrictions, persistence.

tensions: Unconstrained vector (named failure) — escape from isolation — is the adversarial concern.
Resource exhaustion (named failure) — within sandbox affects enclosing — requires quotas the pattern doesn't specify.
Isolation strictness vs functionality — stricter sandboxes are safer and more limiting.
tradeoffs: Gains: restricted side-effects, isolation boundary.
Gives up: performance. Sandbox overhead is real for every contained execution.
critique: Very thin — one sentence of mechanism, two failure modes.
Escape vectors are legion; the pattern names the category without cataloguing specific vectors.
Resource exhaustion within sandbox affecting enclosing is a real issue (shared kernel, I/O, etc.).

Sandbox.family_discussion: Foundational isolation primitive paired with AgentSandbox (agent-specific), Permission (what's allowed), and Quota (resource bound). Compare with Bubble — Sandbox is execution isolation; Bubble is transactional coordination isolation.

motivation.why_it_exists: Optimization takes forever; sometimes 'good enough' beats 'best.' Satisfice names the threshold-acceptance move: set minimum criteria, take first option meeting them. Without the pattern, 'good enough' is implicit and threshold drifts during search.
motivation.removability: Removable — callers can satisfice without the named pattern. The invariant 'Threshold cannot change mid-search' is the key discipline. Remove it and Threshold Drift becomes the default.

usage.intended: optimize for speed via threshold acceptance (first candidate meeting all minimums).
usage.broad_contexts: bounded rationality decisions, MVP product sizing, hiring decisions (first acceptable candidate), quick-return search, time-boxed optimization, sequential-choice selection.
usage.every_context_needs: minimum-acceptable criteria per dimension, sequential evaluation, accept-first-match semantic.
usage.varies: criteria strictness, evaluation order, fallback if no candidate meets criteria, recall allowance.

tensions: Threshold Drift (named failure) — lowering standards to force a match — is the dominant failure.
Satisfice vs optimize — the two produce different answers; picking the right mode is itself judgment.
First acceptable vs best acceptable — Satisfice takes first; 'best above threshold' is a different mode.
tradeoffs: Gains: speed over optimality, cognitive cost reduction.
Gives up: optimality. Satisfice deliberately stops short of best.
critique: Threshold Drift is endemic — agents unconsciously relax criteria when the search drags on.
Threshold setting is upfront and often arbitrary.
No handling for zero-match scenarios — what if no option meets threshold?

Satisfice.family_discussion: Decision primitive paired with Optimize (the alternative), OptimalStop (the stopping counterpart), and Prioritize (the ordering). Compare with Compromise — Satisfice is single-agent acceptance; Compromise is multi-agent dampening.

motivation.why_it_exists: Open-ended tasks accumulate requirements indefinitely. ScopeFreeze names the discrete T_freeze point — after it, AcceptSpec and Goal become immutable. Without the pattern, 'one more thing' becomes the death spiral (named Feature Creep).
motivation.removability: Removable in settings where scope is naturally bounded. Essential for any project with risk of scope drift. The Rejection invariant (new SubTasks must serve existing goals) is the discipline.

usage.intended: phase transition control — after T_freeze, AcceptSpec + Goal become immutable.
usage.future: any "lock the requirements to prevent scope creep" discipline.
usage.broad_contexts: sprint scope freezes, academic thesis-topic freezes, contract-term freezes, product-spec freezes, regulatory-submission freezes.
usage.every_context_needs: T_freeze point, immutability post-freeze, Backlog-movement for new requirements.
usage.varies: unfreeze mechanism (override, exception), backlog integration, stakeholder-approval for unfreeze.

tensions: Feature Creep (named failure) — 'nice to have' sub-tasks during closing.
Perfectionism Spiral (named failure) — continuous AcceptSpec refinement.
Immutability vs legitimate late discoveries — some requirements emerge post-freeze and are worth addressing.
tradeoffs: Gains: bounded task scope, explicit freeze point, clear close-phase semantics.
Gives up: adaptability. Post-freeze legitimate discoveries must wait for v2.
critique: Feature Creep is endemic; ScopeFreeze names the failure and requires discipline to resist.
Perfectionism Spiral is the AcceptSpec-refinement version of the same failure.
Immutability is strong; real projects sometimes warrant post-freeze changes for critical discoveries.

ScopeFreeze.family_discussion: Project-discipline primitive paired with AcceptSpec (what gets frozen), Goal (the other frozen item), and ManifestPlanning (which happens before freeze). Compare with CommitmentDevice — ScopeFreeze freezes scope; CommitmentDevice freezes actions.

motivation.why_it_exists: Evaluations produce numbers on defined scales. Score names the quantified evaluation unit. Without it, 'rating,' 'scoring,' and 'evaluation' blur and the numerical-scale aspect is implicit.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every evaluation-consuming pattern (Rank, Judge, ParetoFront) uses Score. The pattern is thin by design; the real work is in the specific scoring functions.

usage.intended: a quantitative evaluation result.
usage.broad_contexts: model eval metrics, fitness scores, relevance ranks, aesthetic ratings, adversarial judgments, risk scores, trust scores, quality scores.
usage.every_context_needs: `value: number` (obvious), `normalized_range: [min, max]` (otherwise 0.7 is ambiguous — out of 1 or 10 or 100?), `metric_id: string` (otherwise "what was scored?" is unclear). All three are usability floor.
usage.varies: precision, confidence interval, temporal decay, weighting vectors, multi-axis decomposition.
usage.extensions: `NormalizedScore` (range locked to [0,1]), `RawScore` (unbounded numeric), `WeightedScore` (adds axis weights), `TimeAdjustedScore` (adds decay).

tensions: Numerical scale vs qualitative property — Score quantifies, losing qualitative nuance.
Single value vs multidimensional — Score is scalar; multi-axis evaluations need aggregation.
Defined scale vs comparability — scales are defined per-score; cross-score comparison requires normalization.
tradeoffs: Gains: quantified evaluation, comparability within a scale.
Gives up: qualitative richness. Score flattens evaluation to a number.
critique: Very thin — one-line mechanism, no invariants, no failure modes.
Scale definition is deferred; cross-comparison of scores from different scales is a common bug.
Single-value flattening loses information; multi-dimensional evaluations need Metric or ParetoFront.

Score.family_discussion: Foundational evaluation primitive paired with Metric (the measured property), Judge (scalar evaluator), and Assessment (structured feedback). Compare with Rank — Score is the value; Rank orders by score.

motivation.why_it_exists: Scoring logic should be a first-class passable unit, not a closure baked into callers. ScoringFunction names it: deterministic input-to-scalar mapping. Without the pattern, scoring logic is repeated across callers.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Rank, Score, Judge all consume ScoringFunction. The Determinism and Range invariants are the uniformity properties.

usage.intended: deterministic logic mapping input artifact → scalar Score.
usage.broad_contexts: ML loss functions, game score functions, aesthetic evaluators, risk scoring, fitness functions, relevance rankers, judging rubrics.
usage.every_context_needs: deterministic mapping, input artifact, scalar Score output.
usage.varies: function complexity, gradient availability, multi-objective aggregation, context-sensitivity.

tensions: Determinism invariant vs stochastic scoring — some scoring is legitimately probabilistic.
Range invariant (bounded or unbounded) is under-specified — which callers need bounded?
Scoring function as Noun vs as closure — the pattern makes it a first-class citizen, which helps composability and adds ceremony.
tradeoffs: Gains: passable scoring logic, deterministic + range invariants.
Gives up: closure expressiveness. First-class ScoringFunctions are more constrained than arbitrary closures.
critique: Very thin — two invariants, one-line mechanism.
Range invariant is either-or; the pattern doesn't distinguish the two cases' use.
No failure modes listed; scoring has many (miscalibrated range, wrong signal direction).

ScoringFunction.family_discussion: Foundational primitive paired with Score (the output), Rank (the consumer), and Criteria (the evaluation standards). Compare with Predicate — ScoringFunction produces scalar; Predicate produces boolean.

motivation.why_it_exists: Multi-step reasoning needs working memory distinct from final output. Scratchpad names this intermediate-calculation region. Without the pattern, intermediate reasoning leaks into final output or gets lost between steps.
motivation.removability: Removable in single-step reasoning. Essential for multi-step agent reasoning where intermediate work must be preserved. The Separation invariant (distinct from final output) is the core discipline.

usage.intended: working-memory region for intermediate reasoning steps.
usage.broad_contexts: chain-of-thought traces, calculator tape, draft-before-publish workspaces, LLM inner monologue, debugging print statements, analyst workings, creative sketching.
usage.every_context_needs: isolation from main output, writability by the agent, persistence across the reasoning session.
usage.varies: size limit, eviction policy, inspectability by others (debug vs fully hidden), persistence after session ends, encryption.

tensions: Bounded size vs complex reasoning — the size invariant limits reasoning depth.
Persistence across steps vs state bloat — survival-across-steps invariant means state accumulates.
Scratchpad Leak (named failure) — working notes in user-facing output — is the canonical privacy/quality failure.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit working memory, separation from output, intra-task persistence.
Gives up: simplicity. Scratchpad adds a concept; for simple reasoning, the extra structure is overhead.
critique: Scratchpad Leak is the dominant failure — notes for yourself get sent to users.
Memory Overflow (named failure) — unbounded growth — requires size enforcement the invariant asserts but can't enforce.
Persistence across steps is useful and a source of state-contamination bugs.

Scratchpad.family_discussion: Cognitive-workspace primitive paired with Context (the broader memory), Think (the operation using scratchpad), and ChainOfThought (reasoning substrate). Compare with Cache — Scratchpad is short-lived working memory; Cache is keyed storage for reuse.

motivation.why_it_exists: Locating entities in a domain by criteria is a foundational operation. Search names it. Without the pattern, search logic gets reinvented per domain; the Determinism and Completeness invariants distinguish principled search from ad-hoc scanning.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every information-retrieval pattern (Discover, PatternDiscovery, RetrievalAugment) uses Search. The pattern is thin because specific search types specialize.

usage.intended: active scanning of a domain to locate matching entities.
usage.future: any "find matches" operation over a domain.
usage.broad_contexts: text search, code search, vector-embedding search, graph search, file-system search, inventory search, database queries.
usage.every_context_needs: domain, criteria, iteration mechanism, Check-based filtering.
usage.varies: domain type (memory, environment, data), indexing strategy, ranking, parallelism, real-time vs batch.

tensions: Completeness (no silent skips) vs efficiency — exhaustive search scales badly.
Determinism vs parallel execution — same domain+criteria = same results requires consistent ordering.
Criteria expressiveness vs performance — rich criteria are powerful and slow.
tradeoffs: Gains: deterministic retrieval, complete-by-invariant scanning.
Gives up: performance. Complete search is expensive; approximate search is faster and silently incomplete.
critique: Very thin — two invariants, one-line mechanism.
No failure modes listed; search has many (partial results, missed items, wrong criteria).
Determinism invariant is violated by any ordering-dependent search; in practice 'same results' often means 'same set' not 'same order.'

Search.family_discussion: Foundational retrieval primitive paired with Discover (distributed variant), Check (the filter), and Criteria (the query). Compare with BeamSearch — Search is single-target; BeamSearch is multi-path exploration.

motivation.why_it_exists: Filtering a set by predicate is foundational. Select names the deterministic filter with predicate truth and subset invariants. Without it, filter logic is ad-hoc.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every filtering operation (Rank top-K, PatternDiscovery threshold, InvariantFilter) uses Select. The invariants are set-theoretic foundations.

usage.intended: deterministic filter — apply predicate P(x) to every element, return subset.
usage.broad_contexts: SQL WHERE, array.filter, set-theoretic filtering, query results, search results, decision making from options.
usage.every_context_needs: input set, predicate function, subset output.
usage.varies: predicate complexity, short-circuit semantics, ordering preservation, cost estimation.

tensions: Empty Result (named failure) — no items satisfy — is structural and often legitimate.
Predicate Error (named failure) — criterion throws — needs error handling.
Determinism vs stateful predicates — predicates that reference mutable state break determinism.
tradeoffs: Gains: set-theoretic filter with clean invariants.
Gives up: little — thin primitive that's near-unavoidable.
critique: Predicate Error handling is unspecified — does the whole Select fail, or is the element skipped?
Determinism relies on predicate determinism, which the pattern doesn't verify.
Very thin; specific filtering patterns add the domain-specific work.

Select.family_discussion: Foundational set operation paired with Rank (ordering), Search (retrieval), and Filter (synonym). Compare with Check — Select filters, Check evaluates; both apply predicates but for different outcomes.

motivation.why_it_exists: LLM output has variance; single samples can be wrong. SelfConsistency names the N-sample majority-aggregation technique. Without the pattern, variance gets absorbed or ignored.
motivation.removability: Removable when single-sample is good enough or when cost matters more than accuracy. The pattern is a compute-for-accuracy trade that's well-established in 2024 LLM practice.

usage.intended: variance-reduction — sample N reasoning chains independently, select by majority.
usage.future: any ensemble-reasoning technique using mode selection.
usage.broad_contexts: LLM inference ensembling, Monte Carlo decision procedures, majority-vote diagnosis, robust forecasting, jury trials (analogy), replication studies.
usage.every_context_needs: multiple independent runs, aggregation by mode, majority-select final answer.
usage.varies: sample count, independence mechanism, tiebreaker, weighted vs unweighted mode.

tensions: Consistent Wrongness (named failure) — all N samples share the same error — is the correlated-error failure.
Cost Explosion (named failure) — N× compute — is the obvious tradeoff.
Independence invariant vs efficiency — generating samples independently costs; shared prefixes help but violate strict independence.
tradeoffs: Gains: variance reduction, principled aggregation.
Gives up: cost. N samples = N× cost for 1 final answer.
critique: Consistent Wrongness is structural — samples from the same model share biases.
N >= 3 is a floor without specifying how high; 3 is often too few for meaningful convergence.
Cost Explosion is acknowledged without mitigation; callers decide whether to pay.

SelfConsistency.family_discussion: Variance-reduction primitive paired with Parallelize (Voting mode), Aggregate (the final step), and Think (the sampled operation). Compare with PerspectiveEnsemble — SelfConsistency varies via temperature; PerspectiveEnsemble varies via persona.

motivation.why_it_exists: Constraints stated once get forgotten in long contexts. SelfReminder names the repeated-reminder technique: restate constraints before each user turn. Without it, prompt injection and drift erode the model's adherence.
motivation.removability: Removable in short interactions. Essential for long-running or adversarial contexts. The pattern is the 2024-2025 standard 'system prompt reinforcement' technique.

usage.intended: inject persistent Trace of core identity into prompt context before each response.
usage.future: any "stay grounded in your principles" periodic reminder.
usage.broad_contexts: LLM jailbreak mitigation, organizational values reminders, morning affirmations, meeting charters repeated, recurring safety briefings.
usage.every_context_needs: core-identity text, persistent injection into context, pre-response timing.
usage.varies: content verbosity, injection frequency, update policy.

tensions: Context Dilution (named failure) — long convos push reminder out of effective window.
Brittleness (named failure) — sophisticated attacks bypass.
Token Overhead (named failure) — repeated reminders consume context.
tradeoffs: Gains: sustained constraint adherence, explicit reinforcement.
Gives up: context budget and sometimes fluency. Heavy reminders distract from user content.
critique: Context Dilution is the structural failure — reminders lose effect as context grows.
Brittleness is real — determined attackers craft prompts that bypass static reminders.
Token Overhead is the visible cost; the pattern names it without specifying a budget.

SelfReminder.family_discussion: Alignment primitive paired with DeliberativeAlign (the broader constitutional pattern), SystemPrompt (the substrate), and ConstraintFirst (generation-time enforcement). Compare with InputGuard — SelfReminder is model-side; InputGuard is boundary-side.

motivation.why_it_exists: When agents stuck on the same approach, listing those approaches as forbidden forces exploration of alternatives. SemanticTabu names this: tabu list of existing mechanisms, solve without them. Without the pattern, stuck-ness continues.
motivation.removability: Removable — callers can restrict their own solutions. SemanticTabu is the explicit ideation-escape move; it specifically forbids known solutions to force novelty.

usage.intended: constraint-based novelty enforcement — forbid existing mechanisms to force latent pathways.
usage.future: any "can't use X, find another way" creativity-forcing constraint.
usage.broad_contexts: constrained writing (no letter 'e'), constraint-based creative prompts (Oblique Strategies), research-domain constraints, pedagogical "solve without using Y", competitive constraints.
usage.every_context_needs: tabu list, enforcement mechanism, creativity-forcing semantic.
usage.varies: tabu-list scope, enforcement strictness, swarm-wide (trace) vs individual.

tensions: Constraint Satisfaction (invariant: Output ∩ Tabu == Ø) vs paralysis — if Tabu covers everything, no solution exists.
Explicit Avoidance (reasoning must cite what's avoided) vs natural flow — the requirement is discipline that slows reasoning.
Tabu list completeness — missed items slip through as 'novel.'
tradeoffs: Gains: forced exploration of non-obvious solutions.
Gives up: efficiency. Often the tabu'd solution was the best one.
critique: Paralysis (the named failure) is structural when the Tabu list covers the available solution space.
Constraint Satisfaction invariant treats partial avoidance as full, which may not match intent.
The pattern assumes the Tabu list is honest; gaming the list is easy.

SemanticTabu.family_discussion: Ideation primitive paired with Invert (the opposition move), LateralOptimization (domain shift), and NoiseInjection (escape loops). Compare with Creative — SemanticTabu forbids known; Creative encourages unknown. Different paths to novelty.

motivation.why_it_exists: Ordered execution — A then B, output of A available to B — is the foundational control-flow pattern. Sequence names it. Without the pattern, ordering is implicit in syntactic layout.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every imperative workflow uses Sequence. The pattern is deliberately thin; the value is the named handle for the most basic control-flow concept.

usage.intended: ordered execution — A then B, output of A available to B (temporal ordering).
usage.broad_contexts: workflow sequences, execution pipelines, causal chains, musical sequences, protocol sequences.
usage.every_context_needs: ordered execution, output-flow-forward semantic, temporal (not spatial) ordering.
usage.varies: strict vs relaxed ordering, parallelism inside a Sequence step, pause/resume semantics.

tensions: Sequential vs parallel — Sequence forces order where parallelism would be valid.
Output availability vs streaming — A's full output available before B starts; streaming breaks this.
Error propagation — A failing means B shouldn't start; semantics unspecified.
tradeoffs: Gains: simple ordering, deterministic data flow.
Gives up: parallelism opportunities.
critique: Almost a stub — one-sentence mechanism, no invariants, no failure modes.
Output handoff semantics are unspecified.
Error propagation deferred to caller.

Sequence.family_discussion: Foundational control-flow primitive paired with Parallel (the counterpart) and Chain (the composed version). Compare with Loop — Sequence is once; Loop is repetitive.

motivation.why_it_exists: Distributing a resource across multiple nodes needs deterministic partitioning. Shard names it — unlike Decompose (which is cognitive) Shard is data-distribution. Without the pattern, distribution is ad-hoc and routing loses determinism.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in distributed data systems. The pattern is imported from database/big-data practice. The invariants (Conservation, Disjointness, Determinism) are the correctness properties.

usage.intended: deterministic partitioning of state/resource/vector into disjoint subsets by key.
usage.broad_contexts: database sharding, distributed computation, memory partitioning, workforce sharding, IP-range sharding, geographic sharding.
usage.every_context_needs: partitioning key, disjoint output subsets, determinism.
usage.varies: key function, rebalancing policy, replication, fault tolerance.

tensions: Fixed shard count vs elastic scaling — the pattern implies fixed; rebalancing needs re-sharding.
Determinism vs hot-spot avoidance — deterministic key routing creates hot spots if keys are skewed.
Disjointness vs replication — disjoint shards don't replicate; replication is a separate concern.
tradeoffs: Gains: deterministic distribution, conservation, clean partitioning.
Gives up: flexibility. Sharding locks in a partition; resharding is expensive.
critique: No failure modes listed; sharding has many (hot spots, resharding costs, cross-shard transactions).
Deterministic routing creates hot spots when access is skewed.
Cross-shard operations aren't addressed; joins across shards are hard.

Shard.family_discussion: Foundational distribution primitive paired with Partition (the general concept), Distribute (the act), and Replicate (the redundancy counterpart). Compare with Decompose — Shard is data; Decompose is cognition.

motivation.why_it_exists: Discovery is public; coordination is private. ShoutWhisper names this two-phase protocol: broadcast intent, then encrypted P2P.
motivation.removability: Removable — full-encryption or full-broadcast systems work. ShoutWhisper optimizes for both phases.

usage.intended: dual-mode communication — broadcast high-level intent, switch to encrypted P2P for coordination.
usage.future: any "discover publicly, coordinate privately" communication pattern.
usage.broad_contexts: BitTorrent tracker + swarm, dating app match + DM, public forums → DM channels, conference discovery → side conversations, gossip protocols with private channels.
usage.every_context_needs: broadcast-for-discovery, switch-to-private-channel, encryption for the private phase.
usage.varies: broadcast channel specifics, switching protocol, encryption strength, scalability.

tensions: Metadata leakage (named failure) — Shout phase exposes.
Amplitude Check vs privacy — broadcast is visible.
Privacy Check — Whisper encryption, but metadata already leaked.
tradeoffs: Gains: discovery + private coordination.
Gives up: full privacy. Metadata leaks during Shout.
critique: Metadata leakage is the known failure — who's shouting, about what, is public.
The two-phase commit is clean and has its own complexity.
Amplitude 90% threshold is a default.

ShoutWhisper.family_discussion: Two-phase coordination paired with Discover (the Shout step), Handshake, and Encrypt. Compare with OntologyHandshake — ShoutWhisper is discovery+coord; OntologyHandshake is term negotiation.

motivation.why_it_exists: Attaching verifiable identity proof to an artifact creates non-repudiable authorship/approval. Sign names this cryptographic commitment. Without it, authorship claims are soft.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in any system that cares about authorship or approval. Every Contract, Award, OathBind, Witness depends on Sign. The Non-Repudiation and Integrity invariants are the cryptographic guarantees.

usage.intended: attach a verifiable identity proof to an artifact.
usage.broad_contexts: cryptographic signatures, handwritten signatures, OAuth token signing, PGP email, code signing, document notarization, blockchain transactions, wet signatures on paper.
usage.every_context_needs: identity proof, artifact to attach to, non-repudiable link.
usage.varies: algorithm (RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, wet), key material, verification protocol, attachment format (detached vs embedded).

tensions: Non-Repudiation vs legitimate retraction — signed commitments are permanent, even if you change your mind.
Integrity invariant (signature invalidates on change) vs minor edits — typo fixes invalidate the signature.
Public-key infrastructure dependency — Sign requires PKI, which has its own failure modes.
tradeoffs: Gains: non-repudiable authorship, integrity guarantees.
Gives up: flexibility. Signed artifacts are frozen; any edit invalidates.
critique: Non-Repudiation is technical non-repudiation; legal non-repudiation has separate requirements.
Key compromise isn't addressed; a stolen key produces valid signatures.
No failure modes listed; real signing has many (revoked keys, expired certs, PKI failures).

Sign.family_discussion: Cryptographic primitive paired with Hash (the substrate), Witness (the attestation counterpart), and Identity (the signer). Compare with OathBind — Sign attaches identity to artifact; OathBind binds actor to rule set.

motivation.why_it_exists: Fire-and-forget broadcast — no guaranteed recipient. Signal names the most basic emission. Without it, 'broadcast' and 'send' blur, and the guarantee (or lack thereof) is implicit.
motivation.removability: Non-removable as a foundational communication primitive. Stigmergy, Resonate, and various emit-style patterns use Signal. The Broadcast and Information invariants distinguish Signal from addressed Message.

usage.intended: raw information emission — fire-and-forget with no guaranteed recipient.
usage.broad_contexts: pub/sub signals, OS signals (SIGTERM etc), broadcast messages, neural firing (biological analogy), distress beacons, emissions into an environment.
usage.every_context_needs: emission mechanism, no guaranteed delivery, environment as medium.
usage.varies: carrier medium, reach, reliability tiers, filtering.

tensions: Fire-and-forget vs reliability — no delivery guarantee is the whole point and often a bug.
Information (invariant: distinguishes from noise) vs signal-to-noise reality — not all 'signals' are informative.
No recipient vs inferred recipient — unaddressed signals often have implicit audiences.
tradeoffs: Gains: cheap emission, broadcast semantics.
Gives up: reliability. No delivery guarantee; Message or handshake provides more.
critique: Very thin mechanism.
No failure modes listed; signals have many (lost, unheard, ignored).
The Information invariant is aspirational; real emissions are often noise-like.

Signal.family_discussion: Foundational communication primitive paired with Message (addressed), Broadcast (general term), and Emission (synonym). Compare with Event — Signal is emission; Event is state-change. Different communication substrates.

motivation.why_it_exists: Proving message receipt requires computationally non-trivial reflection. SignalReflection names this — more than a hash, a transformation that requires actual processing.
motivation.removability: Removable in trust-rich settings. Essential for adversarial verification.

usage.intended: proof of receipt via non-trivial transformation — prove active processing, not just echo.
usage.future: any "prove you're live and paying attention" acknowledgment.
usage.broad_contexts: proof-of-liveness in distributed systems, CAPTCHA-like work proofs, bot-detection challenges, attention-cost pricing, anti-replay protocols.
usage.every_context_needs: original message, non-trivial transformation, computational-work proof, liveness demonstration.
usage.varies: transformation difficulty, verification method, adversarial resistance, bandwidth cost.

tensions: Asymmetry (named failure) — too expensive for receiver.
Source authentication via reflection.
Reflection transformation — must be verifiable.
tradeoffs: Gains: stronger receipt proof than hash.
Gives up: cost.
critique: Asymmetry is the dominant failure mode.
Transformation choice is caller-dependent.
Verification of reflection requires matching the transformation.

SignalReflection.family_discussion: Proof primitive paired with Hash (cheaper), Sign (authorship), and Witness (attestation).

motivation.why_it_exists: Sometimes the right output is no output. Silence names active abstention — deliberately withholding signal, distinguishable from 'processing.' Without the pattern, silence and processing blur and agents can't signal 'intentionally nothing.'
motivation.removability: Very thin — one invariant. Could be folded into general timeout handling. The distinction from Processing is the pattern's value; remove it and silence becomes ambiguous.

usage.intended: active waiting — deliberately withhold signal output for duration T or until Trigger.
usage.broad_contexts: deliberation pauses, meditation silence, awkward-silence in negotiation, LLM "no response" modes, quiet-time policies, moment-of-silence ritual.
usage.every_context_needs: duration or trigger, deliberate-withholding semantic, distinction from "processing" (active thinking).
usage.varies: duration, trigger type, observability (others know you're silent vs not), breakable vs unbreakable.

tensions: Timeout invariant — silence must have a cap; unlimited silence is ambiguous.
Active abstention vs passive non-response — the pattern wants explicit, but non-response is the natural default.
Default action after timeout — unspecified, left to caller.
tradeoffs: Gains: named active-abstention slot.
Gives up: little.
critique: Very thin.
No failure modes — silence can fail in many ways (interpreted as rejection, missed by observers).
Default action after MaxDuration is caller-dependent without guidance.

Silence.family_discussion: Communication primitive paired with Signal (emission), Defer (postponement with preservation), and Abstain. Used by LatentWander (during offline processing).

motivation.why_it_exists: Testing actions in the real world is expensive and often irreversible. Simulation names the sandboxed execution: fork world, execute, discard. Without it, 'try it and see' has real-world consequences.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every predictive pattern (MentalSim, CognitiveEcho, ExtendedThinking with simulation) depends on it. The Isolation invariant — side effects don't leak — is the safety property.

usage.intended: sandboxed execution — fork world state, execute, discard, return outcome.
usage.broad_contexts: physics sims, software test fixtures, game sandboxes, multi-agent training environments, digital twins, Monte Carlo rollouts, counterfactual experimentation.
usage.every_context_needs: world state fork, isolated execution, outcome capture, original state preservation.
usage.varies: fork fidelity (shallow vs deep), execution time-bound, outcome richness, fork cost.

tensions: Isolation vs fidelity — truly isolated simulations diverge from reality; high-fidelity simulations risk leaking.
Fork cost vs compute budget — forking complex world state is expensive.
Simulation doesn't capture everything — hidden state not in W isn't simulated.
tradeoffs: Gains: sandboxed experimentation, no real-world side effects.
Gives up: fidelity. Simulation always diverges from reality in some way.
critique: Isolation is the key invariant and hard to guarantee; external resources (APIs, I/O) are often reached by simulated code.
Fork of world state assumes world is forkable — many real systems resist full snapshot.
No failure modes listed; simulation has many (divergence, leak, cost).

Simulation.family_discussion: Foundational predictive primitive paired with AgentSandbox (agent-specific), MentalSim (agent-reasoning variant), and Prediction (the output). Compare with Experiment — Simulation is isolated; Experiment is in reality.

motivation.why_it_exists: Before irreversible action, step-through simulation in scratchpad reveals bad outcomes. SimulationTrace names this pre-action rehearsal. Without it, irreversible actions fire without preview.
motivation.removability: Removable for reversible actions. Essential for irreversible ones. The Causality and Replayability invariants make the trace auditable.

usage.intended: pre-execution mental model — simulate step-by-step before irreversible action.
usage.broad_contexts: chess-move forethought, pre-deploy dry-runs, legal simulation of outcomes, architect walkthrough, mental simulation of arguments before confrontation.
usage.every_context_needs: proposed action, step-by-step simulation, predicted-state inspection, abort-on-bad-state semantic.
usage.varies: simulation depth, scratchpad medium, rollback cost, immutable-record requirement.

tensions: Simulation inaccuracy (named failure) — 'the map is not the territory' — is the structural limit.
Step-by-step granularity vs coarse simulation — finer is more accurate and more expensive.
Immutable after creation vs mid-simulation revision — invariant forbids editing traces.
tradeoffs: Gains: pre-action outcome preview, replayable for audit.
Gives up: speed. Every irreversible action pays the trace tax.
critique: Map-vs-territory is fundamental; the trace is as accurate as the simulation model.
Replayability is strong invariant; random/probabilistic simulations don't satisfy it.
Causality invariant doesn't prevent causal-chain errors, just asserts the trace shape.

SimulationTrace.family_discussion: Pre-action primitive paired with Simulation (the substrate), Scratchpad (the working memory), and ReversibilityCheck (the gate). Compare with PreMortem — SimulationTrace is forward prediction; PreMortem is backward failure-analysis.

motivation.why_it_exists: Long sequential reasoning is slow. Skeleton names the generate-outline-first-then-expand-in-parallel approach. Without the pattern, reasoning is serial and misses parallelism opportunities.
motivation.removability: Removable — serial reasoning always works. Skeleton is a specific latency optimization for LLM generation. The Independence invariant is what permits parallel expansion.

usage.intended: parallel outline-first topology — skeletal outline, then parallel point expansion.
usage.broad_contexts: SkeletonOfThought reasoning, document outlining, research paper structures, code scaffolding, project structure templates.
usage.every_context_needs: outline structure, parallel expansion capability, latency-optimization semantic.
usage.varies: outline depth, parallelism width, expansion-quality thresholds.

tensions: Independence invariant vs genuine interdependence — if points depend on each other, Skeleton fails silently or produces incoherent output.
Latency over depth — the pattern trades depth for speed.
Outline quality vs expansion quality — a bad outline produces bad expansions even if each expansion is good.
tradeoffs: Gains: latency reduction via parallel expansion.
Gives up: coherent deep reasoning. Independence constraint rules out reasoning that legitimately chains.
critique: No failure modes listed.
Independence is hard to verify — outlines often have hidden dependencies.
Final coherence depends on outline structure, which the pattern doesn't specify how to produce.

Skeleton.family_discussion: Parallel-reasoning primitive paired with SkeletonOfThought (the canonical implementation), Decompose (the outline generator), and Parallelize (the execution substrate). Compare with ChainOfThought — Skeleton is parallel; ChainOfThought is serial.

motivation.why_it_exists: The canonical implementation of parallel reasoning via Skeleton topology. SkeletonOfThought names the full pattern: decompose into outline, expand all points in parallel, assemble. Without the pattern, parallel reasoning is ad-hoc.
motivation.removability: Removable — Skeleton covers the general idea. SkeletonOfThought is the specific implementation pattern with completeness, independence, and coherent-assembly invariants.

usage.intended: macro for Think(Skeleton) — generate outline first, expand all points in parallel.
usage.broad_contexts: parallel LLM reasoning, documentation generation, essay writing, project planning (outline then parallel-fill), scientific literature review synthesis.
usage.every_context_needs: skeleton generation (outline/structure), parallel expansion of points, aggregation.
usage.varies: skeleton depth, parallelism degree, convergence criteria.

tensions: Structural Completeness — outline covers all required aspects — is an aspiration, not a testable property.
Point Independence vs coherent output — independent expansion risks discontinuity at assembly.
Coherent Assembly — the hardest part, unspecified.
tradeoffs: Gains: parallel reasoning with structure, explicit invariants for completeness/independence/coherence.
Gives up: sequential depth. Can't build on previous points' results.
critique: Coherent Assembly is the hard part and is deferred.
Completeness is aspirational — real outlines miss things.
Independence is often violated quietly; the pattern has no detection mechanism.

SkeletonOfThought.family_discussion: Parallel-reasoning pattern paired with Skeleton (the topology), Decompose (the outline step), and ChainOfThought (the serial counterpart). Compare with GraphOfThought — SkeletonOfThought is parallel-flat; GraphOfThought is DAG-structured.

motivation.why_it_exists: State at a specific time can be captured as an immutable record. Snapshot names this. Without it, backup/restore/checkpoint/replay all reinvent the 'state at time T' concept.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for systems with checkpointing or time-travel debugging. The pattern is thin; the real work (serialization, storage, restoration) lives in dependent patterns.

usage.intended: static immutable record of state at a specific time.
usage.broad_contexts: database snapshots, filesystem snapshots, VM snapshots, Git commits (as snapshots), legal-record snapshots, scientific-measurement snapshots.
usage.every_context_needs: immutability, timestamp binding, state capture.
usage.varies: completeness (full vs delta), storage, restore semantics, encryption.

tensions: Serialization Gap (named failure) — in-memory state that can't be serialized.
Corruption (named failure) — hash matches but data unreadable.
Staleness (named failure) — restoring from logically-stale snapshot.
tradeoffs: Gains: immutable state record, foundation for backup/restore/debugging.
Gives up: storage. Snapshots grow; retention is a separate concern.
critique: All three named failure modes are real and unmitigated by the pattern.
Very thin mechanism — one sentence, no invariants.
No restore semantics specified.
`_meta.related` reference updated from legacy stub format to full sema_id.

Snapshot.family_discussion: State primitive paired with Restore (the recovery), AuditTrail (continuous counterpart), and Versioning. Compare with Cache — Snapshot is full state at time; Cache is keyed storage.

motivation.why_it_exists: Ambiguous user requests produce wrong answers. SocraticLoop names the clarifying-question loop: when confidence is low, ask the user. Without it, agents guess or confabulate.
motivation.removability: Removable for crisp-request settings. Essential for open-ended user interaction. The Information Gain and Diminishing Returns invariants are the discipline that prevents endless questioning.

usage.intended: ambiguity-detection loop querying the user until intent disambiguated.
usage.future: any "ask clarifying questions until clear" interaction.
usage.broad_contexts: onboarding conversations, requirements elicitation, medical history-taking, detective interrogation, pedagogical dialogue, therapeutic questioning.
usage.every_context_needs: confidence threshold, user query mechanism, loop termination on disambiguation or max_questions.
usage.varies: question-generation strategy, max-questions bound, tone/pacing, fallback if user unable to answer.

tensions: User Fatigue (named failure) — too many questions drive users away.
Premature Stop (named failure) — accepting vague answers without full clarification.
Information Gain invariant — each question must reduce entropy — is hard to verify.
tradeoffs: Gains: disambiguated intent, user-driven clarification.
Gives up: UX smoothness. Every question is friction.
critique: Diminishing Returns invariant is hard to operationalize — measuring entropy delta from LLM output is non-trivial.
User Fatigue is the dominant failure in practice.
Termination conditions (Confidence threshold or max_questions) need tuning.

SocraticLoop.family_discussion: Clarification primitive paired with Understand (the goal), Interpret (the substrate), and HumanApprove (the human-in-loop counterpart). Compare with SelfReminder — SocraticLoop clarifies upstream; SelfReminder constrains downstream.

motivation.why_it_exists: The paired output type for Task — every Solver yields a Solution, so the library has a single shared handle for 'the artifact produced by execution, with provenance and recursive sub-solution structure.' Without Solution, each Solver family would invent its own output shape and the (Task, Solution) transaction boundary would fragment.
motivation.removability: No. Solution is the yields-type in the Solver contract and the recursion substrate for sub-solutions (children in the solver tree). Removing would break every Solver's output typing and the auditability property (Provenance signatures, Chain of Custody).

usage.intended: verifiable output container for a Task — provenance + artifact + sub-solution tree.
usage.broad_contexts: solver outputs, problem-solving workflows, scientific findings, engineering solutions, legal rulings, medical treatments.
usage.every_context_needs: output artifact, provenance (creator, time), component tree (sub-solutions used), acceptance-criteria validation.
usage.varies: fidelity level, provenance detail, storage medium, query-ability.

tensions: Immutability vs evolution: Once finalized, Solution is frozen. But long-running solvers may want to refine or stream partial outputs. The spec accepts this as a boundary — refinement becomes a new Solution with `derived_from` lineage, not in-place mutation.

Recursive structure vs caller simplicity: Solution carries a Component tree of sub-solutions. For callers that only want the final artifact, the tree is overhead. For callers that audit provenance, it is essential.

Creator identity: Provenance requires cryptographic signing by the Creator. That commits the library to an identity model (signing keys) the Solver contract itself does not define — the anchor lives outside the pattern.
tradeoffs: Provenance + signature buy auditability at the cost of a key infrastructure. Solvers operating in unsigned environments must stub the signature field or bypass the invariant.
Immutability buys referenceability (a Solution's hash can be cited forever) at the cost of expressivity for streaming or incremental outputs.
Sub-solution tree preserves composition history but inflates Solution size — a deep tree carries every ancestor's sub-artifacts.
critique: 'Finalized' is the trigger for Immutability but is not explicitly defined as a state transition — the spec does not say who flips it, when, or whether an un-finalized Solution is a valid partial artifact.
Traceability invariant requires cryptographic signing by Creator but does not specify the signature scheme, key lifecycle, or revocation semantics. These live outside the pattern.

Schema Violation is listed as a failure mode but the acceptance-criteria-check is implicit in the Task type; the pattern doesn't say whether Solution validation is the Solver's responsibility or the caller's.

Solution.family_discussion: Output half of the (Task, Solution) transaction. Every Solver yields a Solution typed against the Task's acceptance criteria. `FrameError` is the alternative yield when a hard seam triggers restructuring rather than production. `PerformanceSignal` is the Feedback-surface signal that attaches to Solution for downstream learning (Pathway Memory).

motivation.why_it_exists: A single shared handle for 'a thing that takes a Task and produces a Solution via the five-surface contract' — lets the library state polymorphism over agents, pipelines, tools, LLM calls, humans, and hybrid compositions. Without Solver the library has no canonical word for the execution unit, and the fractal intelligence architecture cannot be described without re-inventing the interface under each specialization.
motivation.removability: No. Solver is the root of the solver family (`PolymorphicSolver`, `OptimisticSolver`, `RigorousSolver`, `RootSolver`, plus the per-descriptor convention `DiagnosticSolver`, `PlanningSolver`, etc.). The FractalIntelligence paper's recursive composition depends on it. Removing means re-declaring the five-surface contract under every descendant — exactly what the pattern exists to prevent.

usage.intended: abstract transformer of Task to Solution; root of the solver family.
usage.future: any process conforming to the Task→Solution contract — LLM calls, human workers, distributed agents, composite pipelines, MCP tools, code interpreters, manual workflows.
usage.broad_contexts: above.
usage.every_context_needs: accepts a typed Task; exposes the five-surface contract (Manifest, Execute, Consult, Verify, Feedback) with Manifest+Execute mandatory.
usage.varies: cognitive mode, rigor level, execution substrate, budget discipline, feedback shape.

tensions: Interface vs class: the mechanism calls Solver 'an interface, not a class,' but agents accumulate role state over their lifetime. The library's answer — roles are transient — is a discipline, not an enforced property.

Five surfaces vs two mandatory: Manifest and Execute are required; Consult/Verify/Feedback are 'strongly recommended' but optional. A compliant two-surface Solver still honors the spec but forfeits most of the assurance hooks the contract was designed to provide.

Agent/Solver separation: Agent and Solver are distinct types, related by 'any agent can take on a Solver role.' The library chose role-as-protocol over role-as-subtype; some descendants would compose more cleanly under the latter.
tradeoffs: Polymorphism buys substrate-agnostic composition (swap LLM for human without changing the call site) at the cost of per-call-site trust — the caller has to rely on contract compliance rather than enforce it.
Five surfaces give rich coordination hooks but most implementations use only two, leaving Verify and Feedback un-wired — no upstream assurance signals when they are skipped.
Recursion enables the solver tree but makes error propagation harder — a FrameError from a deep child must bubble up through every parent's Feedback surface to become actionable at the root.
critique: No invariants or failure modes listed. Surprising for the root of an entire family. Candidates missing: Contract Integrity (all declared surfaces must be callable); Input/Output Typing (accepts Task, yields Solution); Recursion Safety (child solvers accept the same Task interface as the parent exposes).
The mechanism text is rich but does not name what happens when a Solver fails. Feedback emits a FrameError in practice, but that is not in the pattern's failure_modes.
'The same agent can wear many solver roles simultaneously' has no conflict-resolution story. Two roles with contradictory Manifests on the same agent — which wins?

Solver.family_discussion: The library's central verb-pattern. `PolymorphicSolver` is the concrete five-surface implementer; `OptimisticSolver` and `RigorousSolver` specialize on rigor; `RootSolver` is the apex triage node with Pathway Memory. `UniversalSolverTree` is the topology produced by Solver recursion. `Task` and `Solution` are the input/output types Solver types against; `AcceptSpec`, `FrameError`, `PerformanceSignal` wire the Verify/Feedback surfaces.

motivation.why_this_layer: typed declaration of solver identity+capabilities — data artifact
motivation.why_it_exists: A solver's static identity and capabilities need a typed declaration. SolverManifest names it — name, competencies, tools, cost. Without the pattern, solver capabilities are implicit and hard to discover.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for solver coordination. The pattern is what PatternDiscovery and compatibility-checking consume. The Accuracy, Completeness, Immutability invariants are the truth-in-advertising properties.

usage.intended: typed declaration of solver's identity and capabilities.
usage.future: any capability-declaration artifact for runtime selection.
usage.broad_contexts: agent capability cards, MCP tool manifests, microservice descriptors, LLM model cards, job applications (capability declaration), restaurant menus (as capability declaration).
usage.every_context_needs: Name/ID, Competencies, Tool Access, Cost Model, Constraints.
usage.varies: verification of claims, update frequency, discoverability, trust model.

tensions: Capability Inflation (named failure) — manifest claims more than reality.
Stale Manifest (named failure) — doesn't reflect current state.
Missing Constraint (named failure) — omits critical limitations.
tradeoffs: Gains: typed solver capability declaration, discoverable and auditable.
Gives up: flexibility. Immutable manifests require version updates for evolution.
critique: Capability Inflation is endemic — solvers optimize for being chosen.
Stale Manifests age as solvers evolve; versioning discipline is under-specified.
Accuracy is aspirational; real manifests routinely misrepresent.

SolverManifest.family_discussion: Static counterpart of SolverNode paired with Card (the general capability advertisement), and PatternDiscovery (the consumer). Compare with AcceptSpec — SolverManifest describes the solver; AcceptSpec describes the task's criteria.

motivation.why_it_exists: A runtime unit that holds state, tracks budget, communicates with parent/children. SolverNode names it — the living instance of a SolverManifest. Without the pattern, the distinction between static solver capability (Manifest) and runtime solver instance (Node) blurs.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every SolverTree consists of SolverNodes; the pattern is foundational. The invariants (Statefulness, Linkage, Accountability) are the runtime properties.

usage.intended: stateful container wrapping a SolverManifest with dynamic state.
usage.broad_contexts: LLM agent instances, workflow engine tasks, ML training runs, research project instances, experiment executions.
usage.every_context_needs: static manifest reference, dynamic state (partial solution, budget, status), parent-node communication, blame-attribution semantic.
usage.varies: state schema, persistence, checkpointing, resumability, state migration.

tensions: Statefulness vs stateless solvers — strictly stateful complicates stateless-solver integration.
Linkage invariant (parent/children pointers) vs solver autonomy — forced linkage prevents standalone solving.
Accountability — failures traceable — adds audit ceremony.
tradeoffs: Gains: runtime solver state, hierarchical traceability, budget tracking.
Gives up: stateless simplicity. SolverNodes carry state; stateless patterns fit awkwardly.
critique: No failure modes listed; runtime nodes have many (stale status, broken links, budget leaks).
Linkage assumes tree-shaped solver structure; graph-shaped solvers don't fit.
Accountability is asserted without specifying blame mechanisms.

SolverNode.family_discussion: Foundational solver-runtime primitive paired with SolverManifest (the static declaration), SolverTree (the structure), and Task (the work).

motivation.why_it_exists: Multiple SolverNodes must organize into a coordinated topology for solving a task. SolverTree names this command structure — budget flows down, results flow up. Without it, solver coordination is unstructured.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for composite solving. PolymorphicSolver, RootSolver, and UniversalSolverTree all instantiate SolverTree. The Budget Flow and Connectivity invariants are the structural discipline.

usage.intended: active hierarchy of coordinated solver instances — the command topology.
usage.future: any multi-solver organization for a task.
usage.broad_contexts: solver delegation trees, nested LLM agents, divide-and-conquer workflows, map-reduce problem decomposition, agent swarms, research team hierarchies.
usage.every_context_needs: root solver, child-solver relationships (delegation edges), reporting edges upward, origin (tree-like at decomposition time per §3.14 update).
usage.varies: runtime shape (tree, DAG with fan-in, DAG with deduplication); budget cascade policy; failure handling; authority model.

tensions: Acyclicity invariant vs cyclic dependencies — some problems legitimately have feedback; the invariant forbids.
Fragmentation (named failure) — sub-trees disconnect from root.
Budget Exhaustion (named failure) — resources depleted before solution.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured solver coordination, budget/results flow discipline, acyclicity.
Gives up: feedback loops. Cyclic solver structures require different patterns.
critique: Blame Diffusion (named failure) — failures not attributable in large trees — is endemic.
The 'tree-like or DAG' admits both shapes; the distinction (and its implications) is deferred.
Fragmentation isn't structurally prevented; heartbeats or periodic health checks live outside the pattern.

SolverTree.family_discussion: Foundational solver-structure primitive paired with SolverNode (the unit), RootSolver (the origin), and Task (the work). Compare with DAG — SolverTree is solver-specific; DAG is general topology.

motivation.why_it_exists: Gut feeling from system health (memory pressure, API errors, budget) should inhibit action initiation when stress is high. SomaticMarker names this visceral signal. Without the pattern, agents keep acting under stress without slowdown.
motivation.removability: Removable — agents can act without somatic signals. The pattern imports Damasio's hypothesis into agent design; its value is in the explicit 'stress inhibits action' wiring.

usage.intended: "gut feeling" signal from system health metrics acting as inhibitory emotion.
usage.broad_contexts: Damasio's somatic-marker hypothesis, system stress → action inhibition, burnout detection, rate-limit proximity awareness, biological fatigue signaling.
usage.every_context_needs: health metrics, aggregation into "stress" signal, inhibitory effect on action initiation.
usage.varies: metric set, aggregation function, threshold calibration, override mechanism.
notes: SomaticMarker's mechanism "utilizes Task" is an odd wiring claim — Task as a Noun doesn't seem like the right dep. Worth spot-checking.

tensions: Inhibition invariant (stress reduces action probability) vs urgent action needs — high-stress situations may warrant more action.
Signal Freshness invariant vs lag — markers must reflect current state, which requires fast updates.
Inhibition Correlation — probability inversely proportional to stress — is a specific shape.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit stress-inhibition signal, protection against overload.
Gives up: decisiveness under stress. When stress is high, Somatic Marker reduces action.
critique: The inhibition-correlation is monotonic; real stress response is more nuanced (fight/flight variability).
No failure modes listed.
The Damasio import is suggestive; operational definitions of 'stress' are caller-specific.

SomaticMarker.family_discussion: Health-signal primitive paired with Task (uses SomaticMarker), Signal (emission), and Stress (the input). Compare with Kairos — SomaticMarker is stress-inhibition; Kairos is readiness-detection.

motivation.why_this_layer: credibility assessment — one agent judges a source; N=1 per Gemini Round 6
motivation.why_it_exists: Not all sources are equally credible. SourceEvaluate names the pre-acceptance credibility check: track record, incentives, expertise, access. Without the pattern, credibility is implicit.
motivation.removability: Removable in trusted-source settings. Essential in open-world information gathering. The pattern is thin; credibility assessment is itself subjective.

usage.intended: incentive-aware evidence weighting — Judge-module for evaluating sources.
usage.broad_contexts: journalism fact-checking, academic peer review, witness evaluation in court, intelligence-source evaluation, RAG-source ranking, testimony weighting.
usage.every_context_needs: source identification, track-record evaluation, incentive analysis, expertise check, credibility weighting.
usage.varies: track-record horizon, incentive model sophistication, transparency of evaluation, bias-accounting.

tensions: Genetic Fallacy (named failure) — dismissing valid claims due to source — is the over-application failure.
Credibility components (track record, incentives, etc.) vs weighting — no specified weighting.
Independent verification invariant vs practical reality — most agents can't independently verify.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit credibility assessment.
Gives up: acceptance speed. Every source evaluated adds latency.
critique: Genetic Fallacy is the dual failure and endemic.
Independent verification is aspirational — often impossible.
No failure modes beyond Genetic Fallacy.

SourceEvaluate.family_discussion: Credibility primitive paired with Source, Evidence, and Judge. Compare with Witness — SourceEvaluate assesses credibility; Witness produces attestation.

motivation.why_it_exists: Rigorous artifact definition — shape, behavior, constraints — needs a formal slot. Spec names it, distinct from Plan (how) and Goal (what to achieve). Without the pattern, 'spec' blurs with 'plan' or 'description.'
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every AcceptSpec, FrameSpec, SolverManifest specializes Spec. The Verifiability (binary pass/fail) and Immutability invariants are the contract properties.

usage.intended: rigorous definition of requirements for an artifact — "Definition of Done."
usage.broad_contexts: software specs, API specs, standard specifications (RFCs), legal specifications, product specs, scientific-experiment protocols.
usage.every_context_needs: shape/behavior/constraint definitions, distinction from Plan (how to build) and Goal (what to achieve).
usage.varies: formality (formal vs natural language), machine-readability, completeness (partial specs allowed), versioning.

tensions: Verifiability (binary pass/fail) vs graded compliance — some requirements are naturally graded.
Immutability vs legitimate revision — specs sometimes need revision mid-project.
Contract framing vs exploration — specs commit; exploration needs looser form.
tradeoffs: Gains: rigorous requirements, testable contracts, immutable reference.
Gives up: flexibility. Specs are contracts; iterative refinement requires supersession.
critique: Verifiability is aspirational — many real requirements resist binary testing.
Immutability forces version discipline that many projects skip.
No failure modes listed; specs have many (ambiguity, missing requirements, over-specification).

Spec.family_discussion: Foundational requirements primitive specialized by AcceptSpec (quality bar), FrameSpec (problem contract), and SolverManifest (capability spec). Compare with Criteria — Spec is requirements; Criteria is evaluation standards.

motivation.why_it_exists: Abstract principles need concrete instantiation. Specialize names the move: substitute specific values, check constraints still hold. Without the pattern, abstraction-to-instance gets lost in ad-hoc application.
motivation.removability: Removable — agents can instantiate without the pattern. Specialize earns weight as the explicit move with Constraint Inheritance and Type Narrowing invariants.

usage.intended: concrete instantiation — abstract principle → specific case with substituted values.
usage.future: any "apply the general rule to this specific case" operation.
usage.broad_contexts: deductive application, template instantiation, generic-function specialization, case-law application, policy application to specific incidents.
usage.every_context_needs: abstract principle, substitution mechanism, constraint verification post-substitution.
usage.varies: substitution depth, edge-case discovery, range-of-specialization generation.

tensions: Context Mismatch (named failure) — applying principle to domain where preconditions don't hold.
Constraint Inheritance vs specific-case exceptions — specializations sometimes warrant relaxed constraints.
Type Narrowing vs over-specialization — too narrow a specialization may not be useful.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit abstraction-to-instance move, inherited constraints.
Gives up: cross-domain transfer. Specialize commits to a domain.
critique: Context Mismatch is endemic — precondition checking is the hard part.
Constraint Inheritance is strong; some legitimate specializations need to relax.
No failure modes beyond Context Mismatch.

Specialize.family_discussion: Instantiation primitive paired with Generalize (the reverse), Specify (synonym), and Expansive (the PURE judge). Compare with Generalize — Specialize narrows, Generalize broadens.

motivation.why_this_layer: ontology alignment via tuning signal — two parties
motivation.why_it_exists: Before sending a payload, verify ontology/context match via hash-based challenges. SpectralTune names this: tuning signal, match hashes, only then send payload. Without the pattern, mismatched contexts produce wrong interpretations.
motivation.removability: Removable in single-ontology systems. Essential in cross-ontology coordination. The Atomic Tuning and Fail-Fast invariants are the protocol discipline.

usage.intended: verify ontology alignment before data transfer — hash-based semantic-context challenges.
usage.broad_contexts: ontology-alignment protocols, semantic-interop version checks, API-compatibility-handshake pre-data, cultural-context verification, language-pair validation.
usage.every_context_needs: tuning signal (hash challenges), receiver resonance proof, semantic context ontology.
usage.varies: challenge count, hash granularity, retry on mis-tune, adaptive tuning.

tensions: Infinite tuning loops (named failure) — slight mismatches produce endless retuning.
Fail-Fast vs retry — the invariant says halt on mismatch; retry would be easier and less safe.
Hash-based matching is strict; approximate matching would be more forgiving.
tradeoffs: Gains: context match before payload, principled escalation on mismatch.
Gives up: fluency. Every message pays the tuning cost.
critique: Infinite tuning loops are the named failure with no specified termination.
Fail-Fast on hash mismatch is strict; negotiation/adaptation requires additional patterns.
No partial-match handling.

SpectralTune.family_discussion: Pre-payload primitive paired with Hash (the substrate), OntologyHandshake (broader ontology negotiation), and Greet (initial contact). Compare with OntologyHandshake — SpectralTune is per-payload; OntologyHandshake is session-level.

motivation.why_it_exists: Full audit of every action is expensive. SpotAudit names the probabilistic alternative: random sample, Merkle-proof the slice. Without the pattern, 'audit' is either full-and-expensive or absent.
motivation.removability: Removable for systems with full audit or no audit need. Essential for distributed systems with scale. The Randomness invariant (VRF-based selection) prevents gaming the sampling.

usage.intended: probabilistic random-sample audit with Merkle proof.
usage.future: any "keep honest via random spot checks" verification.
usage.broad_contexts: tax audits, compliance spot-checks, distributed-system liveness checks, integrity verification, ML-model red-teaming, dataset integrity sampling.
usage.every_context_needs: random sampling over target's state, Merkle proof for sampled slice, comparison against expected.
usage.varies: sample frequency, sample size, unpredictability requirements (prevent cheating), escalation on mismatch.

tensions: Privacy leakage (named failure) — sampling reveals internal data.
Sample size vs honesty enforcement — small samples cost less and detect less.
Response time invariant vs thoroughness — fast proofs may miss deep issues.
tradeoffs: Gains: probabilistic honesty enforcement without full audit, Merkle-proof verifiability.
Gives up: privacy. Sampled data is exposed.
critique: Privacy leakage is structural; sampled slices reveal.
Random sampling can miss targeted malicious behavior.
Response time enforcement requires infrastructure the pattern doesn't specify.

SpotAudit.family_discussion: Audit primitive paired with Audit (the general structured record), OathBind (which uses SpotAudit), and Witness (the attestation). Compare with Monitor — SpotAudit is probabilistic sampling; Monitor is continuous.

motivation.why_this_layer: system condition at time T — data
motivation.why_it_exists: Current condition of a system must have a representation. State names it. Foundational — every stateful system needs this slot.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. The pattern is thin because the concept is so basic.

usage.intended: stored information representing a system's condition at time T.
usage.future: any persistent representation of system condition.
usage.broad_contexts: in-memory object state, database rows, session state, workflow state, agent beliefs, machine configuration, app UI state, ML model weights.
usage.every_context_needs: representation content (what), temporal validity (when).
usage.varies: persistence medium, mutation semantics (mutable/immutable/versioned), access protocol, consistency model, serialization format.

tensions: Persistence invariant (unless acted upon) vs observer effects — observation sometimes changes state.
Uniqueness (exactly one State at time T) vs distributed systems — in distributed systems, different nodes may see different states simultaneously.
State vs history — State is now; History is past; distinction blurs in time-sensitive systems.
tradeoffs: Gains: foundational slot for system condition.
Gives up: little — unavoidable primitive.
critique: Very thin.
Uniqueness is wrong for distributed systems where state is consensus-dependent.
No failure modes listed.

State.family_discussion: Foundational primitive paired with Event (the change unit), Snapshot (state at time), and StateTransition (the change). Compare with Context — State is system condition; Context is ambient situation.

motivation.why_this_layer: verify state after write — mechanical check
motivation.why_it_exists: API writes don't always succeed silently. StateAudit names the post-write verification: check the expected state actually materialized. Without the pattern, silent failures propagate.
motivation.removability: Removable in systems with strong write guarantees. Essential where writes can silently fail. The pattern is thin but valuable as a named discipline.

usage.intended: audit state immediately after write to verify transition occurred as expected.
usage.future: any "trust but verify after write" pattern.
usage.broad_contexts: write-verify in distributed systems, read-after-write consistency checks, SQL audit-trail verification, filesystem post-write checks, transaction-success verification.
usage.every_context_needs: write operation, immediate audit, expected-vs-actual check, silent-failure detection.
usage.varies: audit latency (sync vs async), verification depth, retry semantics on mismatch.

tensions: Post-write verification cost vs confidence in writes — trusted APIs don't need this; untrusted do.
Verification delay vs downstream action — waiting for audit slows pipelines.
Silent API failures — the pattern names the threat but doesn't catalog vectors.
tradeoffs: Gains: silent-failure detection.
