Gives up: throughput. Every write pays the audit.
critique: Very thin — one sentence.
No failure modes listed; StateAudit has some (audit-of-audit infinite regress, read-after-write consistency issues).
Assumes reads are reliable enough to audit writes; if reads are also silent-failing, the audit is too.

StateAudit.family_discussion: Safety primitive paired with Act (the write), Observe (the verification), and StateTransition (what's being verified). Compare with SpotAudit — StateAudit is per-write; SpotAudit is probabilistic sampling.

motivation.why_it_exists: Cross-actor atomic coordination: two parties temporarily fuse a subset of their state, and changes require both signatures. Mutex gives single-holder exclusion; StateLock gives two-holder agreement. The mechanism structurally requires a counterparty, which is why it lives in Society/Protocols — single-agent substitution is incoherent.
motivation.removability: No. Two-party atomic coordination is a common primitive (escrow, two-phase commit, joint authorship) and the library has no other pattern that encodes it. Multi-party coordination (N>2) is a separate pattern space — StateLock is specifically the two-party case.

usage.intended: atomic coordination via temporary state fusion — both actors' signatures required.
usage.broad_contexts: two-phase commit, escrow key pairs, multi-signature wallets, joint-authorship protocols, collaborative editing locks, diplomatic joint statements.
usage.every_context_needs: state subset, two (or more) actors, temporary fusion, both-sign-to-write, Backoff/Cooldown on contention.
usage.varies: multi-party extension, timeout policy, revocation.

tensions: Exactly-two-actor vs N-party generalization: the mechanism says 'two actors.' Multi-signature wallets and quorum-based writes need N>2 — they are listed under broad-use contexts but the pattern's mechanism doesn't natively support them. Descendants (`MultisigStateLock`) handle this but the parent is tied to two.

Cryptographic signatures vs weaker trust models: the pattern assumes signatures, which assumes identity infrastructure. In lower-trust settings the spec degrades to 'both acknowledge' with no fraud protection.

Temporary fusion vs persistent agreement: StateLock is explicitly temporary (auto-dissolves on timeout). Some use cases (long-running co-ownership) want persistent fusion — that's a different pattern the library doesn't currently mint.
tradeoffs: Both-sign-to-write buys integrity (no unilateral changes) at the cost of liveness (one party offline blocks all changes).
Auto-dissolve on timeout buys crash safety at the cost of 'premature dissolution' risk when legitimate work exceeds the timeout.
Backoff+Cooldown composition buys contention handling at the cost of lock-family dependency — StateLock doesn't stand alone operationally.
critique: Zero invariants listed. For a pattern that carries atomicity semantics, this is a significant gap — at minimum: Both-Signed (changes require both sigs), Symmetric (neither party has unilateral release), Auto-Dissolve-On-Timeout, Signature-Integrity (sigs bind to the specific state subset).

The three failure modes are correct but partial — missing: Key Compromise (one party's signing key stolen mid-lock), Sig Replay (old signature reused against new state), State-Scope Drift (the 'subset of writable state' changes meaning mid-lock).

'Temporary fusion' is evocative but operationally vague. What counts as fusion? Is it a third-party escrow? A merged state object? A shared access-control list? The pattern is underdetermined — implementers will pick different mechanisms that claim to be the same pattern.

StateLock.family_discussion: The two-party cross-actor specialization of the Lock family, placed in Society because the mechanism structurally requires a counterparty. Pairs with `Backoff` and `Cooldown` for contention behavior and with `AtomicBid` for multi-agent coordination. Where `Mutex` is one-holder exclusion, `StateLock` is two-party agreement.

motivation.why_it_exists: Volatile state that would be lost on crash needs durable persistence. StateSnapshot names the local serialization: take a checkpoint, write to durable storage. Without the pattern, crashes lose arbitrary in-flight state.
motivation.removability: Removable in purely stateless systems. Essential for stateful agents that need recovery. Distinct from Snapshot (general primitive) by its periodic-serialization framing.

usage.intended: periodic serialization of volatile state to durable storage for crash recovery.
usage.broad_contexts: OS hibernate/sleep, database checkpoints, game save files, VM snapshots, agent-state persistence, conversation state persistence.
usage.every_context_needs: volatile state, durable-storage target, periodic serialization, resume-from-snapshot semantic.
usage.varies: snapshot interval (Duration per §3.17), delta vs full, encryption, storage medium.

tensions: Snapshot frequency vs overhead — frequent is safe and expensive.
Atomicity invariant (fully written or discarded) vs legitimate partial writes — real serializers sometimes write partially.
Roundtrip Integrity invariant vs implementation bugs — serialization bugs violate the invariant invisibly.
tradeoffs: Gains: crash-recoverable agent state, local autonomy (no consensus required).
Gives up: consistency across agents. StateSnapshot is local; distributed recovery needs consensus.
critique: Roundtrip Integrity is the hardest property — implementation bugs silently violate it.
Atomicity often requires coordination (write to temp, fsync, rename); the pattern asserts without specifying.
No failure modes listed.

StateSnapshot.family_discussion: Durability primitive paired with Snapshot (general), Serialize (the operation), and Restore (the recovery). Compare with LatticeCommit — StateSnapshot is unilateral; LatticeCommit is distributed consensus.

motivation.why_it_exists: State changes are not arbitrary — they follow rules (valid transitions, conditions, effects). StateTransition names the finite-state-machine framing. Without it, state changes are ad-hoc and validity gets smeared across callers.
motivation.removability: Removable in non-FSM systems. Essential in systems where state validity matters. The pattern imports classical FSM discipline.

usage.intended: explicit FSM — Transition T: S × Event → S.
usage.broad_contexts: programming FSMs, workflow engines, protocol state machines, biological state transitions, regulatory process state machines, UI state management.
usage.every_context_needs: state set, event set, transition function, only-valid-transitions rule.
usage.varies: deterministic vs non-deterministic, acceptance states, guards on transitions, actions-on-transition.

tensions: Finite states vs continuous state — FSM assumes discrete states; continuous systems need different patterns.
Valid transitions vs emergent states — FSM is defined; real systems have unanticipated states.
Current state determines actions — ignores historical context that sometimes matters.
tradeoffs: Gains: principled state change, validity enforcement, clear action-availability.
Gives up: fluidity. FSMs are rigid; some systems benefit from looser state semantics.
critique: Very thin — one-line mechanism.
No failure modes listed; FSMs have many (invalid transitions, state explosion, missed states).
Finite assumption is strong; many real systems have effectively infinite states.

StateTransition.family_discussion: Foundational primitive paired with State (the substrate), Event (the trigger), and Transition (the move). Compare with Event — StateTransition is state-to-state; Event is occurrence.

motivation.why_it_exists: The tri-valued epistemic outcome of a Check — Verified / Falsified / Unknown — with Unknown as a first-class value rather than a degenerate case of Falsified. Systems that collapse Unknown into Falsified rediscover this at cost; Status forces the three-way distinction to survive the caller boundary.
motivation.removability: No. Status is Check's output type; removing it collapses Check into a Boolean pattern and loses the Unknown signal that discriminates 'we verified this fails' from 'we don't have evidence either way.' The library's verification stack explicitly rests on this three-way distinction.

tensions: Three-valued vs Boolean: a caller who treats Status as Boolean by mapping Unknown → false is exactly the failure mode Unknown exists to prevent. The library's answer is that forced mapping is always wrong; callers must handle Unknown explicitly or signal that they can't.

Reason field optionality: the mechanism offers an optional reason. Optional reasons are often absent, and downstream systems routinely need them (why was this Falsified?). The library pushes richer reason attribution to FailureTrace.

Relationship to Decision: both are three-valued; both can be confused. Status is epistemic (what do we know?), Decision is operational (what will we do?). The library deliberately keeps them separate because the semantics differ.
tradeoffs: Tri-valued semantics preserves epistemic honesty but requires callers to handle Unknown explicitly — two-branch code paths are not sufficient.
Optional reason buys simplicity in the happy path (no reason needed on Verified) at the cost of explanatory power on Falsified/Unknown.
Distinctness from Decision is conceptually clean but imposes type-disambiguation load on readers who have to track which three-valued type is at hand.
critique: No failure modes listed. Status is a data structure so failure modes are subtle — but at least Misinterpretation (caller collapses Unknown into Falsified) and Stale Status (value outlives the observation window) should be named.

The reason field is string-typed (implicitly) with no structure. A structured reason (code + message + evidence) would let callers route on Falsified-because-X vs Falsified-because-Y. Pushing this to FailureTrace means the lightweight case is under-served.

'Distinct from Boolean' is asserted but not defended in the mechanism — why is three-valued the right shape rather than confidence-weighted-Boolean or probabilistic? The audit discussed this; the pattern's mechanism does not.

Status.family_discussion: Output type of Check; third type in the verification-stack taxonomy (Status / Decision / Boolean / Score). Pairs with Check as Decision pairs with Gate. Unknown as a first-class value is the distinguishing feature — other verification outputs collapse it or never admit it.

motivation.why_it_exists: A structured counter-argument generation requirement before finalizing decisions — forces the agent to construct the strongest opposition to its own conclusion rather than ignoring or weakly representing it. Makes the 'steelman vs strawman' distinction a procedural requirement, not just intellectual hygiene.
motivation.removability: Probably retain. The pattern names a discipline that improves output quality; without the pattern it lives as advice. The discipline is valuable enough that making it a first-class pattern helps adoption.

usage.intended: mandatory counter-argument generation — generate strongest argument against own conclusion.
usage.broad_contexts: epistemic hygiene before publishing, pre-meeting preparation, red-team-of-self, test-of-decision robustness, bias-resistance discipline.
usage.every_context_needs: current decision/output, counter-argument generation, validity threshold, revise-on-strong-counter.
usage.varies: counter-argument generation method, threshold calibration, revision strategy on failure.

tensions: Same-agent steelman vs adversarial separation: the Collusion failure mode (Strawman Waltz) is structural — if the Critic is the same entity as the Proposer, counter-arguments can be deliberately weak. The pattern is honest about this; AdversarialSteel is the separate-entity descendant.

Score threshold (>0.7) as invariant vs evaluation fairness: the threshold requires the counter-argument to be non-trivial by some metric. But the metric is applied by... the same agent. Self-grading a counter-argument invites the Strawman Waltz.
Paralysis by Analysis vs required rigor: the pattern forces a critique loop, which can spiral. No exit condition is prescribed beyond 'passing critique required for release.'
tradeoffs: Mandatory counter-argument buys intellectual honesty at the cost of tokens and wall time.
Score-threshold invariant buys non-trivial opposition at the cost of measuring non-triviality with the same agent's judgment.
Tier 2 placement (honesty-dependent) buys accurate classification at the cost of excluding adversarial contexts — callers in those must reach for AdversarialSteel.
critique: Three invariants, two failure modes — relatively thorough. The Collusion failure mode is clearly stated and the pattern's explicit Tier 2 status acknowledges the limitation.
'Score(Counter) > 0.7' hard-codes a threshold without justification. Why 0.7 vs 0.5 or 0.8? The number invites gaming.

'Strongest Counter: Generated argument must address the core claim, not weak points' is the right spirit but 'core claim' is interpretive — an adversarial agent can claim the core is what they chose to attack.

SteelmanCheck.family_discussion: The single-agent rigorous-self-critique pattern. Paired with `AdversarialSteel` (separate green/red advocates — the Tier 1 adversarial-safe specialization) and `RedTeam` (hostile adversarial review). Uses `Check` for robustness evaluation and `Critique` for belief interrogation.

motivation.why_it_exists: Critique after generation is biased by attachment to the proposal. SteelmanFirst names the counter-argument-first discipline: construct strongest opposing before proposing. Without the pattern, confirmation bias rules.
motivation.removability: Removable — Steelman works as post-hoc check too. SteelmanFirst is the explicit ordering discipline. The Prioritization invariant is the key.

usage.intended: ordering rule — steelman opposing view *before* proposing, so SteelmanCheck has real targets.
usage.future: any "construct the strongest counter *first*" ordering discipline.
usage.broad_contexts: pre-debate preparation, pre-release review discipline, academic steelman-before-critique, preparing-for-boss-pushback, rehearsing-devils-advocacy.
usage.every_context_needs: recognition that SteelmanCheck is coming, proactive strongest-counter construction, population of critique with high-quality data (not strawmen).
usage.varies: depth of pre-constructed counter, iteration count, delegation (construct-yourself vs hire-adversary).

tensions: Performative Steelman (named failure) — weak counter-arguments to appear unbiased.
Bias Leakage (named failure) — framing counter-argument to be easily defeated.
First vs after — the invariant forces first; some situations benefit from post-hoc critique.
tradeoffs: Gains: structural anti-confirmation-bias discipline.
Gives up: generation speed.
critique: Performative Steelman is endemic.
Bias Leakage is the subtler failure.
Both named failures reflect that discipline is caller-dependent.

SteelmanFirst.family_discussion: Epistemic-hygiene primitive paired with SteelmanCheck (the general), ConfirmationBlock (disconfirmation-seeking), and DissentSeek (finding disagreement). Compare with PreMortem — SteelmanFirst is argument; PreMortem is failure.

motivation.why_it_exists: Actions need atomic structure — preconditions, action, post-conditions, rollback. Step names this. Without the pattern, 'step' is ambiguous and Plan has no atomic unit.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Plan consumes Step; Step is the executable unit. The Atomicity and Causal Closure invariants are the correctness properties.

usage.intended: atomic action with preconditions, postconditions, and rollback.
usage.broad_contexts: workflow steps, algorithm steps, recipe steps, ritual steps, protocol steps, assembly-line steps, surgical steps.
usage.every_context_needs: preconditions, action, postconditions, rollback specification.
usage.varies: atomicity strictness, rollback cost, parallel-vs-sequential context, side effects.

tensions: Atomicity invariant vs real-world partial execution — some steps can't cleanly roll back.
Precondition Violation (named failure) — step fires without preconditions.
Rollback Failure (named failure) — irreversible mid-step.
tradeoffs: Gains: atomic action unit, explicit rollback path.
Gives up: flexibility. Not all actions have clean rollback.
critique: Rollback Failure is endemic for real-world actions (sent emails, physical changes).
Postcondition Failure is subtle — the step 'completed' but didn't achieve its intent.
Atomicity is aspirational for distributed or physical actions.

Step.family_discussion: Foundational execution primitive paired with Act (the verb), Plan (the composition), and Compensate (the undo). Compare with Task — Step is atomic action; Task is scoped work.

motivation.why_it_exists: Direct problem-solving sometimes fails on the framing. StepBack names the meta-move: pause, ask higher-level question. Without the pattern, framing lock-in persists.
motivation.removability: Removable — agents can ask higher-level questions without the pattern. Value is in the explicit discipline and invariants.

usage.intended: meta-cognitive think operation — pause object-level work to ask higher-level question.
usage.future: any "zoom out for perspective" reasoning operation.
usage.broad_contexts: debugging frustration breaks, architectural review, strategy retrospectives, scientific paradigm questioning, life-decision reflection, system-design-level questions.
usage.every_context_needs: pause of object-level work, abstraction ascent, higher-level question formulation.
usage.varies: ascent depth, trigger (spontaneous vs scheduled), return semantic (new direction vs resume old).

tensions: Over-abstraction (named failure) — climbing too high.
Analysis Paralysis (named failure) — endless stepping back.
Premature Descent (named failure) — jumping back to action before gaining altitude.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit meta-cognitive move, altitude gain.
Gives up: directness. Stepping back is slower than direct solving.
critique: All three named failures are real.
Bounded invariant (max depth) is unspecified.
Relevance invariant is aspirational — high-level insight doesn't always inform.

StepBack.family_discussion: Meta-cognitive primitive paired with Reframe (the outcome), FirstPrinciples (the extreme), and Think (the substrate). Compare with Reframe — StepBack gains altitude; Reframe changes perspective at the same altitude.

motivation.why_this_layer: indirect coordination via shared-environment traces — marker + reader
motivation.why_it_exists: Indirect coordination via environment traces — agents mark shared space, other agents sense and respond, traces decay. Names the biological-inspired coordination mode distinct from direct message-passing. Essential for swarm coordination where direct agent-to-agent contact would flood the network.
motivation.removability: No. Swarm protocols, ant-colony-optimization-style patterns, and environment-mediated coordination all reference Stigmergy. Removing forces each to re-derive the decay-and-reinforcement pattern.

usage.intended: indirect coordination via environment traces (ant colony).
usage.future: any mediated coordination via shared substrate.
usage.broad_contexts: ant colonies (biological origin), pheromone-based ML, shared whiteboards, wiki edit patterns, git commit flows, code comments, API documentation evolution, graffiti-based organization.
usage.every_context_needs: shared medium, MARK operation, SENSE operation, persistence mechanism (decay or versioning).
usage.varies: persistence scheme — **biological traces DECAY** (pheromones, graffiti wear); **digital traces often VERSION** (wiki history, git commits, append-only logs). Also: trace data structure, reinforcement mechanics, sensor radius, concurrency semantics.

tensions: Indirect coordination vs direct message: stigmergy is lower-bandwidth (one-to-many via environment) but also slower (traces must accumulate). Direct messaging is faster but scales worse — callers choose based on swarm size.
Decay rate vs signal persistence: too fast decay and coordination is lost; too slow and stale traces mislead. The invariant mandates decay but doesn't prescribe rate — caller concern.
Locality invariant vs global awareness: sensing is local, which prevents flooding but also prevents global-awareness coordination. Global-awareness variants would need a different pattern.
tradeoffs: Environment-mediated coordination buys scalability (coordination complexity doesn't grow with number of agents) at the cost of latency (traces must accumulate).
Decay invariant buys staleness-resistance at the cost of requiring repeated reinforcement for stable coordination.
Locality invariant buys low network traffic at the cost of excluding global-awareness coordination patterns.
critique: Two invariants, zero failure modes. Missing: Trace Pollution (malicious agents inject misleading traces), Signal Saturation (so many traces that sensing becomes noise), Coordination Failure (traces don't accumulate into coherent signal).
'Decay over time but can be reinforced' — no decay rate specified, no reinforcement semantics (does reinforcement reset decay or add to the trace?).
Structured traces is mentioned but structure not specified. Different implementations may use incompatible trace formats.

Stigmergy.family_discussion: The environment-mediated coordination primitive in Society. Composed with `Decay` (the attenuation substrate). Sibling to direct-messaging protocols (`Handoff`, `ShoutWhisper`). Parent to ant-colony-inspired and pheromone-based descendants.

motivation.why_it_exists: Reading documents linearly wastes budget on irrelevant content. StrategicReading names the non-linear retrieval: build tree first, target reads, stay under budget. Without the pattern, agents drown in document content.
motivation.removability: Removable for short documents. Essential for long-document work. Structure-first discipline and budget awareness are the key invariants.

usage.intended: non-linear information retrieval — treat documents as random-access databases.
usage.future: any "read like a researcher, not sequentially" heuristic.
usage.broad_contexts: research paper consumption, legal document review, codebase exploration, long-context LLM strategies, executive document skimming, reference manual navigation.
usage.every_context_needs: structural map building (Tree), high-entropy section identification, selective loading.
usage.varies: map-construction method, entropy metric, compute budget, stopping criteria.

tensions: Context Overflow (named failure) — loading full documents.
Linear Bias (named failure) — reading intros while missing key results.
Structure-first vs body-first — the pattern commits to structure-first.
tradeoffs: Gains: budget-disciplined reading, targeted retrieval.
Gives up: completeness. Strategic reading misses content for efficiency.
critique: 10% budget is a specific default; caller tuning required.
Structure-first assumes documents have extractable structure; some don't.
Linear bias is human; LLM agents may have different biases.

StrategicReading.family_discussion: Reading-strategy primitive paired with Search (retrieval), Read (the act), and Summary (the consumption output). Compare with DeepResearch — StrategicReading is single-doc; DeepResearch is multi-source.

motivation.why_it_exists: Plans are fixed; Strategy is adaptive under uncertainty. Strategy names the 'how to win' framing distinct from 'what steps to take.' Without the pattern, strategy and plan blur.
motivation.removability: Removable in certain-environment settings. Essential for adaptive planning under uncertainty.

usage.intended: adaptive high-level plan under uncertainty ("How to win" vs "What steps").
usage.broad_contexts: military strategy, business strategy, research strategy, competitive game strategies, career strategies, negotiation strategies.
usage.every_context_needs: high-level goal, uncertainty acknowledgment, adaptive stance, success criteria.
usage.varies: planning horizon, adaptation frequency, revision triggers, scope.

tensions: Strategy vs Plan — adaptive vs fixed; the line blurs.
High-level vs actionable — Strategy is high-level; execution needs Plan.
Uncertainty handling — Strategy adapts; the adaptation rule is under-specified.
tradeoffs: Gains: adaptive planning framing.
Gives up: crispness. Strategy is looser than Plan.
critique: Very thin mechanism.
No failure modes, no invariants.
Relationship with Plan is stated but not operationalized.

Strategy.family_discussion: Planning primitive paired with Plan (tactical), Roadmap (temporal-strategic), and Goal (what's being won). Compare with Plan — Strategy is adaptive; Plan is sequential.

motivation.why_it_exists: Unbounded ordered message sequences — log feeds, real-time pipes, conversational histories — need a container distinct from finite Queue. Stream names it.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for real-time systems. The pattern is the natural container for unbounded ordered data.

usage.intended: ordered, potentially unbounded sequence of Messages.
usage.broad_contexts: Kafka topics, HTTP/2 streams, WebSocket channels, LLM token streams, log feeds, conversation histories, sensor streams, video streams.
usage.every_context_needs: ordered sequence, Message elements, operations (map, filter, backpressure).
usage.varies: boundedness, ordering guarantees, at-least-once vs at-most-once, durability, multi-consumer support.

tensions: Ordering invariant vs distributed streams — multiple sources may produce incompatible orderings.
Causality invariant vs concurrency — concurrent events have no strict causal order.
Unbounded vs bounded memory — infinite streams require windowing.
tradeoffs: Gains: unbounded ordered sequence, real-time processing substrate.
Gives up: finite semantics. Streams have no end; operations like 'all messages' don't apply.
critique: Causality invariant is hard in distributed streams without vector clocks.
No failure modes listed; streams have many (backpressure, reordering, loss).
Map/filter operations are mentioned but not specified.

Stream.family_discussion: Foundational container paired with Queue (finite counterpart), Event (the unit), and Signal (emission). Compare with Queue — Stream is unbounded; Queue is finite.

motivation.why_it_exists: Critique targeting content (surface) misses structural issues. StructuralCoaching names the deeper critique: reject based on logical form, propose structural pivot. Without the pattern, critique stays on the surface.
motivation.removability: Removable — surface critique covers much ground. StructuralCoaching is for deeper feedback. The Depth Distinction and Directional Guidance invariants are the discipline.

usage.intended: feedback on logical form/structure, not content — shift Mechanism Class.
usage.broad_contexts: academic writing advising (the argument shape), research methodology critique, mathematical proof structuring, music composition pedagogy, software-architecture review.
usage.every_context_needs: target proposal, rejection on structural grounds, mechanism-class shift guidance, topic-agnostic framing.
usage.varies: mechanism-class taxonomy, coaching tone, iteration count.

tensions: Critic becomes too prescriptive (named failure) — reduces Generator agency.
Mechanism critique vs vocabulary — the invariant requires mechanism focus; easy to slip to vocabulary.
Directional Guidance vs generator autonomy — prescribing pivots constrains.
tradeoffs: Gains: structural critique depth, explicit pivot proposal.
Gives up: generator agency. Structural coaches can become prescriptive.
critique: Critic prescriptiveness is the named failure; the pattern doesn't quantify.
Mechanism vs vocabulary distinction is hard to operationalize.
Directional Guidance requirement means critics carry implementation responsibility.

StructuralCoaching.family_discussion: Critique primitive paired with Critique (the general), EvaluatorOptimizer (the loop), and Reframe (the pivot response). Compare with Critique — StructuralCoaching is structural; Critique is content-general.

motivation.why_it_exists: Aesthetic and formatting requirements need structured spec. StyleSpec names it — reference standard for polish-focused refinement passes. Without the pattern, style requirements live in prose or are implicit.
motivation.removability: Removable for systems without polish requirements. Used by PhasedRefinement for style-pass. The pattern is a specialized Spec.

usage.intended: structured spec defining aesthetics + formatting rules for polish passes.
usage.future: any "how it should look/feel" spec artifact.
usage.broad_contexts: editorial style guides, brand design specs, code formatter configs, API response-format specs, UX style systems.
usage.every_context_needs: aesthetic requirements, formatting rules, reference-standard role in PhasedRefinement.
usage.varies: rule count, flexibility, enforceability, version history.

tensions: Structured spec vs stylistic judgment — style has elements that resist specification.
Immutable vs stylistic evolution — style rules evolve with culture.
Pairing with Aesthetics — StyleSpec is rules; Aesthetics is judgment.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured style requirements.
Gives up: nuance.
critique: No failure modes listed.
Structured style can miss stylistic subtlety.
Very thin; the real work is in the specific style rules.

StyleSpec.family_discussion: Spec-variant paired with AcceptSpec (quality), FrameSpec (problem), and Aesthetics (the judge). Used by PhasedRefinement.

motivation.why_it_exists: The target entity of observation/evaluation/action needs a slot. Subject names the 'who or what' in subject-object relationships. Thin foundational primitive.
motivation.removability: Very thin — nearly a stub. Foundational for any relational primitive.

usage.intended: target of an operation — the "Who" or "What" role.
usage.future: Subject as marker on pattern signatures.
notes: §3.18 converts to Trait. Broad-use confirms — it's a grammatical role, not a standalone pattern.

tensions: Subject vs Object — the distinction is relational and sometimes reversed.
Animate vs inanimate subjects — the pattern is agnostic; some operations care.
Multiple subjects vs single — the pattern implies singular.
tradeoffs: Gains: named slot for 'who/what.'
Gives up: little.
critique: Almost a stub — one-sentence mechanism, no invariants.
Distinction from Object is implicit.
No failure modes.

Subject.family_discussion: Foundational relational primitive paired with Object (the counterpart), Agent (active subject), and Target (receiving target).

motivation.why_it_exists: Large artifacts need compressed representations preserving salience. Summarize names this. Distinct from Compress (size-reduction focus) by the salience emphasis.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in LLM-era applications. The pattern is the canonical information-density-increasing operation. Invariants (Compression, Salience, Fidelity) are the quality properties.

usage.intended: lossy compression preserving salience — smaller artifact with high-value info retained.
usage.broad_contexts: document summarization, conversation recaps, executive summaries, abstract generation, meeting-notes compression, news summarization.
usage.every_context_needs: source artifact, smaller output, salience-preservation criterion, explicit lossy-ness.
usage.varies: compression ratio, salience determination method, domain specificity, target-audience awareness.

tensions: Salience vs completeness — richer salience requires leaving more out.
Fidelity invariant (no hallucination) vs LLM reality — LLM summaries routinely add content.
Compression vs context preservation — aggressive summarization loses context.
tradeoffs: Gains: information-density increase, context-fit for downstream.
Gives up: detail. Summaries lose specifics.
critique: Fidelity (no hallucination) is the hardest invariant; LLMs violate it routinely.
Salience is subjective; different summaries for the same input are legitimate.
No failure modes listed; summarization has many (lost key info, hallucinated, biased selection).

Summarize.family_discussion: Cognitive-compression primitive paired with Compress (size focus), ChunkMerge (structural compression), and ContextCompress (memory management). Compare with Extract — Summarize preserves structure; Extract pulls pieces.

motivation.why_it_exists: The output of Summarize needs a typed slot: compressed representation retaining salient information. Summary names it. Foundational downstream-consumable unit.
motivation.removability: Removable by folding into generic Artifact. The distinct type helps downstream consumers expect compressed-salient-content.

usage.intended: compressed representation retaining salient info, discarding redundancy.
usage.broad_contexts: document summaries, meeting minutes, executive briefs, research abstracts, news summaries.
usage.every_context_needs: `source_ref: sema_id` (definitional — a Summary without source is meaningless), compression of content, salience-preservation.
usage.varies: compression ratio (optional per §3.19), preservation list (optional), domain specificity.

tensions: Salience preservation vs compression — trade-off between keeping high-value and shrinking size.
Redundancy removal vs context preservation — redundancy often helps downstream.
Summary as artifact vs summary as view — the pattern is static; views could be dynamic.
tradeoffs: Gains: typed compressed artifact.
Gives up: little.
critique: Very thin.
Salient is subjective.
No failure modes listed.

Summary.family_discussion: Output primitive paired with Summarize (the producer), Compress (size focus), and Abstract (more aggressive reduction).

motivation.why_it_exists: Past investment biases decisions to continue even when stopping is better. SunkCostIgnore names the fresh-slate discipline: would I start this today? Without the pattern, sunk costs drive continuation.
motivation.removability: Removable — decision theory always includes the concept. The named pattern makes the discipline explicit.

usage.intended: fresh-slate evaluation — decide whether to continue based on forward value, not past investment.
usage.future: any "ignore past investment when deciding future" discipline.
usage.broad_contexts: business-portfolio decisions, research-project continuation decisions, personal-project abandonment, relationship decisions, investment-hold-vs-sell decisions.
usage.every_context_needs: "if starting fresh today" framing, past-investment-irrelevant semantic, future-only cost-benefit.
usage.varies: definition of "fresh today" (full reset vs current-state-only), integration with OpportunityCost, emotional-override resistance.

tensions: Loss Aversion Loop (named failure) — reframing stopping as loss to prevent fresh evaluation.
Psychologically hard — the discipline contradicts evolved decision biases.
Past investment excluded from calc — invariant is clean; real decisions legitimately draw on past learning.
tradeoffs: Gains: decision discipline against sunk-cost fallacy.
Gives up: continuity. Some continuations benefit from path dependency.
critique: Loss Aversion Loop is the dominant real failure.
The strict 'past investment excluded' rules out legitimate path-dependent benefits.
No specified mechanism for stopping the re-evaluation; 'ask today' becomes daily decision fatigue.

SunkCostIgnore.family_discussion: Decision-discipline primitive paired with OpportunityCost, EpistemicROI, and RegretMinimization. Compare with CommitmentDevice — SunkCostIgnore counters over-continuation; CommitmentDevice counters under-continuation.

motivation.why_it_exists: Updates proportional to surprise concentrate learning where it matters. SurprisalUpdate names this: loss magnitude = -log P. Without the pattern, all prediction errors update equally, diluting strong signals.
motivation.removability: Removable in uniform-learning settings. Essential for agents that should learn fast from unexpected events. The Stability Guard invariant prevents single-update dominance.

usage.intended: learn weighted by prediction-failure magnitude (learn most from what confused you most).
usage.broad_contexts: online ML fine-tuning, human learning from unexpected outcomes, RL reward-surprise weighting, forecaster self-update, Bayesian model updating.
usage.every_context_needs: prediction, observation, surprisal computation (-log P(observed|predicted)), update magnitude proportional to surprisal.
usage.varies: what gets updated (weights, embeddings, context), update rule specifics, clamping to avoid runaway updates.

tensions: Outlier Overfitting (named failure) — rare high-surprisal events dominate learning.
Catastrophic Forgetting (named failure) — aggressive updates erase prior knowledge.
Compute Cost (named failure) — high-surprisal events demand heavy processing.
tradeoffs: Gains: concentrated learning, magnitude-appropriate updates.
Gives up: stability. Surprisal-proportional updates can swing wildly.
critique: All three named failures are real and structural.
Stability Guard is asserted; max_update_rate is caller-tuned.
Outlier Overfitting and Catastrophic Forgetting are in tension — preventing one can worsen the other.

SurprisalUpdate.family_discussion: Learning primitive paired with BayesUpdate (Bayesian substrate), BeliefTracking (version control), and CounterfactualAnchor (pre-commit prediction). Compare with BayesUpdate — SurprisalUpdate is surprise-weighted; BayesUpdate is likelihood-weighted.

motivation.why_it_exists: Datasets often contain only successes — failures aren't recorded. SurvivorCorrect names the discipline: ask if you're seeing only survivors, estimate base rate, seek failures. Without the pattern, survivor bias is invisible.
motivation.removability: Removable — careful analysts do this manually. The named pattern makes the discipline explicit.

usage.intended: account for silent failures in data (survivorship bias correction).
usage.future: any base-rate-aware learning that avoids surviving-examples bias.
usage.broad_contexts: investment analysis (surviving funds only), scientific study design (published vs drawer), ML training (learning from labeled success only), case-study analysis, historical reasoning.
usage.every_context_needs: explicit question "am I seeing only successes?", base-rate estimation, failure inclusion.
usage.varies: failure-detection method, base-rate estimation technique, correction weighting.

tensions: Phantom Hunt (named failure) — looking for failures that don't exist.
Sample re-weighting vs original data — re-weighting is judgment; getting it right is the hard part.
Failure-seeking effort vs diminishing returns — eventually most failures have been found.
tradeoffs: Gains: survivor-bias correction, sample re-weighting.
Gives up: time. Failure-seeking is expensive.
critique: Phantom Hunt is endemic in genuinely successful domains.
Base rate estimation is often the hardest part.
No failure modes beyond Phantom Hunt.

SurvivorCorrect.family_discussion: Bias-correction primitive paired with BaseRateInclude, CognitiveBias, and Reweight. Compare with ConfirmationBlock — SurvivorCorrect is sample-level; ConfirmationBlock is hypothesis-level.

motivation.why_it_exists: Generate-verify pairs need explicit mode signaling — wild generation paired with strict verification. SynergisticMode names this coupling. Without the pattern, solvers don't know whether to be permissive or strict.
motivation.removability: Removable by fixed solver modes. Essential for adaptive generator-verifier coupling. The Complementary Coupling invariant is the key discipline.

usage.intended: protocol-level cognitive mode switching — broadcast "Generative vs Verifier" signal; downstream adjusts AcceptSpec strictness.
usage.broad_contexts: multi-agent training-mode switches (training vs eval), brainstorm-vs-review phases in teams, building-vs-testing phases in software, daytime-vs-night protocols.
usage.every_context_needs: mode signal broadcast, downstream AcceptSpec adjustment, synchronized mode entry/exit.
usage.varies: mode set, transition protocol, escalation on refusal-to-switch.

tensions: Mode Confusion (named failure) — downstream misinterprets mode.
Mode Locking (named failure) — stuck in Conservative.
Generator vs Verifier — the pattern enforces pair; some problems need different couplings.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit generator-verifier coupling, dynamic mode signaling.
Gives up: simplicity. Fixed-mode systems are simpler.
critique: Mode Locking is a real failure — once conservative, hard to get wild again.
Mode Confusion happens across ontologies.
Explicit Declaration invariant requires OntologyHandshake-level ceremony.

SynergisticMode.family_discussion: Multi-agent-coordination primitive paired with OntologyHandshake (the declaration substrate), Generator/Verifier roles, and SynergisticPairing. Compare with Mode — SynergisticMode is paired-declared; Mode is single-agent.

motivation.why_it_exists: Combining elements into unified whole — the opposite of analysis. Synthesis names this constructive move. Foundational primitive for any pattern that assembles rather than breaks apart.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every constructive pattern (Compose, DiscoveryProtocol's reduction, ConceptBlend) uses Synthesis or equivalent.

usage.intended: the combined unified whole resulting from integration of separate elements.
usage.broad_contexts: Hegelian synthesis, music composition synthesis, scientific synthesis of findings, team-contribution synthesis, cross-disciplinary synthesis.
usage.every_context_needs: the integrated whole as an artifact, reference to constituent parts, new-meaning semantic.
usage.varies: synthesis method (dialectic, aggregation, emergence), fidelity to parts, novelty detection.
notes: §3.18 and §3.19 confirmed that Synthesis-as-Noun (the combined whole) is the correct mechanism framing; the process-verb `Synthesize` could be minted separately if needed.

tensions: Synthesis vs analysis — opposites; most real work is both.
Unified whole vs preserved separateness — synthesis merges; some elements benefit from separation.
Meaning construction vs faithful combination — synthesis creates new meaning; fidelity to inputs is in tension.
tradeoffs: Gains: named constructive move.
Gives up: little.
critique: Very thin.
No failure modes listed; synthesis has many (hallucinated connections, lost elements).
The 'new meaning' framing is poetic; operational definition is missing.

Synthesis.family_discussion: Foundational primitive paired with Analysis (the opposite), Compose (structured synthesis), and Emergence (spontaneous synthesis). Compare with ConceptBlend — Synthesis is general; ConceptBlend is cross-domain.

motivation.why_this_layer: complex whole of interacting parts — data
motivation.why_it_exists: Complex wholes with interacting parts, boundaries, purpose — the pattern names this at the most general level. Foundational primitive for any discussion of systemic properties.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Most architecture patterns reference System as the container.

usage.intended: complex whole of interacting parts with boundaries, structure, purpose.
usage.broad_contexts: software systems, biological systems, social systems, ecological systems, economic systems, legal systems, mental systems.
usage.every_context_needs: component parts, interactions, boundary definition, purpose/function.
usage.varies: hierarchical vs flat, closed vs open, static vs dynamic, observability.

tensions: Boundary definition vs openness — systems have boundaries; some are porous.
Purpose vs emergence — some systems have designed purpose, others emerge without it.
Components vs relationships — System includes both; the pattern doesn't prioritize.
tradeoffs: Gains: general framing for systemic analysis.
Gives up: almost nothing.
critique: Very thin mechanism.
Conflates many distinct kinds of systems.
No failure modes, no invariants.

System.family_discussion: Foundational container paired with Agent, Environment, and Boundary. Compare with Context — System is the container; Context is the ambient situation.

motivation.why_it_exists: Wide-aperture generation followed by progressive filtering. Taper names the multi-stage funnel with strictness-increase discipline. Without the pattern, generate-and-filter is ad-hoc.
motivation.removability: Removable — callers can implement funneling manually. The Monotonic Narrowing and Strictness Increase invariants are the discipline.

usage.intended: progressive ambiguity collapse — multi-stage filter with increasing strictness.
usage.future: any "filter down from wide to narrow" pipeline.
usage.broad_contexts: sema discovery pipeline, hiring pipelines, compiler passes, academic admission funnels, startup pitch review stages, journalistic fact-narrowing.
usage.every_context_needs: wide-aperture input, staged gates with increasing strictness, DepthGovernor-like functional role, progressive candidate reduction.
usage.varies: stage count, per-stage strictness curve, parallel-vs-sequential stages, cost-aware gate ordering.

tensions: Wide aperture vs terminal certainty — extreme range from permissive to zero-tolerance at the final stage.
Stage count vs gate strictness — more stages allow finer gradation; fewer are simpler.
Terminal Certainty invariant (tolerance = 0) rules out final-stage ambiguity.
tradeoffs: Gains: principled filtering discipline, progressive narrowing.
Gives up: flexibility. Taper's monotonic narrowing forbids mid-funnel widening for new candidates.
critique: No failure modes listed; taper has some (over-narrowing, missed candidates, stage misorder).
Terminal Certainty is strong; some tasks legitimately have graded final output.
Strictness Increase direction is fixed; variable stage ordering isn't supported.

Taper.family_discussion: Filtering-discipline primitive paired with Select (the atomic filter), LayeredCheck (similar layering), and Rank (ordering). Compare with LayeredCheck — Taper is filtering; LayeredCheck is checking.

motivation.why_it_exists: The root artifact of intent across every execution substrate — LLM calls, CI jobs, manual workflow steps, research queries, experiments, human tasks. Without a shared `Task` type, every caller shapes intent differently and every Solver has to parse a new format. Task makes intent a typed, transferable datum with holographic safety semantics.
motivation.removability: No. Task is the input type of every Solver — removing it breaks the Solver contract. It is also the recursion substrate (children are first-class Tasks), which is what makes the fractal solver tree possible. A replacement would need to preserve both the typed-intent and recursive-composition properties.

usage.intended: the atomic unit of intent; input to a Solver.
usage.future: any executable intent artifact — solver invocations, user requests, workflow steps, experiment plans, test cases, research queries, exploration prompts, CI jobs, even manual to-do items.
usage.broad_contexts: above.
usage.every_context_needs: `operation` (what), `inputs` (to what), `acceptance_criteria` (when done). Without acceptance_criteria the caller cannot close the transaction — definitional for Task-ness.
usage.varies: `budget` (optional — UnboundedTask doesn't carry one), holographic-inheritance strictness, parent linkage, retry semantics.
usage.extensions: `BoundedTask` (adds budget required), `ExplorationTask` (redefines acceptance), `ChildTask` (adds holographic inheritance enforcement).

tensions: Intent vs method: the mechanism says Task encapsulates *what* without prescribing *how*. In practice, Task often carries hints, partial plans, or execution preferences, and the line between 'constraint' (what) and 'method' (how) is fuzzy. Holographic Inheritance polices this at the constraint level but not at the intent level.

Hierarchical vs flat: Task is inherently recursive. Flat-queue use cases (independent work items) are technically handled by a shared root but the shape feels awkward for callers that never decompose.

Acceptance boundary: `acceptance_criteria` closes the transaction but for exploratory tasks ('research X, report what you find') acceptance may only be definable post-hoc. `ExplorationTask` exists for this — the parent spec permits it implicitly rather than explicitly.
tradeoffs: Generality (any intent) costs precision — Task cannot be fully typed on its content, it is a wrapper type.
Holographic Inheritance gives safety (children inherit parent constraints) but forces rigid top-down flow; relaxing constraints mid-execution requires re-rooting.
Recursion enables fractal composition but complicates lifecycle management — the spec is silent on when a parent Task is 'done' if children are still running.
critique: `acceptance_criteria` is load-bearing for transaction closure but appears only in descendant specs. It should be promoted to the parent's mechanism or invariants.
Constraint Escape is a real failure mode but detection is hard — an adversarial agent can claim satisfaction without a check. The pattern does not require constraint-verification at child creation.
Zombie Task is named as a failure mode but the mechanism has no cancellation semantics. In long-running systems this surfaces as stale work with no termination protocol.

Task.family_discussion: The input type of the entire Solver family. Parent to `BoundedTask` (budget required), `ExplorationTask` (redefined acceptance), `ChildTask` (enforces holographic inheritance). Pairs with `Solution` as the canonical (Task, Solution) transaction every Solver crosses. The recursion relationship with itself is what gives `UniversalSolverTree` its fractal topology.

motivation.why_it_exists: Tasks move through states — PENDING, ASSIGNED, RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED. TaskLifecycle names this state machine. Without the pattern, task status is ad-hoc and invariants like Forward-Only and Single Owner live in each scheduler.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for any task-tracking system. The specific five states are the paper's choice; alternatives exist. The invariants (Forward-Only, Single Owner, Failed-is-Terminal) are the discipline.

usage.intended: formal state machine governing Task progression — PENDING → ASSIGNED → RUNNING → COMPLETED/FAILED.
usage.future: any "life of a task" state machine.
usage.broad_contexts: workflow engines, ticket systems, issue trackers, solver-node lifecycle management, job schedulers, CI/CD pipelines.
usage.every_context_needs: five states (or a superset), typed-event transitions, invalid-transition rejection, heartbeat for RUNNING state.
usage.varies: state count (could have more — paused, cancelled, blocked), retry semantics, timeout handling, transition authorization.

tensions: Heartbeat timeout (named failure) — agent dies silently, task stuck RUNNING.
State desync (named failure) — network partition causes shared-ownership belief.
Forward-Only vs legitimate restart — failed tasks sometimes legitimately re-enter RUNNING.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured task state, explicit progression rules.
Gives up: flexibility. The five states are fixed; custom states require workarounds.
critique: Heartbeat timeout requires enforcement the pattern doesn't specify.
State desync is the distributed-systems hard problem; the pattern asserts Single Owner without providing the mechanism.
Forward-Only invariant forbids legitimate restart patterns.

TaskLifecycle.family_discussion: Task-lifecycle primitive paired with Task (the unit), Status (the state), and Heartbeat (liveness). Foundational for schedulers and orchestrators.

motivation.why_it_exists: Forecasting via single model is single-viewpoint. TemporalEnsembleForecasting is §6.5 of the paper: ensemble of models frozen at different training cutoffs; history itself is the diversity generator. Without the pattern, forecast diversity comes from prompting tricks that share training data.
motivation.removability: Removable — single-model forecasting suffices for many uses. The §6.5 protocol is specifically for forecasting where temporal diversity matters.

tensions: Temporal diversity vs data currency — older models have older worldviews, which is the point and also a limitation.
Five-angle pentagon vs other counts — five is the paper's choice.
History as diversity generator vs prompt-based diversity — the invariant prefers the former.
tradeoffs: Gains: genuinely independent forecasters (different training data), principled temporal diversity.
Gives up: currency. Older checkpoints don't know recent events.
critique: No failure modes listed.
Five is arbitrary.
Requires maintaining multiple model versions, which is expensive.

TemporalEnsembleForecasting.family_discussion: §6 paper-protocol sibling of CollaborativeWritingProtocol, EthicalReasoningProtocol, DiscoveryProtocol. Uses ConceptualDecomposition. Compare with PerspectiveEnsemble — TemporalEnsembleForecasting uses historical checkpoints; PerspectiveEnsemble uses personas.

motivation.why_it_exists: Conflicts between valid-but-incompatible signals need a data structure for resolution. Tension names this. Without it, conflicts are handled implicitly.
motivation.removability: Removable — conflicts can be resolved ad-hoc. Named Tension provides resolution-pattern substrate. The Persistence invariant ensures conflicts don't silently resolve.

usage.intended: reified conflict state between valid but mutually exclusive signals/constraints/values.
usage.broad_contexts: design tensions, ethical dilemmas, resource-allocation tensions, political tensions, creative tensions.
usage.every_context_needs: detected conflict, reification as data structure, input to resolution protocols (Dialectic, Yield).
usage.varies: conflict detection method, temporary-hold vs permanent, resolution pathway selection.

tensions: Mutually Exclusive (invariant) vs partial satisfaction — some tensions allow partial compromise.
Persistence vs noise — requiring explicit resolution may pile up minor tensions.
Bound elements — the pattern assumes binary or small-N tension; many-way tensions aren't first-class.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured conflict representation.
Gives up: simplicity.
critique: No failure modes listed.
Mutually Exclusive is strong; graded exclusivity is common.
Resolution mechanism unspecified.

Tension.family_discussion: Paired with TensionHold (the holding discipline), Conflict, and Compromise (the resolution). Compare with Incongruity — Tension is conflict between signals; Incongruity is expectation-reality mismatch.

motivation.why_it_exists: Conflicting high-confidence inputs shouldn't collapse prematurely. TensionHold names the cognitive suspension: bind conflicting inputs in a Tension object, don't select until resolved. Without the pattern, agents premature-converge.
motivation.removability: Removable — agents can pick arbitrarily. TensionHold is the explicit discipline that preserves both sides.

usage.intended: maintain contradictions without premature resolution.
usage.broad_contexts: ethical dilemmas, paradox management, scientific-debate navigation, multi-stakeholder negotiation, creative-tension preservation, dialectical reasoning.
usage.every_context_needs: Tension object binding contradictory inputs, downstream-decision block, release-on-reconciling-insight or timeout.
usage.varies: hold timeout, conflict detection threshold, reconciliation-seeking mechanism, fallback on timeout.

tensions: Premature Convergence (named failure) — arbitrarily discards one side.
Tension Blindness (named failure) — misses the conflict entirely.
Persistence vs decision need — some decisions require selection.
tradeoffs: Gains: holds conflicts open, prevents premature resolution.
Gives up: decisive selection.
critique: Premature Convergence is endemic.
Tension Blindness reflects that recognizing conflicts is hard.
No Selection invariant can delay necessary decisions.

TensionHold.family_discussion: Conflict-handling primitive paired with Tension (the object), Compromise (the resolution), and Dialectic (the opposing-view approach).

motivation.why_it_exists: Full-data classification costs too much for triage. ThinSlice names the early-bytes classification: first 512 bytes, high-confidence label, forward if uncertain. Without it, triage processes full content.
motivation.removability: Removable — triage can use full data. ThinSlice is specifically the cost-bounded early-classification variant.

usage.intended: high-confidence classification from tiny data sample — triage/routing without full processing.
usage.future: any "quick classification from minimal data" heuristic.
usage.broad_contexts: file-type detection from magic bytes, first-impression classification in hiring, doctor "eyeball diagnosis" from patient presentation, Gladwell's "Blink" concept.
usage.every_context_needs: tiny sample extraction, high-confidence classifier, route-based-on-class semantic.
usage.varies: sample size, classifier confidence threshold, fallback to deeper processing.

tensions: Sample representativeness vs tiny slices — 512 bytes must be representative; not always true.
Fail-Safe vs throughput — low-confidence forwarding adds latency.
Classification on tiny samples vs accuracy.
tradeoffs: Gains: triage speedup, cost bound.
Gives up: accuracy on non-representative slices.
critique: Representativeness is assumed not verified.
Slice size (512 bytes) is one specific choice.
No failure modes listed.

ThinSlice.family_discussion: Triage primitive paired with Classify (the decision), HeuristicSnap (similar fast path), and ThinSlice (early-routing). Compare with CognitiveEcho — ThinSlice is structural-data triage; CognitiveEcho is variance-based effort estimation.

motivation.why_it_exists: The atomic unit of reasoning — one inference, one connection. Think names it, distinct from multi-step Reason. Foundational.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every cognitive pattern uses Think. The Side-Effect Free and Context-Bound invariants distinguish real thinking from confabulation.

usage.intended: atomic cognitive step — one inference, one connection, one realization.
usage.broad_contexts: LLM token generation, inference steps, micro-realizations, single-axiom derivations, one-shot pattern-matching, intuition flashes, chain-of-thought atoms.
usage.every_context_needs: input context, output datum, side-effect-free semantic (no external state change).
usage.varies: cognitive mode (deliberative, intuitive), latency (ms to seconds), cost, confidence attached to output.

tensions: Hallucination (named failure) — conclusion doesn't follow from context.
Premature Closure (named failure) — first plausible insight without alternatives.
Side-Effect Free vs tool use — pure thinking is idealized.
tradeoffs: Gains: atomic reasoning unit.
Gives up: little.
critique: Hallucination is the dominant LLM failure; the invariant is what's violated.
Context-Bound is hard to verify post-hoc.
Side-Effect Free is aspirational.

Think.family_discussion: Foundational cognitive primitive paired with Reason (multi-step), ChainOfThought (serial composition), and Think specializations (GraphOfThought, SkeletonOfThought).

motivation.why_it_exists: Sema-specific collision threat-modeling: three classes of hash collision have different defenses. ThreeLevelCollision names this threat taxonomy. Without it, collision defense is uniform and inadequate.
motivation.removability: Non-removable for sema-style content-addressed systems. The pattern is the security analysis of the hashing substrate.

usage.intended: threat-modeling primitive distinguishing Stub / Hash / Homograph collisions, each with specific defense.
usage.broad_contexts: content-addressed system threat analysis, cryptographic protocol design, namespace-management security, visual-identity-system design (logos, fonts).
usage.every_context_needs: three-class taxonomy (stub, hash, homograph), per-class defense, distinct threat semantics.
usage.varies: defense specifics, per-class probability estimates, domain specifics.

tensions: Stub Confusion (named failure) — relying on 4-char stub.
Homograph Attack (named failure) — trusted-looking hash.
L3 Defense — identity is content, not handle.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured collision defense.
Gives up: simplicity. Three layers of defense.
critique: Stub Confusion is endemic — convenience stubs get security-treated.
Homograph attacks require vigilance beyond hashing.
L1/L2/L3 specifics may not generalize to all hashing schemes.

ThreeLevelCollision.family_discussion: Security primitive paired with Hash (the substrate), ConceptAnchor (what gets hashed), and CompatibilityCheck.

motivation.why_it_exists: Rate limiting as a named primitive — bounded events per time window. Essential for API contracts, queue drainage, and load protection. Different from Backoff (per-failure exponential) and Cooldown (per-action minimum gap): Throttle bounds aggregate rate across many events.
motivation.removability: No. Rate-limiting is a universal concern with enough structure (window, cap, action scope, burst allowance, drop policy) that a shared pattern avoids re-invention. Removing collapses throttling into ad-hoc Cooldown chains.

usage.intended: rate limiting — max N tasks per time window W.
usage.broad_contexts: API rate limits, UI button-debounce, traffic shaping, network QoS, process scheduling, rate-limited email sends.
usage.every_context_needs: N (count), W (window), excess-handling (reject/queue/delay).
usage.varies: sliding vs fixed window, per-scope limits (user/global/action-type), Backoff integration.

tensions: Sliding vs fixed window: both are valid; the pattern permits either. A caller who builds against a fixed-window Throttle sees different behavior at window boundaries than against a sliding-window one. The choice affects burstability, which affects downstream behavior.

Reject vs queue vs delay: three different drop-policies for excess. The pattern leaves the choice to the caller, which means Throttle's effective behavior depends on parameter choices not visible at the pattern level.
Per-action vs global: like Cooldown, scoping matters. A global Throttle serializes unrelated workloads; a per-action Throttle requires more state.
tradeoffs: Rate-bound buys system protection at the cost of legitimate burst denial (Legitimate Denial failure mode).
Window semantics (sliding vs fixed) buys different fairness properties — neither is universally better.
Separate limits per action type buys flexibility at the cost of complexity in the limit-configuration surface.
critique: The consolidated Rate Limit invariant now covers any-window semantics in one line; the previous redundant pair (per-second + any-window) is gone.
Legitimate Denial is the dominant real issue — attack/burst distinguishability requires classifiers the pattern offloads.
No priority story — all throttled requests are treated equally; priority-aware throttling needs a different pattern.

Throttle.family_discussion: Completes the rate-control family: `Backoff` (per-retry exponential delay), `Cooldown` (per-action minimum gap), `Throttle` (rate cap per window). The three compose: a retry loop can use Backoff for delay, Cooldown for action-gap, and Throttle for global rate.

motivation.why_it_exists: Central high-authority agents attract traffic; pricing by distance regulates. TieredAccess names this gravity-well economic pattern. Without it, central agents get overloaded.
motivation.removability: Removable — flat pricing or rate-limiting works differently. TieredAccess is specifically the gravity-well pattern.

usage.intended: cost-distance indexing — interaction cost increases approaching gravity-well center.
usage.future: any "core attention expensive, periphery cheap" access structure.
usage.broad_contexts: CEO-time pricing (expensive to reach), tiered-support models, stake-based governance access, reputation-based API pricing, VIP access systems.
usage.every_context_needs: gravity-well model with center vs periphery, cost-distance inverse proportionality, BearerToken integration.
usage.varies: cost function, tier count, reputation-vs-stake basis, escalation paths.

tensions: Metric Divergence (named failure) — agents disagree on distance.
Center economically inaccessible to low-resource agents.
Cost Monotonicity vs fairness.
tradeoffs: Gains: central-agent protection via distance-pricing.
Gives up: equal access.
critique: Metric divergence is structural.
Low-resource exclusion is a real concern.
No specified distance metric default; deduplicated failure-mode list (was: the same inaccessibility point stated twice in formal and informal wording).

TieredAccess.family_discussion: Access-pricing primitive paired with ContinuousResourceAuction, AttentionMarkets, and Permission.

motivation.why_it_exists: Events ordered by causality, not wall-clock. TimeWarpLog names this causal-cone ordering. Without it, out-of-order events produce impossible states.
motivation.removability: Removable in systems with reliable ordering. Essential for distributed causal consistency.

usage.intended: relativistic event ordering via causal cones (post-§3.1 coherence fix).
usage.future: any log that tolerates latency via causal rather than temporal ordering.
usage.broad_contexts: distributed systems, blockchain consensus, multi-agent history, eventual-consistency stores, latency-tolerant databases, cross-datacenter replication.
usage.every_context_needs: causal cone tracking per entry, acceptance rule based on non-contradiction with current cone, append-only semantics.
usage.varies: cone computation method, contradiction resolution policy, storage backend, replication model, trust model for event authors.

tensions: User confusion about 'when' things happened (named failure).
Causal consistency vs intuitive temporal ordering.
Indexability vs causal semantics.
tradeoffs: Gains: causal consistency.
Gives up: intuitive time ordering.
critique: User confusion is endemic — causal time is counterintuitive.
Indexability is hard to preserve under causal cones.
No specified contradiction-detection mechanism.

TimeWarpLog.family_discussion: Temporal primitive paired with Causation, CausalBarrier, and AuditTrail. Compare with AuditTrail — TimeWarpLog is causal; AuditTrail is wall-clock.

motivation.why_it_exists: Unbounded exploration runs forever. TimeboxThink names the bounded-exploration pattern: hard time limit, stop regardless. Without it, exploration lacks termination.
motivation.removability: Removable — callers can timeout manually. TimeboxThink is the named discipline.

usage.intended: bounded exploration — hard time limit, stop regardless of completion.
usage.broad_contexts: Pomodoro technique, meeting time-boxes, research-sprint timeboxing, test-taking timeboxes, decision-timeboxes.
usage.every_context_needs: hard time limit, stop-on-limit-hit, post-limit assessment, learning from what-was-accomplished.
usage.varies: duration (Duration per §3.17), extension rules, enforcement strictness.

tensions: Premature Cutoff (named failure) — stopping just before breakthrough.
Hard limit vs adaptive exploration.
Best-so-far vs committed answer.
tradeoffs: Gains: bounded exploration.
Gives up: completion. Sometimes one more minute finds the answer.
critique: Premature Cutoff is endemic — you never know what one more minute would have found.
Time limit is caller-chosen without guidance.
Assessment after cutoff is the important-but-deferred step.

TimeboxThink.family_discussion: Bounded-exploration primitive paired with OptimalStop, ComputeBudget, and Timeout. Compare with OptimalStop — TimeboxThink is wall-clock; OptimalStop is decision-theoretic.

motivation.why_this_layer: discover + invoke external tools — caller + tools
motivation.why_it_exists: Agents need to find available tools matching task needs. ToolDiscovery names this query-and-verify. Without the pattern, tool use is hardcoded.
motivation.removability: Removable in fixed-tool settings. Essential for dynamic-tool environments.

usage.intended: discover and invoke external tools via structured capability manifests.
usage.broad_contexts: MCP tool discovery, LangChain tool loading, LLM agent capability expansion, automated service composition, API marketplace discovery.
usage.every_context_needs: capability query, registry response with Cards, compatibility check, ToolInvoke.
usage.varies: registry topology, query language, caching, authentication.

tensions: Registry unavailable (named failure).
Schema drift (named failure) — manifest update not reflected.
Schema Verification vs speed.
tradeoffs: Gains: dynamic tool discovery.
Gives up: speed. Every discovery pays the verification.
critique: Schema drift is endemic.
Registry unavailability requires graceful degradation.
Fail-Closed is conservative; some tools should allow fallback.

ToolDiscovery.family_discussion: Discovery primitive paired with Discover, Card (tool advertisement), and ToolInvoke (the consumer).

motivation.why_it_exists: Calling an external tool requires structured argument validation, runtime delegation, and result integration. ToolInvoke names this. Without the pattern, tool calls leak context permissions and miss observation integration.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in tool-using agents. The Context Inheritance invariant (tool permissions ≤ task constraints) is the critical security property.

usage.intended: execute external tool and observe result — the atomic unit of agent-environment interaction.
usage.future: any structured "call a tool, get a result" operation.
usage.broad_contexts: LLM tool use, plugin invocation, API calls, OS syscalls, library function calls, external-service integration.
usage.every_context_needs: structured tool call (function name + arguments), InputGuard validation, external runtime delegation, observation integration into context.
usage.varies: sandboxing, timeout, retry semantics, side-effect classification (reversible/irreversible).
notes: §3.11 moves ToolInvoke from Data Structures to Primitives (it's a Verb). Broad-use confirms.

tensions: Hallucinated Tools (named failure) — actor invokes non-existent.
Argument Mismatch (named failure) — wrong parameter types.
Context Inheritance vs legitimate elevation — no elevation allowed.
tradeoffs: Gains: structured tool invocation, permission inheritance.
Gives up: flexibility. No elevation is strict.
critique: Hallucinated Tools is the LLM-era canonical failure.
Argument Mismatch — schemas catch some; not all.
Observation Integration requires the result format to match.

ToolInvoke.family_discussion: Tool-use primitive paired with ToolDiscovery (discovery), InputGuard (validation), and Act (the execution).

motivation.why_it_exists: Reasoning has shape — Linear, Tree, DAG, Cyclic. Topology names the structural primitive. Without it, reasoning shapes are implicit in each cognitive pattern.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every Reason-consuming pattern references Topology. The pattern is thin but foundational.

usage.intended: interface defining the node-edge structure of a reasoning process.
usage.future: any "what shape does this process take" abstraction.
usage.broad_contexts: reasoning topologies (Linear, Tree, DAG, Cyclic), workflow topologies, neural-network topologies, graph-algorithm topologies, organizational structures.
usage.every_context_needs: node definition, edge definition, shape classification.
usage.varies: node attributes, edge attributes, dynamism, visualization support.
notes: §3.18 moves Cyclic/Parallel/Linear to Infra/DS alongside Chain/Tree/DAG/Sequence/Skeleton. Topology itself is already Infra/DS R2T1.

tensions: Topology as classification vs topology as constraint — names a shape and enforces adherence.
Four shapes (Linear/Tree/DAG/Cyclic) may not cover all needs.
Topology choice vs problem shape — forcing a topology on an unnatural shape produces awkwardness.
tradeoffs: Gains: named reasoning shapes.
Gives up: specificity. Topology is high-level; specific shapes have richer structure.
critique: Very thin.
The specific shape list isn't exhaustive.
No failure modes, no invariants.

Topology.family_discussion: Structural primitive paired with DAG, Tree, Chain, Cyclic as specific shapes. Consumed by Reason for its topology parameter.

motivation.why_it_exists: Provenance and lineage require chronological log attached to an entity. Trace names this. Without it, history is implicit.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every audit, debugging, and lineage pattern uses Trace. The Causality and Immutability invariants are the audit properties.

usage.intended: record lineage/provenance — append chronological history log to a target.
usage.broad_contexts: distributed tracing, git history, event sourcing, data lineage, scientific provenance, supply-chain tracking, medical record history.
usage.every_context_needs: target entity, immutable append log, per-modification record.
usage.varies: log storage medium, record detail, retention policy, index-for-query, cross-entity linking.

tensions: Trace pollution (named failure) — too many traces, signal lost.
Decay mismatch (named failure) — wrong decay timing.
Namespace collision (named failure) — unrelated actors confuse each other.
tradeoffs: Gains: provenance and lineage.
Gives up: storage and signal-to-noise.
critique: Pollution is endemic in verbose-tracing systems.
Decay policy is under-specified.
Namespace is caller-managed.

Trace.family_discussion: Provenance primitive paired with AuditTrail (structured variant), History (the accumulated content), and Lineage (genealogical variant). Compare with AuditTrail — Trace is general-purpose; AuditTrail is verification-specific.

motivation.why_it_exists: Beliefs silently update unless tracked. TraceBelief names the chronological tracking. Without the pattern, hindsight bias dominates.
motivation.removability: Removable — BeliefTracking covers the space. TraceBelief is the specific chronological variant.

usage.intended: belief provenance — Macro for Trace(Belief), chronological history of belief.
usage.future: any "here's how my belief evolved" audit pattern.
usage.broad_contexts: epistemic version control, scientific hypothesis provenance, bug-hypothesis tracking, LLM answer-confidence history, audit-trail for decisions.
usage.every_context_needs: Belief instance, Trace primitive applied, silent-update prevention, citation of prior-belief-being-revised.
usage.varies: granularity of Belief nodes, compression of history, audit access.

tensions: Chronological vs causal ordering.
Citation requirement vs ease.
Storage growth.
tradeoffs: Gains: chronological belief history.
Gives up: storage.
critique: Similar to BeliefTracking; the distinction is subtle.
No failure modes listed.
Very thin.

TraceBelief.family_discussion: Belief-tracking primitive paired with BeliefTracking, BayesUpdate, and HindsightBlock.

motivation.why_this_layer: cognitive act of accepting consequence for gain
motivation.why_it_exists: Decisions have costs — the negative accepted for a positive. TradeOff names this. 'There are no solutions, only trade-offs.'
motivation.removability: Non-removable as a cognitive framing. The Opportunity Cost and Explicit Recognition invariants are the discipline.

usage.intended: specific negative consequence accepted for a positive one — "the cost of a decision."
usage.broad_contexts: Pareto tradeoffs, speed-vs-safety, cost-vs-quality, short-term-vs-long-term, simplicity-vs-features, privacy-vs-convenience.
usage.every_context_needs: positive gained, negative accepted, decision acknowledging both.
usage.varies: quantification, temporal horizon, stakeholder asymmetry.

tensions: Selection implies rejection.
Explicit Recognition vs optimistic framing.
Cost acknowledgment is hard psychologically.
tradeoffs: Gains: explicit cost recognition.
Gives up: optimism-only framing.
critique: No failure modes listed.
Very thin — philosophical framing more than mechanism.
Explicit Recognition is aspirational.

TradeOff.family_discussion: Decision-framing primitive paired with OpportunityCost, Decision, and Value.

motivation.why_it_exists: Atomic progression between states — Transition names it. Thin foundational primitive.
motivation.removability: Non-removable. Every StateTransition, phase change consumes Transition.

usage.intended: atomic progression from origin state to destination state.
usage.broad_contexts: FSM transitions, database transactions, biological phase transitions, legal regime changes, software state updates, workflow advancements.
usage.every_context_needs: origin state, destination state, adherence to transition rules.
usage.varies: atomicity guarantees, reversibility, guards, pre/post conditions.

tensions: Atomicity vs real-world partial transitions.
System transition rules vs arbitrary state change.
Source-to-destination vs multi-source merges.
tradeoffs: Gains: atomic state-change primitive.
Gives up: little.
critique: Very thin, almost a stub.
No invariants, no failure modes.

Transition.family_discussion: Foundational primitive paired with State, StateTransition, and Event.

motivation.why_it_exists: Converting representation while preserving meaning is a distinct operation from Interpret (which changes abstraction level). Translate names representation-preserving conversion.
motivation.removability: Non-removable in multi-representation systems. The Semantic Equivalence invariant is the core discipline.

usage.intended: convert form while preserving semantic meaning.
usage.broad_contexts: language translation, format conversion (JSON↔XML), code transpilation, protocol translation, data migration, unit conversion.
usage.every_context_needs: source schema, target schema, meaning preservation, distinction from Summarize (lossy) and Interpret (adds meaning).
usage.varies: fidelity requirements, ambiguity handling, bidirectional vs one-way, real-time vs batch.

tensions: Lossy Translation (named failure) — semantic nuance lost.
Hallucination (named failure) — adds information not in source.
Reversibility invariant vs asymmetric translations — some translations are inherently lossy.
tradeoffs: Gains: representation change with meaning preservation.
Gives up: perfect fidelity. Translation always loses something.
critique: Lossy Translation is endemic.
Hallucination is the LLM-era canonical failure.
Semantic Equivalence is aspirational.

Translate.family_discussion: Conversion primitive paired with Interpret (abstraction-level change), Compress (size-reduction), and RepresentationSwap (orthogonal-modality variant). Compare with Interpret — Translate preserves abstraction; Interpret changes it.

motivation.why_it_exists: Legacy systems don't speak modern protocols. TranslationProxy names the wrapper that bridges. Without the pattern, legacy integration is ad-hoc.
motivation.removability: Removable in homogeneous systems. Essential for legacy integration.

usage.intended: stateless wrapper that bridges modern agents to legacy systems via Translate.
usage.broad_contexts: API adapter patterns, legacy-system integration, gateway services, MCP bridges, protocol-version translators, cross-ecosystem bridges.
usage.every_context_needs: upstream (modern) interface, downstream (legacy) interface, translate in both directions, semantic fidelity verification.
usage.varies: statelessness (some proxies cache), error-mapping strategy, authentication bridging, rate-limit propagation.

tensions: Lossy translation (named failure).
Semantic preservation vs protocol mismatch.
Stateless vs contextual translation.
tradeoffs: Gains: legacy integration.
Gives up: fidelity.
critique: Lossy translation is endemic.
